en: The great Baroque parish of the village.
A work in progress by Giuliano Mauri, with columns formed by 108 trees on the left bank of the Adda.
The quadrangular fortress built by the Venetians between 1457 and 1470, now a large public park and summer arena.
The cry of the angels.

Of the castle that gives its name to the village remains the Norman walls. A plaque from the tenth century on the facade of the cathedral recalls that the castle was built under Constantine, patrician and strategist of Sicily; on the entrance arch the inscription "Castle faithful to His Majesty in the year 1578" .
In the National Park of the Casentino Forests, the waterfall of the river Rabbi produces a powerful sound in a rocky gorge.
A medieval town buried under the center.
It tells the history and life of the Walser community of Alagna, people of Alemannian origin who colonized the valleys of Monte Rosa from the 13th century.

Itinerary in nine stages among the mosaic works of the village: the Monument to the Fallen by Pietro Pellarin (1925), the birthplace of Gian Domenico Facchina (1826-1904), pioneer of the modern mosaic, the SOMSI headquarters, the Fountain of frogs (1936), the mosaic by Piergiorgio Patrizio for the centenary of Carnera (2006) and Palazzo Domini (1750), today city hall, with coat of arms in mosaic.
Valentine's Church, patron saint of lovers.
A cycle of frescoes in a castle in the woods.

Complex born between the fourth and fifth centuries and transformed by Longobards and Normans: since 1069, at the behest of Robert Guiscardo, it preserves the remains of the Altavilla; the great enlargement of the twelfth century, built also with stones of the Roman amphitheatre and never finished, is called the Unfinished. In the Foresteria the Museo del Territorio.
Set up in a trulli complex of 1792 in Masseria Montedoro, it illustrates the peasant life.
The theatre of 1668, architectural jewel of the historic center.
The frescoes of Gonin in a small elliptical church.

Castellaro, a fortified high-rise settlement of the ancient Ligurians, which dominates some mountain routes between the Val di Vara and the castle of Pignone; together with the Mount Dragonone it testifies the Ligurian settlements of the area.

On a rocky spur at the southern end of the village, with a single nave with a flat apse and wooden roof; a 1489 plaque on the façade recalls great works, other extensions at the end of the eighteenth century. Inside a baptismal font in marble of the fifteenth century and a sixteenth-century table of Sienese school with the Madonna and Child and Saint Augustine who holds the castle of Roccatederighi.

The village is walled on the balcony of the Marches at the foot of Mount San Vicino: the Baroque collegiate church of Sant'Urbano, the town hall of 1246, the Mestica theatre and, in the valley of the Esinante, the Romanesque abbey of Sant'Urbano; around the lake of Castreccioni and the beech woods of Pian dell'Elmo.
498 steps, not accessible for disabled motors
steep alleys and stairs go up to the Fortress, dominated by the castle; in the center the Confraternity of San Gerolamo, home of the Museum of Sacred Art.
Samnitic walls and a panorama of twenty-eight villages of Molise.
The medieval crenellated door of the village.
The medieval castle, heart and symbol of the city, with views of the city and the hills around; inside the Museum of the Middle Ages Gorizia.

The museum occupies the surviving tower of the castle at the top of the hill of Giano, called the Bell Tower: base staircase with slits, windows of 1467, bell tower rebuilt after the collapse of 1491 and elevated with Ghibelline blackbirds in 1847-55. The collections, begun in 1946, include a fresco of the Pordenone of 1514, organ doors of the workshop of Cima (1510-1517), a large canvas of Palma il Giovane, terracotta of Brustolon and Arturo Martini and, on the upper floors, archaeological finds from the Neolithic to the Roman age; on top a panoramic terrace.
We'll weed it in the meadows.

Environmental education center of the Sila National Park on the shores of Lake Cecita, built around the ancient State sawmill, where from the early twentieth century were produced also colophony and Trementina. It includes nature trails, wildlife observers, a naturalistic museum, the geological garden with the typical rocks of Sila and a botanical garden of 10,400 m2 at 1,156 m of altitude, with 115 native species and path accessible to blind and visually impaired (panels, audioguides, braille cards); next to a picnic area on the lake and an archaeological site under study with finds from Neolithic to Eneolithic.
Low and salty lagoon north of the city, with the Great Island, the island of Santa Maria and Mozia.
The Museum of Sacred Art of the Diocese, among the stages of the official itinerary of Agrigento Capital of Culture.
Common: Monday-Friday 9-13, Tuesday also 16-18, tel. 091 8247134; the building family is referred to as Gardner-Rose (Comune) or Rose-Forester (Metro City)

The parish church, at the highest point of the village, existed before 1118, when the bishop of Orvieto Guglielmo consecrated it; from a basilica to three naves it was transformed into a single nave, with the inverted entrance. The façade dates back to 1739; the coffered ceiling of the late nineteenth century is by Luigi Fontana, with four paintings and one fifth, the Mission of the Apostles of Father Nazarene Confaloni.
The sea in town.
Area of 4,500 m2 set in a park, bordered by walls, with the remains of the town and of the Etruscan-Sannitic necropolis.
The castle of the Countess of Castiglione.
The only altar of Giovanni Della Robbia in the Marches.
The neo-Gothic façade and the crucifix by Fra' Umile.
The Way of the Cross.
In the former Cimatoria Campolmi documents and fabrics from the 5th century to the present, costumes and ethnic textiles from all over the world.

In addition to the Sannitic enclosure of the Civita, with tombstones, the territory preserves the remains of a Roman villa in the locality of Casaglivune, Sannitic and Roman finds in the locality of Vicende, Casale and San Basilio and, in the locality of San Tommaso, a shrine in ruin between rocks and vegetation. On the tracturo remains traces of Sannitic fortifications and the farmhouse of the Duke of Pescolanciano. Always accessible.

Borgo dei Peloritani overlooking Capo Milazzo and the Aeolies, born around the castle of Federico II d'Aragona: the 17th century Mother Church with the sundial of 1854, the churches with works by Antonello Gagini, the Civic Museum in the oratory of the Filippines and the Parish Museum in Santa Maria degli Angeli.
The fortress overlooking the sea with a view of the gulf and Vesuvius.
Blue Flag Sea at the foot of the castle.
On the main square, built in the first half of the fourteenth century by the Marquises Spinola and expanded in 1693.
In a house of 1684, about 250 objects once used by the small community of Castelmagno, in the upper Grana Valley.
The wine told by its labels, inside monastic caves.
Country house transformed by Alfonso I d'Este into a ducal residence for Laura Eustochia Danti; it houses the museum of the Sepulcreto dei Fadieni, a Roman family.
no services on site; the Municipality recommends contacting the Info Point Mines of Bauxite for accesses and routes

Cittadina on the eastern shore of Trasimeno, born around the hospice of the Knights Gerosolimitani, today Castle of the Knights of Malta, theatre in 1502 of the conspiracy against Cesare Borgia; in the village the Lambardi Tower and the frescoes of Gerardo Dottori, on the lake the villages of Monte del Lago and San Feliciano with the Museum of Fishing, around a crown of castles and the nature reserve La Valle.
16th century church with coevo cloister.
From the Austrian period, after Casalmaggiore had the title of city in 1754, designed by architect Mones with the approval of Giuseppe Piermarini: it is a small version of the Scala of Milan.

Park of the villa of almost 24,000 sqm, with central lawn and wooded belt perimeter rich in trees of the first plant. It preserves the romantic "fabbriche" of the nineteenth century: the turret on the Colleonesca Roggia (1815-1816), the "gothic" ruins of 1849 designed by Angelo Cattò with Ghibelline turret, a cave with log stone nymph, the "alpine" chalet with glacier (now in ruins) and the statues of Venus and Ceres, the hermitage of Pan and the tuft for the passage of the emperor Francesco I of Austria. Flat paths, accessible.
The secular trees.
18th century villa with neo-Gothic battlements.

Founded by a group of volunteers to document the origins of the community, linked to the reclamation, it collects about 2,800 pieces of tools, equipment, machines and tools for earth processing, with a photographic archive; the route also shows how the peasants adapted and invented tools. Every year in July the harvest festival with agricultural machinery exposed at the entrance. Visits on request, with audio guides and guided tours.
Easy beach suitable for children, just a few steps from the center.

Founded in 1873 in the building of one of the oldest hospitals in Sicily, established in 1376 by the will of Gregorio Saglimpi and then entrusted to the Fatebenefratelli. It exhibits prehistoric finds, Greeks from Himera, Romans (a series of marble togates, mosaics, imperial portraits), Arabs and Normans with an inscription in kufic characters; in the artistic section the fifteenth-century polyptych of Gaspare da Pesaro, a Flemish Annunciation of the sixteenth century, a sketch of St. Jerome attributed to Bernini, works by Vincenzo La Barbera and Pietro Novelli, then the nineteenth-century termite, sculptor Filippo Sgarlata and a frescoed chapel of the fifteenth century.
Rebuilt after the demolition of 1959; the previous church, in 1686, had remained intact but isolated from the new settlement.

Centro dell'alto Frignano famous for the Corpus Domini infiorata along Via Tamburù, with the hamlet of Roccapelago, where the castle of Obizzo da Montegarullo preserves the mummies discovered in 2011, and Lake Santo, the largest lake of the Apennines.
The reading room in the Palazzo degli Studi, born from an idea by Maria Teresa of Austria.

Remembered as "Cappella S. Salvatoris in a notary act of 1235, has rectangular plan and sail bell tower; behind the simple façade frescoes from the XII to the XV century, including ex-vote with three Madonna del latte and a fourteenth-century fresco of Umbrian school re-emerged with a recent restoration.
The forest of Calatino.
The central square of the island, between alleys, shops and outdoor cafes; from here Via Vittorio Emanuele leads to Via Tragara.

According to tradition, the merchant Alberto Besozzi, escaped a storm on the lake, in 1195 had a small church built in thanksgiving to the saint; the complex then became a monastery, inhabited over the centuries by various religious communities until its closure in 1770. It has been the property of the Province of Varese, it has been restored since 1970 and in 1992 frescoes from the fourteenth century have been re-emerged. It comprises three buildings: the southern convent with a long arched corridor on granite columns and the frescoed capitular hall, the convent with a portico with acute arches, refectory and cells, and the church with fourteenth-century bell tower and mural paintings around the altar. You go down from the square with a panoramic staircase of 268 steps or with the elevator; from the lake, arriving by boat, the steps are about 80.

Castrum Sancti Angels was born around 1300, when the people of the valley floor of the Black gathered there to defend themselves from the raids, under the protection of the archangel Michael: triangular plant, square tower (turris capitis), walls with stretches of battlements and the gates Castello, Sant'Angelo and Nocrina, the latter with double arch.

Documented in 1237, rebuilt and consecrated in 1452, it preserves the triptych of the Trinity made of polychrome and golden wood by Georg Artzt (1517), among the most precious wooden works of Trentino, although some statues are copies.
The cells of the Risorgimento patriots.
The clock tower rises on the ancient Porta Sibilla and houses a sculpture of Giano bifronte, one of the oldest Roman gods.
Alpine architecture and popular painting in few steps.
A Franciscan stop.

Next to the museum, the Brossasca Park preserves ancient industrial buildings dedicated to the different phases of mineral processing; along the river Assa are visible roasting furnaces, washing basins, forges and mechanical sweaters used to produce iron without passing through the cast iron.
The Castle of the Battle of Murat.

Ruins of the fortress wanted by Pope Innocent III at the beginning of the thirteenth century on a rocky promontory, then passed to the Orsini; it was severely damaged at the end of the fifteenth century in the clash with Pope Alexander VI Borgia and the last tower collapsed during the Second World War. Free access 24 hours a day, with a path lit at night, climbing the staircase next to the church of the Assumption.

In the former convent of the Augustinians, active from the early seventeenth to the second half of the nineteenth century and then barracks of the Carabinieri on horseback, ten rooms tell with historical, anthropological and ethnographic cut the role of the horse, central in the culture of the country; it also houses the Donation Pesarin of architraves, capitals, columns and stone frames recovered from the historic center.

Dedicated to the sculptor, restorer and sindonologist Lorenzo Ferri (1902-1975), brought to Cave by the parish priest Mgr. Lorenzo Castellani. Inaugurated in December 2013 in the palace of the former Mattei Hospital, it exhibits on three floors the plasters from the 1920s to 1975: sketches of the statues of Trilussa and Giolitti, Ecce Homo, Christ the Redeemer, reliefs for the competition of the bronze doors of St. Peter, the Alata Victory, the bas-relief of almost three meters   ...The legend of Orpheus and the oil of Eva in Eden. Tactile path for people with visual disabilities; open Wednesday-Sunday 10:30-12:30 and 16:30-19:30.
Wide view of the valley of the Aterno and a Bourbon curiosity.

Built at the end of the 12th century, in the years immediately following the death of the saint to whom it is dedicated, as a chapel of the feudal family of the Andreans; inside frescoes from the 14th to the 16th century.
Purchased in 1918 by statesman Francesco Saverio Nitti, it was the summer residence of the family; it was reopened after a recent restoration.
The village suspended in the clouds.
A small, intact state museum.

Church built between 1441 and 1468 at the behest of the Sanseverino family; in the convent restored by the Municipality the BoCs Museum, opened in 2017 with the works of contemporary art of the artistic residences BoCs Art.

In part of the building donated to the Municipality by the Cuneo family in 1905: the hall of memories with furniture, objects and books of the family, including a rare Venetian edition of 1571 of the life of Christopher Columbus written by his son Fernando, late nineteenth century piers and fragments of the "patàffio" linked to the conspiracy of the Tower of 1672; then a shoemaker workshop rebuilt with original tools, an ancient village workshop and, outdoors, agricultural machinery and wine making. According to the Metropolitan City opens Tuesday and Thursday from 15 to 17 or by appointment. Tel. 0185 358791.
Picnic and walk in the Dauni Mountains woods.
Secular beech and high-rise meadows of the Apennines.
Accessibility to be verified on the MiC website
The rare Romanesque roundabout with four apses.
The otter forest in the Pollino.
A Renaissance castle-palace with graffita prison and moat in the rock.
The cells dug by the monks along the abbey road.

Just east of the city, born as a Benedictine grange in the 12th century and transformed into a castle in 1357 for the Varano; in May 1815 there was defeated Gioacchino Murat, battle re-evoked every May.
Ceramics and artifacts of Caracupa in a frescoed building.
The Amphitheatre of Traiano in the Sabina countryside.
An imperial nymph became a church.
The future velvet museum.
Portals, masks and alleys of the triangular village.
Beach of the seaside resort with a low and sandy backdrop, suitable for children.

Built in the early 1970s and opened in 1984 in the area of Turris Libisonis, it exhibits in two sections the statuary and architectural sculpture of the cult buildings and the objects of daily life from spas, tabernacles, houses and necropolis, mostly of the I-III century AD, including the Ara di Bubastis in marble of the first century AD and the marble mask of the Domus del Satiro; it preserves a heated environment of a spa and from the windows of the upper floor you can see the excavation. Open from Tuesday to Saturday 9-16 (ticket office until 3 pm), closed on Sunday and Monday.

The sixteenth-century parish church of San Marco, probably built on a previous chapel and expanded several times, preserves valuable paintings. The nearby Loggetta del Cinquecento, inspired by the Palazzo Comunale di Brescia, was the seat of the town hall and is now a parish museum. In the center also the Gothic House, medieval house-tower partly hidden from nearby buildings.

On the plateau of Poddi Arvu, in a forest near the Tirso springs about 13 km from the village: about seven hectares entirely granite with a hundred huts, a well temple with a corridor of over 40 meters leading to a basin surrounded by six steps amphitheatre, two megaron temples, a rectangular temple and a spiral labyrinth. Well and labyrinth date back to the 13th-IXth century BC; the name comes from a Roman settlement of the II-III century A.D. Admission fee.
Another fifteenth-century cycle in the village.
Church built in 1655, dedicated to the patron saint of the tunarotti; the festival is celebrated 50 days after Easter with sporting events, music and folk.

Opened to worship in 1536 and enlarged in 1671: single nave with barrel vault, dome on drum and transept, the side altar of 1695 in the ancient oratory of the Blessed Sacrament and a four-storey bell tower about 30 meters high.

Small alpine church at 1,860 meters above sea level in the larch tree above Mezzullo, linked in the sixteenth century to the Chiericato di Santa Giulia, which in 1567 raised controversy during the visit of Bishop Domenico Bollani.

An ancient Latin city on the Laurentina street, now known for the Museo Giacomo Manzù, which preserves hundreds of works donated by the sculptor, for the Gardens of the Landriana designed by Russell Page and for the archaeological areas of Casarinaccio and Colle della Noce; on the sea the beach of Tor San Lorenzo.
Easy, family-friendly.
Remains of the baths of an imperial domus, with traces of a porch and small heated rooms; one conserves part of a white and black tiles floor.
The place of the wolf of Gubbio.
The Norman Crusader and his grave.
One of the great Etruscan cities, with the National Archaeological Museum, the underground tunnels of the "Labyrinth of Porsenna" and the lake at 4 km.
A giant of rock carried by the glaciers, straight into the lake.
The straight called Spaccanapoli because it cuts the city in two, between Via dei Tribunali and the Decumani of the historic center.
The heart of the city's activities, where every day fish is discharged; it is the starting point of the Trabocchi Route.
The church in the heart of the ancient Altinum.
The village of the tanneries where the films taken from Verga were shot.
Park of the villa indicated by the Region among the places to see.

The information center of the Majella Park is next to the eighteenth-century Palazzo De Meis, which housed the stables of a noble family, and is the starting point for guided excursions to Monte Rotella and the Regional Nature Reserve Monte Genzana Alto Gizio, among beech woods, oaks, pine trees and firs with deer and bears. Open from July 16th to September 4th on Saturday, Sunday and August 10th to 13th and 16th-19th.

The ancient Tibur on the Aniene Falls, with two UNESCO sites: Villa Adriana, residence of Emperor Hadrian (1999), and Villa d'Este with its 16th century fountain garden (2001); on the acropolis the Roman temples and, in the gorge, the park of Villa Gregoriana.
The political and religious center of the city, with the parish church of Saints Gervasio and Protasio and the Palazzo Pretorio, seat of the Grey government since 1552 and today of the Municipality.
The geology of Cuneese in a former vault.
White pebbles and water birds.
Beech of about 200 hectares, Site of Community Interest, with imposing trees and a fairytale atmosphere; in the woods there is the Margari Stone, large dark boulder once hiding from the brigands.

Modern shrine with large dome and colonnade in Carniglia stone, built where from the seventeenth century there was the Chapel of the Well dedicated to the Madonna; the first church was wanted towards the end of 1685 by Lieutenant Marco Lezoli. The original shrine, with a single nave, preserves parts of the wooden choir and the niche of the statue of the Madonna della Belt. Since 2000 it has been a jubilee church. Open every day 9-19.
A Norman church in the woods.
The papyrus by the sea.

The church was built between the 8th and 9th centuries and was mentioned since 971, which belonged to Bonifacio di Toscana and then to Matilde di Canossa, who donated it in 1108 to the bishop of Modena; it rises on a cliff almost inaccessible above the valley of the river Fossa, next to an ancient fortress. The interior with three naves has capitals of the 11th century with vegetable braids, leaves and volutes, among the most beautiful in northern Italy, and a base of column with heads of lion, goat, bear and grifo; the restorations of 1913-1937 have recovered the Romanesque aspect. Open every day from 9 am to 6 pm.

Wanted by the Farnese in the sixteenth century as a former vote against the plague; inside votive paintings attributed to the brothers Lorenzo and Bartolomeo Torresani and a sixteenth-century Crucifixion of Folignate school with Jerusalem in the background. Since 1969 it has been a shrine of the fallen of all wars.
The step that at the beginning of summer becomes red with flowers.
The Dolomites Pesarine from the refuge.

Built in 1463 for the interest of the Agnesi family as a hospital to separate the plague patients from the healthy, it remained active for 130 years. The façade, one of the most imposing in the valley, has two cross-windows (one with the knot of Solomon, symbol of the mountain community), megalithic portals and a covered passage; today it is of the Municipality, restored, and often hosts exhibitions. It is reached from Paschero on a narrow municipal road that starts from the cemetery.
Sacred art, nativity scenes and the memory of the wool of Val Gandino.
The covered cast iron market opened in 1873 in the district beyond Santa Croce, the heart of the life of the district, with flower stalls, clothes and housewives all around.

Carlo Antonio Albino's work on the site of a Marian sacellus: isolated temple with Greek cross with longitudinal elongated arm and central crypt lowered in polychrome marbles; bell tower completed in 1772 and dome added in 1844 on a project by Giuseppe Squassi. In the altars paintings of Lombard artists of the seventeenth century.
The palace of the lords of the city.
Itinerary along the western bank between green, water, silence and neoclassical villas.
The Cistercian frescoes of the thirteenth century.
The family museum.

The museum centre of Intesa Sanpaolo between Piazza della Scala and Via Manzoni, with the 19th century Lombardy, the "Cantiere del '900" with Boccioni, de Chirico and Fontana and the garden of Alessandro Manzoni.
Alleys and squares with portals and windows marked by Latin inscriptions; the Chapel of San Sebastiano, conical plan, is from the fifteenth century.

Greco-Roman city founded by Dionigi di Syracuse in 397-396 BC: you can visit the Greek-Roman theatre overlooking the sea and the Aeolian Islands, seat of the Tindari Festival, part of the urban system with three decumans, the houses peristilius, the thermal baths, the Romanophylle called Basilica and the walls. At the entrance the Antiquarium with statues of togati and a head of Augustus. A cumulative ticket with the Roman Villa di Patti €11.20 (reduced €5), valid for three days.
The Blue Flag of the High Ionian Sea.
Panoramic cycle path from the old railway track, which runs from Levanto to Bonassola to Framura.
The 16th century Madonna of Rinaldo Bonanno.
It's called Death's for the seventeenth-century wooden skeleton it keeps.
Lemonets terraced between Minors and Maiori.

Built between the end of the fourteenth and the beginning of the fifteenth century, it is 21 meters high with a diameter of 14 and a large portal with the coat of arms of Carafa; inside flowerbeds with busts and inscriptions and a family chapel. From the top we read the development of the village, still partly surrounded by walls.
The art gallery that testifies to the tradition of the painters of Vezzini.

The village of Val Gerola where, in addition to the fifteenth-century picta room of Homo selvadego, a house near the church has a refined votive fresco with the Pietà di Andrea De Passeris (1508) and the parish house preserves the Quadreria di San Lorenzo. From here pass the ancient road of the valley, in the stretch between Campione and Rasura, with panoramic views, chestnut woods and higher conifers.
Crystal clear sea in front of the calanchi.
Romanesque frescoes.
A facade to read like a book.
A thousand years of Nuragic history on a panoramic hill.
Sunny terrace of Valpelline on a morainic basin at 1176 meters, the ancient Roman Dovia, with views of Mont Emilius.

Small village of medieval origin on the slope next to the center, part of a defensive system that included Mandello, with a surviving house tower and view of the lake; the parish church of Sant'Antonio Abate, renovated until the seventeenth century, preserves a canvas of the mid seventeenth century with the territory of the parish. The patron saint's feast, the Sunday closest to 17 January, provides for the blessing of animals.
A Norman tower in the southern quarters.
The craft of the shopkeeper in his original shop.
The castle that dominates the village and houses the cultural centers of the village.
open from 1 April to 1 November, closed in winter; visit to book at least 10 days before; pedestrian area without parking
€5 (MiC card); reduced rates to check

In the stables of the castle: the agriculture museum tells about the agricultural innovations from 10,000 BC, with a section dedicated to the Lower Padana; the bread museum, in five rooms, the cycle from cereal to bread, the forms of Italian bread and the world and historical tools. They are visited with the castle, with cumulative ticket and guide.
Let's Marche and Tourism Marche indicate the temporarily closed hydrotherapy station

In the woods of Curadureddu sul Limbara, between holm oaks and cork trees about 7 km from Tempio along the SS 392: works installed outdoors and the CEDAP Space, a former troticulture transformed by the architect Antonello Menicucci in two exhibition rooms, near the pools of the Rio Pisciaroni.
A small baroque mountain in the plain.
A spectacular gorge just a stone's throw from the village.

Small island of the Pontine archipelago, exile place of the daughter of Augustus and the anti-fascist confino where the Manifesto of Ventotene was born: Roman port dug into the tuff, remains of Villa Giulia at Punta Eolo and backdrops of the Marine Protected Area, with in front of Santo Stefano and its Bourbon prison.
The monumental entrance to the city from below.
The Romanesque heart of the village.
The Norman mother church.
Reserve of about 380 hectares established in 1995 and managed by the WWF: calanchi with roverella, licorice and capers, raptors and barbarians, paths to walk alone or with a guide.
Sea and bike on the Palm Riviera.
Liberty Bolognese.
€6 according to the Castelli del Ducato circuit; €5 according to the Ministry of Culture
A nuragic village almost intact.

Trapanese seaside town, among the major fishing ports of the Mediterranean, with the North African Casbah, the Norman Cathedral of the Most Holy Savior, the Norman Arch of Piazza Mokarta and the Museum of Satyr, which exhibits the Greek bronze fished in 1998 in the Sicily Canal.
The ancient history of the whole Sorrento peninsula in one museum.
The highest tower in the city, 50 meters, with 207 wooden steps and the historic clock mechanism, still working, that you can see going up.
A Madonna by Michael Pacher.
The symbol of the city suspended on the valley.
From the castle to the caves, the history of the peninsula on foot.

The Gothic church of the Apostles was built in 1467-1470 by master Jörg, with simple portal, pyramid bell tower and five octave choir; the small round church of the Hospital, founded after 1200 by bishop Konrad von Rodank for the hospice of the travelers, is the only part of the complex survived the floods.
Included in the Monastery ticket (€8, reduced €4, FAI members free)

Chapel of Orthodox rite of medieval times (the FAI card the date to the XI-XII century), with the interior entirely frescoed by a succession of panels depicting icons of saints. Style and iconography are compared to the great Norman music cycles of Monreale, Palermo and Cefalù, and the frescoes are probably the work of Byzantine masters: together with the other rock churches in the area are an important example of Byzantine painting in Western Europe.

Frazione from the well-preserved medieval center, home of the humanist Antonio Bonfini, with the Porta del Borgo which bears an epigraph dedicated to King Manfredi and the Romanesque church of Santa Maria in Viminatu, frescoed between the fourteenth and sixteenth centuries.
The noble walk of Forlì.
One of the oldest facades in Cuneo.
Vicchio is also the village of Blessed Angelico.

Built between the 13th and 14th centuries on a church of the 9th century, with large portal, rose window and bell tower; in the choir the largest cycle of frescoes in the region, masterpiece of Andrea de Lithium, and inside Renaissance chapels and a sixteenth century baptistery.

The shopping street from Piazza Dante to Porta Nuova on the ancient Aurelia, with the church of San Pietro (documented in 1118), the Art Nouveau palaces Pallini and Tognetti and the neoclassical Palazzo Ariosti.

Romanesque church on Via Roma with caves, a bas-relief with the Hunt of Adone under the main altar, paintings of the eighteenth century and a crypt with the tomb of the patron Saint Vivenzio, celebrated on 11 December.
The civic heart of the country, with a robbian work survived flooding and war.
The Renaissance frescoes by Callisto Piazza.
The Flemish statues of San Rocco.
A church returned to the cultural life of the country.
The castle on the sea.
Romanesque frescoes above the city.

The town of stone of Annunzio, about 600 meters on the Maiella with views from the coast to the valleys: the collegiate church of Santa Maria Maggiore, the medieval and baroque churches and the goldsmith tradition of Nicola da Guardiagrele.

Church mentioned in 1070 as the chapel of San Prospero of the goods of Bonifacio di Canossa, from the end of the fourteenth century dedicated to Santa Maria; it was probably rebuilt in 1697, date carved on the façade in sandstone blocks. An interior with a single nave with a barrel vault; next to the canonical with arched loggia on columns. In the hamlet of Grassano, on the hills towards Canossa, known for its stone houses.
The mountain pond.

The largest green area of Porto Viro, north of the center, on fossil dunes: the pine trees were planted from the early twentieth century, especially in the 1940s and 1950s, and today return native species like holm oak and roverella. It is the site of Community importance of the Natura 2000 network.
Two alpine dams under the Andolla Pizzo.

Small chapel in the green, restored by the Municipality in 2006, on the site of a more ancient church mentioned in 1531; interior entirely frescoed with the Madonna in the center and Sant'Antonio, sign of the influence of the monastery of Bobbio. In the area traces of a Roman rustic villa (1st century BC-VI century AD), of a late ancient necropolis with cappuccino tombs and two medieval burials.

The historic centre, always open to visitors, has one of the five gates of the walls in the eastern part, the Monte di Pietà (recreational circle since 1868) and the Hospital of Santa Maria della Pietà; the castle, destroyed by the earthquake of 1786, remains the name of the promenade, where in 1873 the Teatro Alfieri was born. From the central square you can see the Aeolian Islands, Nebrodi and Etna.

San Bonifacio has its most important monument in the Romanesque abbey of San Pietro a Villanova, with frescoes from the Giotto school and a crypt with 24 columns, which also houses the Geopaleontological Civic Museum; besides the Alpone stands the parish church of Sant'Abbondio alla Motta, of the twelfth century, and in the hamlet Prova the seventeenth-century Villa Carlotti.

Borgo dell'alta Val di Susa was born in the 11th century along the Strada di Francia: the parish church of St. John the Baptist and the Natural Park of the Gran Bosco with the ecomuseum Colombano Romean.
The Byzantine Cagliari.
Church of the Serbian Orthodox community overlooking the Grand Canal.
In a room of the municipal library there is a 16th century fresco of the Madonna di Loreto.
Damini and Dalla Oglio's shovels.

The Church of Purgatory (XVII century) rises on a primitive church of about 1000 recently discovered; Saint Lucia is of the seventeenth century; San Cataldo was completed in 1783 in Baroque style with dynamic façade; San Quirico was built between the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries.
One of the most beautiful canyons in Italy, to walk.
The largest artificial lake in the Marche region, for fishing, trekking and water sports.

It is located in the old town hall of the village and preserves evidence of human settlements from the lower Paleolithic. There is also the baptismal font of 1452 coming from the Pieve di San Pietro di Offiano.
A walk through the boats on the Tyrrhenian Sea.
Numerous fountains dot the center of the village and the slopes of Mount Summano.

Open-air museum through the streets of the historic centre, born from the project "Old Calabria" inspired by the book of Norman Douglas and promoted by the Fondazione Napoli 99: ten murals tell about the work, customs, traditions and economy of the people of Castelsilano, painted by the artist Francesco Candido, born in the village and lived for a long time in Paris.
It has old tools and agricultural machinery.

The 15th century civic tower, the main monument of the town, the rest of the Rangoni Rocca: testifies to the X century castle strengthened by the Rangons in the fourteenth century; recently there are traces of walls of the thirteenth century. The castle, rebuilt after the Second World War, houses the Town Hall.
The watchtower in front of Dino Island.

Sacred area linked to the cult of the waters on the granite ridge of Mount Senes, about 600 meters overlooking Gennargentu and Supramonte. The temple, in granite blocks well squared and dated to the Bronze final-first Iron (XII-IX century BC), has a rectangular atrium with seat and a circular cell with fireplace, inside a trapezoid temenos where the offerings were laid. The source of Su Notante (XII-X century B.C.) is built in squared basalt, non-local stone brought to the place, and the water gushes still. You can reach from Irgoli following for about 12 km the road to Mount Senes.
The paintings donated by Count Zurlo.

Borgo gathered around the Savelli Torlonia Castle, among olive trees and cherry trees at the foot of Monte Gennaro in the Parco dei Monti Lucretili, about 40 km from Rome; in the surroundings the abbey of San Giovanni in Argentella, the abandoned village of Stazzano Vecchio, the castrum of Castiglione and the Baths of Cretone.

In the countryside between Bastille and Modena, where already in the 11th century there was a church linked to the abbey of Nonantola. In 1689 the roof collapsed under the snow but a fresco of the 15th century of the Madonna and Child was saved, and the pilgrimages financed the reconstruction: a Baroque church with a Greek cross with dome designed by Antonio Loraghi, with a canvas by Giovan Battista Cipriani, a Martyrdom of Saint Ignatius of Antioch by Sigismondo Caula, a Pietà by Antonio Verni da Guercino and dozens of votive tablets.
The monastery of music.
The cathedral of the baptism of Tasso and Tarsia Sorrento.
the source indicates the currently maintained quarry
In the former convent of Sant'Agostino, the furnishings of the Villanovian necropolis (IX-VII century BC), with very rare woods and fabrics.

Church excavated in the rocky bank, part of a monastic settlement of the twelfth century; today it is a single irregular environment with lateral entrance, but the traces indicate an ancient iconostasis. An inscription in Greek given the frescoes in 1196: it is one of the few examples of rock church decorated with Christological scenes (Annunciation, Nativity, Escape into Egypt, Presentation at the Temple, Entrance to Jerusalem), with stories of the saint, episodes of the Gospels apocryphal and saints of the East and West. Guided visits, tel. 0831 955236.
A 16th century farmhouse in the fields of the South Agricultural Park.
The Gran Paradiso Valley.
After the earthquake of 2012 many buildings in the center remained unworkable: check if the church is open

Built in 1553, it is the second bastion for the importance of the Venetian pentagonal fortress and preserves intact its military structures; the southern section played a role in the sieges of Napoleonic and Risorgimento wars. From the walk above Porta Verona you can see the entire eastern front of the fortress, the railway bridge rebuilt after the bombings of 1944, the back of the Ponte dei Voltoni and in the distance the Bastione Cantarane; you can climb it from a stone staircase in the Piazza della Caserma d'Artilleria.
The countryside is surrounded by walls.

Parish church built between 1757 and 1782 on the design of the Lombard Whites, with a single nave with four side chapels and the main altar of the Venetian Temanza; the bell tower of about 60 meters is 1886-1888. It preserves the altarpiece of Francesco Guardi with the Holy Trinity that appears to Saints Peter and Paul (1778 about), frescoes by Valentino Rovisi, pupil of Tiepolo, and the Evangelists by G. Battista Chiocchetti; the Pugina organ was inaugurated in 1931.
Built in 1491 by Francesco di Giorgio Martini on the hill above the junction for Pesaro, it houses the tombs of Duke Federico and his son Guidobaldo.
The heart of the village born from the union of two farmhouses.

Built between 1884 and 1895 by the Franciscan Tertiaries on land donated by the priest Raffaele Ierna; on the high altar the wooden statue of St. Francis of the Palermo Rosario Bagnasco. Parish since 1951.
To see a mosaic in the labs.

Built in 1612-1628 by Cardinal Pietro Aldobrandini for the Franciscans of the Reformation and restored by Leo XIII. It preserves seventeenth-century sculptures by Fra' Stefano da Piazza Armerina, the  "Stimmate di San Francesco" attributed to Simon Vouet and the "Immaculate" of Fr. Diego da Tavello; in the cloister lunettes frescoed by Serbuccio da Tivoli with the life of San Francesco (stems of 1685).
One of the most beautiful seabeds in the Mediterranean.
Dedicated to the patrons, of Renaissance form on Romanesque origins, with the side portal late Dogotic, the coffered ceiling of 1699 and the lower church of the second fifteenth century.
The church of Valperga at the top of the village.

13th century, with a late-Doromatic façade and a large rose window; three frescoed naves, altars with works by Moretto and Romanino, the cloister of the Madonna and the large cloister with columns in red marble of Verona; mechanical nativity scene in the Christmas period.
The civic tower with the exhibition on peasant life.
A late baroque villa of delight along the bike path of the Brianza parks.
The central market, renewed: day market, in the evening meeting place.
The carved altars.
Beach known for the picturesque castle perched on a spur of rock on the sea.
Small church and museum that preserve the Seven works of Mercy of Caravaggio.
There's a nice belvedere from the Rescue Square.

Wanted in the 10th century by the Duke of Amalfi to guard the northern borders, part of the network of fortifications that controlled the two slopes of the Lattari; documents of 1030 and 1033 describe it as a fortified village. The trapezoidal castle preserves four towers, the highest was the mast; within the walls the cathedral, bishop's seat since 987, with 12th century bell tower decorated with tarsies, and the Grano Tower. The museum exhibits ceramics, bronzes and animal remains from excavations started in 2007, from the 10th to the 16th century. Free with the ticket of Pompeii of the same day.

Born in 1966 for the finds of Ugento and the territory and inaugurated in 1968 as Civic Museum of Archaeology and Paleontology, it was re-equipped in 2009 as New Archaeological Museum, with materials also from other sites of Salento, in the halls of the former convent of Friars Minor Observing next to the church of Sant'Antonio. Open from Tuesday to Saturday 9.30-12.30 and 18-21, Sunday 18-21.

Small village of medieval origin on the slopes of the Alburni Mountains, crossed by the Sele: in the territory there are the WWF Oasis of Persano, famous for its otter, and in the hamlet of Persano the ancient Bourbon hunting pavilion of the Reggia, where the breed of horses of Persano was bred.
The Gothic façade of the parish.
Two painters of Antrodocus.
Liberty in Irpinia.

From the Prati d'Angro, with the refuge of the same name, start several paths of the Park: towards the Sorgente Puzza (2 hours), the Valico Aceretta (1 hour and 30) and the Vallone Acquaro (45 minutes, easy); from the Madonna della Lanna you go up to the refuge in 1 hour and 15. Other routes lead to the Coppo dell'Orso Refuge, also directly from the village (4 hours).
Prepare for excursions in the park.
The symbolic theatre of the Festival of the Two Worlds, founded in 1958 by Gian Carlo Menotti.
Everyday life on the slopes of the volcano.
On the promontory overlooking Trasimeno, the village of Della Corgna: the Doge's Palace connected by a covered walk to the Fortress of Leone, between medieval walls with three doors.

In the former late 19th century brick school on Piazza Gramsci, inaugurated in 1994, it brings together the Giulio Superti Furga Toy Collection (hundreds of dolls and toys, largely of local production: Furga, founded by Luigi Furga Gornini around 1880, was the first factory of dolls in Italy), the Oglio-Church Ecomuseum with fossils, archaeological finds, peasant tools, dioramas and the Visitor Centre of the Oglio Sud Park, the donation Bellani and the Mortara Collection of Lombard painting between Scapigliatura and Divisionismo (Tranquillo Cremona, Previati, Longoni, Tosi). Open Saturday afternoon, Sunday and holidays.

It is 2.521 metres high in the Prealpi Orobie, called Regina, for the limestone walls compared to the Dolomites; the hamlet of Bratto-Dorga is the starting point for the climb. The territory, in the Parco delle Orobie Bergamasche, offers hiking, mountain biking, climbing and in winter skiing, cross-country skiing and snowshoes.
The Borgia fortress on the sea.

In the House Peter Rosegger in Redagno di Sopra, at the other end of the GEOPARC: popularizing panels and a stratigraphic column that reproduces the sequence of rocks of the gorge, from the porphyry quartzifer of Bolzano to the sandstone of Val Gardena, to the layers in Bellerophon and Werfen up to the Formation of the Contrin. On Sundays in season guided tours in the gorge start from here.

Born in 1987 on the initiative of citizens of Montepagano with publicist Luigi Braccili, he is set up in a peasant house: agricultural tools, furnishings of the late nineteenth century, cooking branches, wedding accessories and vintage clothes, a herbarium with dialect names of plants, photographs from 1850 to 1950, coins and posters of the Second World War. An audioguide is available.

Valley at the foot of the Ortles-Cevedale, in the Trentino area of the Stelvio National Park: the thermal baths of Peio Fonti, the fauna area of deer, the museum of the Great War of Peio Country with the finds of Punta Linke, the Ecomuseo with Casa Grazioli and the cable car Pejo 3000.

Former Franciscan monastery on a rocky step about 600 meters, wanted by the Marquis Piccolomini as a kind church. The Baroque church has three aisles and six chapels, a bronze door with the miracles of the saint, a wooden statue of St. Anthony in Spanish style with inlaid flowers on gold background and an organ of the late eighteenth century by Domenico Antonio Rossi, organist of the Royal Chapel of Naples. Left by the Franciscans with the suppression of Murat in 1811, it passed to the Redemptorists of the Consolation until the suppression of 1886.

Mines at 1800 meters, exploited by the Romans for copper and millstones, today open-air museum with guided tours (momentally closed); in the town hall the Viviminiera center tells them with plastic, reconstruction and video.
The Aragonese fortress of the city.

In the seventeenth-century complex of Palazzo Toffoli, exhibits the excavations carried out in the municipal territory in the last twenty years of the twentieth century: testimonies from the recent bronze age (XIV century BC) to the Middle Ages, including the supplies of the necropolis of Dominu. Open from May to September Saturday and Sunday 15-18, from October to April the first Sunday of the month 15-18.
A long coastline with white sandy coves: Cala Marina, Cala Bernardini, Cala d'Ostia and Cala Verde.
The heart of the defensive system of the middle valley of Oglio.
Worked stone and noble palaces of Alta Irpinia.
The nuragic landscape of Abbasanta.

An ancient plebanic seat outside the historic centre, it was rebuilt in 1580-81 by Vespasiano Gonzaga demolishing much of the previous building; in the sixteenth century a convent was flanked, today disappeared, and in the nineteenth century it became a cemetery church. Inside there are altars with marble tarsies and a beautiful seventeenth-century wooden cantoria from the parish. Free access to the ground floor.

Built between 1913 and 1923 on the site of the Old Establishment and still in operation: plant at E, architecture of Ugo Giusti and decorations by Galileo Chini that combine oriental motifs and liberty. Named to the doctor Lorenzo Berzieri, who since 1839-40 studied the properties of the waters; they offer thermal baths, massages and Kneipp routes. In front is the Scotti well in wrought iron and glass.
The view over the Oltrepò from the castle towers.

The courtyard of the abbey, similar to a piazza d'armi, is closed by the entrance tower with the coat of arms of the Grimani, the only surviving of the seven towers of the walls, from the bell tower of the XI-XII century perhaps born as a sighting tower, from the palace of the Chancellery and from the palace of the Abbot, which with the frescoed coat of arms of the five commendatory abbots houses today the Town Hall. Next to the entrance of the church the loggia with chivalrous frescoes of the 13th-XIV century.
A Roman remnant on the valley floor.
On the battle sites of 217 B.C.
A village still closed in its walls.
The medieval ruins with frescoes from the thirteenth century.
The baptistery of the cathedral of Rome.
A signed canvas by Luigi Crespi.

Housed in the ancient Cascinale dei Nobili, a large courtyard with rural houses that opens under an arched porch and is bordered by five churches of decreasing size, called churches "matrioska" , some used as exhibition halls. A multimedia path (consultable with tablets or smartphones) tells about life in rice fields, the work of peasants and worldly people, customs and songs; the second section is a gallery of wagons, tools and machines for processing rice. Open only by reservation; accessible to disabled people.
The oldest little church among the olive trees.
Elegant theatre with stage, audience and frescoed ceilings; it hosts mainly prose, from comedy to cabaret. Discount with the Touring card on the performances of the Apulian Public Theatre.
The Novecento italiano in a historic building.
The longest promenade of the Ponente Ligure, to be walked or biked to Varazze, accompanies about 3 km of equipped beach.
Walk up to the castle among the stones.

Started at the end of the thirteenth century by Sozzo Rustichini, with façade in white and pink marble: inside the source and altar of the Madonna by Antonio Ghini, a painting by Matteo di Giovanni and a crucifix attributed to the Vecchietta.

Established by the Lombardy Region in 1983 at the request of the Municipality, which manages it, protects 41,68 km2 of the two Brandet and Campovecchio twin valleys, separated by a long dorsal and joined by the village of Sant'Antonio. It rises from willow and white alder woods to the skins with the rare white fir and larch, then rhododendrons and blueberries, lakes, wetlands and peat bogs; there live chamois, marmots, cedar roosters, coturnals and royal eagles. Hiking trails on foot, on horseback or by mountain bike, picnic areas and two refuges: Alpini di Campovecchio (1310 m) and Val Brandet (1360 m).
Artworks, murals and sculptures of the competition banned every year since 1993.
Still functioning water mills; in summer, on Tuesday, the activity "Dal Chicco al Mulino" is 15-18 with a walk.
Manager Archeonova, 378 30270077; the MiC card indicates mandatory booking.
Ancient frescoes in the surviving apse of the old church.
The religious and cultural heart of Val Taro.
A monastery of the fifteenth century.
Housed in the Palace of Gaia da Camino, it exhibits historical bicycles and shirts worn by famous Italian and foreign champions.
Church that preserves works by Antonio Zanchi.
The tower of the castle and the frescoes of the fourteenth century.
A country to read between portals and panels.

A coastal lake with fresh and brackish waters, a stopover of many migratory birds, with paths and banks to walk, by mountain bike or on horseback; it is in the system of regional parks of the Ausoni and Aurunci Mountains.

Country at the foot of the Alpe di Siusi, the largest plateau in Europe, with the Sciliar massif and the Santner peak in the background: in Kraus square the 82-metre bell tower, the parish church of Saints Peter and Paul and the town hall of 1607, around houses with facades painted by Eduard Burgauner and, on the Colle, the Via Crucis among the porphyry rocks.
Contemporary sacred architecture signed by Botta.

In the village Enel Green Power, the museum renovated on the history of geothermal energy, from the boric acid of 1777 to the first bulbs of 1904, with 3D room and a visit to the demonstration shower.
Alleys and medieval walls descending to the Oglio.
The twisted tower of Venice.

The fortress about 270 meters high that dominates the village: in half an hour of ascent you reach the blackbirds, the remains of the Temple of Diana linked to the cult of water and a castle of the twelfth century.
Complete the visit to the Duomo.

Reserve of 206,88 hectares established in 1984 between Cattolica Eraclea and Ribera, at the mouth of the Platani dominated by the cliff of Capo Bianco, with sandy beaches, dunal cordons, promontories and clay gullies; protects the birds, for many migrators from Africa first stop.
The balcony on the Sibillini.
The Cistercian jewel of the Marches.
The monument to the water workers.
The lion marches by Pomponius Amaltheus.
The chapel on the high ground.

In the hamlet remains the ancient fortified fortress; the church of Saint Lucia, documented since 1381 and with Romanesque portal, was damaged by the earthquake of 1943 and reduced in the sixties, and preserves copies of four tables by Pietro Alemanno (the originals are at the Diocesan Museum of Ascoli Piceno).

Opened in 1990 in the former convent of the Augustinians next to the parish of Santa Maria Assunta. The ethnographic section collects tools of arts and crafts, agricultural machinery, chariots and calexs, an ancient still working mill and rebuilt peasant environments (stalla, cucina, camera); the section of sacred art exhibits objects of worship, banners and pictures, while the cloister houses photographic documentation on the churches of the valley. Tel. 010 95033.

Curated by the Association E. Kyé', exhibits objects and memories of the mountain life of the past and recalls the easternmost Provençal enclave of Europe present in the valley. Open by reservation (tel. +39 0174 349240, +39 338 3843572).

Carnia Municipality in Val Degano, \'balcony of the valley \', with the Pieve di Santa Maria di Gorto, one of the oldest in Carnia, and the slope of Monte Zoncolan, legendary ascent of the Giro d'Italia.
The life of caves and mountain crafts.

One of the oldest artifacts of Villafranca, today reduced to remains: you can see the tower, the arch of the ancient drawbridge and frescoes of the 13th century with the Crucifix between the Saints Peter and Paul.
The most photographed glimpse of the Vena channel.
A destination for a more demanding hiking route.
For an ancient rest village with a 16th century painting.
Area fenced at sea near the port, built with the Cetacea Foundation of Riccione (NetCet project), where the rescued and cured sea turtles remain until they are ready to be released.
A 360° view of the Riviera.

Cittadina del Vulture-Melfese on the road between Lagopesole and Melfi: the Angevin Tower, the remaining remains of the castle destroyed by the earthquake of 1694, the cathedral of Santa Maria in Nives and the monastic complexes of Santa Maria degli Angeli and Santo Spirito.
An easy path in the heart of the Musi.
A 15th-century parishioner.
Taste the Collio in its capital.
In the countryside around the village, imposing karst cavities embellished with crystal-clear formations and a forest of stalactites and alabaster stalagmites.
On the ancient Roman forum, the Romanesque church of Pisa-Lucchese with its marble façade, crowned by the archangel in bronze; inside statues by Andrea della Robbia and paintings by Filippino Lippi.
Accessible courtyard, inside with charge
Walking through the vineyards of Montepulciano.

Abbey probably founded by St Romualdo in 1008-1009 and linked to the Camaldolese: upper Romanesque church consecrated in 1105, octagonal bell tower perhaps obtained from a 14th century defensive tower and crypt of Saint Mary of the Graces, perhaps of the 11th century.
Trekking among secular oaks, mouflons and shepherd huts.

In the hamlet Rochemolles, in the former school: objects and tools of everyday life, the traditional costume, sacred furnishings of the chapel of the Madonna degli Angeli and tombolo lace; on the stream the horizontal wheel water mill with two millstones, in service until 1961.

In the former Borghese Granaio, where between the nineteenth and twentieth centuries the peasants gave grain, today also the seat of the City Council; it is part of the museum system of the Lepini Mountains. It exhibits finds from the town of Piano della Civita and materials collected by the local Archaeological Group, from the Neolithic to the early Middle Ages: ceramics, architectural decorations, metal objects, inscriptions, coins and glass.
Where the two rivers of the city unite.

15th-century Colombara, owned by the municipality, with the coats of arms of Monza (lion) and Pagello (lince) and frescoes on the four sides, partially restored. It is one of the 11 remaining doves of the 18 counted at the beginning of the twentieth century, including the Colombara della Cuca (XV century) and that of San Gaetano (Sixth century).

It preserves the relics of the patron saint of Abruzzo and the young: born as a convent in the 16th century and enlarged in the 20th century, in front of the ancient church a new sanctuary was built to welcome pilgrims after the canonization of 1959.
Alleys that smell like sea.
The tower against the pirates, symbol of the city.
The fortress of the Colonna, cradle of Martin V.
By bike on the old railroad, in the countryside of the low Verona.
Baroque in the village of Cireggio.

Born from the ethnographic group La Barchessa founded in 1977, it tells the history and production of Parmigiano Reggiano and the peasant life of the valley: about 40 carriages, carriages and agricultural wagons inlaid between the late nineteenth and mid twentieth centuries and about 3,000 work tools. Access to be agreed with the Association La Barchessa.
Listing in extension: the guide covers for now 3 of the 5 places of culture recorded by the Ministry of Culture in this municipality, as well as churches, squares and nature.

Ancient romoratory then sanctuary where he lived in prayer St. Liberate (born between 1215 and 1218); in 1421 the church was partly rebuilt with a convent next door. The Friars Minor and a little above the Prati di San Liberato, suitable for picnics, look at the Adriatic.
Monastery known for the frescoed cloister, attributed to Todisco or his school.
The majolica ceiling.
€7,50 whole; €5 from 11 to 18 years; free under 11 years
Tower of 1290 on the second hill, reachable on foot by a staircase from the center.

In the hamlet of Pieve Terzagni, the parish church dates back to the 12th century, when the territory was under the dominion of Matilde di Canossa, and was renovated, restored and enlarged between the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries. In the presbytery there is a precious Romanesque mosaic floor of the 12th century with figures and symbols.
Baroque garden among the greats of Europe, with stairs, statues, labyrinth, theater of verzura, the water staircase and the statue of Fama; the villa "of the hundred windows" is not open to visitors.
Three castles in a half-day walk.

Set up like a ...wunderkammer: eighteen showcases of reproductions of plaster and resin mushrooms and sections of natural sciences with fossils, naturalized animals, shells, reptiles and over 130 species of butterflies, as well as exotic fibers, silks and ceramics. Open on the first Sunday of the month from April to October, other days by reservation.

Born with the Marine Biology Station of Porto Cesareo, established in 1966 with museum, library and a small laboratory, today it is located in Villa Lucisani. Over 900 finds on the fauna and flora of the sea: reconstructions of reefs and a breeding of mussels, marine molluscs, deep fishes of the Ionian Sea, tropical sea fauna and unusual or malformed specimens.
Hunting delight of Alfonso II d'Este built between 1578 and 1583 on a project by Giovan Battista Aleotti, with four crenellated towers; it houses the Ecomuseum of the Bosco and the Deer.

Fortress of probably Norman origin of the Sanseverino, strengthened by Ferrante d'Aragona after the Conspiracy of the Barons: pentagonal belt with angular towers, the mast and the Tower of the Cimmaruca; from the terrace you can see the whole Vallo di Diano. Private property, partly exhibition space; in August the re-enactment of the siege of 1497.
Small fortified village of the fourteenth century above the valley towards Siena, with the church of Santi Cosma and Damiano and the playful statue of Luca Cava.

The Mother Church, also known as the Sanctuary of the Madonna dei Miracoli, dates back to the Norman era: it has a characteristic bell tower, a carved portal and works of art in the aisles and chapels.
Discover Cesena Card €13 (with Malatestiana, Rocca and Museum of Ecology)
The Carthusian wanted by Borso d'Este in 1452 and the church started by Biagio Rossetti in 1498, in the center of the large chamber of the monumental cemetery.
The history of the mines before going down to the tunnel.

A ridge village whose first traces date back to the Basilian monks between the 6th and 7th centuries; in the 11th century the town grew around the castle and until the abolition of the fief in 1806 feudal families such as Matera, Loria and Carafa were succeeded. The narrow streets preserve works of modern art, murals and ceramics of various artists; among the historical buildings the parish church of Santa Maria del Piano and the ancient palace seat of the Museum of Chili pepper.
Shows in a Roman theatre.
The theatre saved from his dome.

The peak is 1256 metres from the Aurunci Mountains, reachable from Campodimele with a comfortable walk with a stop at the source Faggetina; from the top the view spans over the Piana di Fondi, the Valle del Liri, the Tyrrhenian and the abbey of Montecassino.
Built during World War I on a deep abyss of more than 80 meters.

Borgo dei Monti Lepini divided between Cori Monte and Cori Valle, surrounded by about two kilometers of polygonal walls; on the acropolis the Temple of Hercules of the first century BC, in the valley the columns of the Temple of Dioscuri, and then the complex of Sant'Oliva with the City Museum and the Oratory of the SS. Announced. In the hamlet of Giulianello the Palazzo Salviati and the lake, a natural monument.
Among the shelters of the vineyards.
Fountain of about 1300 with the original tub used as a washbasin, surmounted by a large lion of stone of Roman times, on the wide open space in front of the cathedral.
Erected in the 12th century and modified several times, it retains much of the Romanesque perspective; it venerates the ancient icon of the Iconaveter, at the origin of the first church.

It was founded in the 13th century between the fortifications fought between Asti and the Biandrate, and passed to the Roeros and from 1680 to the Beraudo, made by Maria Giovanna Battista of Savoia Nemours. In 1840 the court architect Ernesto Melano transformed it: removed moat and drawbridge, added entrance porch and staircase, covered the courtyard to form a double-height living room. The visit goes from the cellars to the Salone delle Feste and to the Chamber of the Minister; the "Trenino del Conte" is a railway model of the late nineteenth century with locomotives and wagons from 1896 to 1939. Closed in August.
Mountain a few minutes from the center.
Above Ballino, on the slope of Monte Misone, opens with an entrance about 12 meters high and about 20 meters wide; it is reached with a path and in some summer periods hosts events.

Molco mine at 1,580 m in the valley of Brissout, active from the early twentieth century to 1979, set up and managed by CAI di Lanzo. The galleries, about 3 km on two levels, are preserved as during the activity and are only visited with a guide by reservation; the external mining park (miner's room, electric locomotive shed, engine room) is always open and freely accessible. You can only walk from the village Vrù, in about an hour-one-and-a-half; not accessible in a wheelchair.
Along Via Brisa the remains of the imposing imperial palace of the end of the III century.
One of the Romanesque parishes of the Matilda plain.

The villa was built between the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries by the influential Panzerini family and then passed to the Simoncini; it is accessed near the parish church of San Girolamo, but the interior is not visitable. A little further north, Casa Panzerini hosts associations, library, historical archives and exhibition and cultural halls.
Fourteen km of track along the canal to Altedo, land of the green IGP asparagus.

A nineteenth-century noble house in Sicilian neoclassical style, already home to the writer Luigi Capuana, father of Verismo with Verga and De Roberto: the alcove, the studio and the library preserve vintage furnishings, newspaper clippings, prints and youthful photos, two etchings by Telemaco Signorini with the old Florence, a caricature by Ugo Fleres and 1,300 ancient volumes by the library of the Cappuccini.
The San Cristoforo frescoed on the bell tower.
The fifteenth century next to the castle.

Villa of the XVII century wanted by the Priuli family, with a large cycle of frescoes by the seventeenth-century painter Paolo Piazza di Castelfranco; today owned by the municipality, it houses cultural center, library and the Civic Museum. The archaeological collection includes ceramics from the Middle-Recent Bronze Age from the Motte di Castello di Godego, bowls, olles, millstones and millstones, recovered since 1975 by the Historical Archaeological Group of Castelfranco Veneto and Godego Castle, and the Longobard sets with lunula earrings found in San Pietro in 1952. In 1481 Francesco di Giorgio Martini built for Federico da Montefeltro the fortress on the Cappuccini hill, demolished in 1502 by Guidobaldo so that it would not fall into the hands of Cesare Borgia. Fraction close to the village, abandoned by the inhabitants in 1982 after an earthquake: a small ghost village where you can see glimpses of the daily life of the post-war period.

It excels restored ex-vote chosen from about 300 recorded, dating from the seventeenth to the mid-20th century; the dozens of oldest wooden tablets, from the San Quirico Sanctuary, are a unique case among the collections of the sanctuaries of the province. Renovated in Baroque style in the 18th century by the Lorraine architect Francesco de Willencourt, who reversed the original orientation (facing west, apse east). The 11th century Romanesque bell tower is the oldest medieval artifact that has come to us; in the interior there is a single nave, on the right of the main altar, a wooden crucifix from the 15th century.
Beach of 1.7 km of clear sand and pebbles, immediately after Coccorrocci, with services similar to Foxi Manna; further north Foxi de Lioni, south on Prettu.

The country of the Iglesiente surrounded by about thirty sites of mining archaeology, with the Roman temple of Antas dedicated to the Sardus Pater, the caves of Su Mannau linked to an ancient water cult, the water mill Licheri of 1750 and, about 10 km, the beach of Portixeddu.

Managed by the Regional Direction National Museums Veneto, it was born from the exhibition Terredacque set up in 2014 by the Superintendence and tells the territory from the protohistoric village of San Gaetano to the Portus Reatinum of Plinio up to the modern Caorle. On the first floor the most significant finds of Caorle and surroundings, from the late Bronze Age (XIII-early XII century BC) to the modern age; on the ground floor the history of the brig Mercury, a warship with two trees of Napoleonic age passed from the French fleet to the Italian one. Number reservations +39 0421 83149 and +39 379 1805649.

Built in 1499, it has a white interior, a upper gallery with wrought iron grate and a baroque altar in gold lacquered wood from 1697 by the Palermon sculptor Pietro Bencivinni.

On the square are gathered the parish church of St. Peter the Apostle, former cathedral of the fifteenth century several times rebuilt, the oratory of St. Cross of the sixteenth century, the oratory of the Rosary of the eighteenth century and the parish house with the archive of ancient writings and documents; the town hall occupies the former Granatic mountain.

In an ancient restored paper mill (the Lower Maina) in the Valley of the Cartiere, with sixteenth-century nucleus: it tells the production of paper from the Middle Ages to the twentieth century, with the first printed books in Toscolano in the sixteenth century and demonstrations of paper handmade by former papermakers. The medieval gate with a sharp arch joins the Earth to the district of Santa Maria; the civic tower, symbol of the village, takes its name from the wild olive tree that grows there. First work of the Fiumara d'arte, the open-air sculpture museum designed by Antonio Presti and inaugurated on October 10, 1986, which extends for about 200,000 square meters of state property among the most common. Ruins of the Roman town hall of Superaequum in Macrano and Colle Caprelle: the excavations have returned houses with mosaic floors, paved streets and sacred buildings, including one dedicated to Hercules Winner with bronzes and votive inscriptions. Medieval tower at the entrance of the village, under the fourteenth-century belt. Borgo collected at the foot of Monte Baldo, built on ancient Etruscan and Roman settlements, with squares, churches and historical buildings: Villa Carlotti with the Civic Museum and the 14th-century Companti, the monumental Platano dei Cento Bersaglieri and the panoramic paths of Baldo.

On the ground floor of the eighteenth-century Palazzo Ferla-Bonelli, in the rooms once inhabited by the massarium, collects the objects of the peasant civilization saved by the poet and ethnologist Antonino Uccello (Canicattini 1922), established at Palazzolo in 1944: wooden spoons, orange wood nativity scenes, cart keys and iron sculptures, which he also exhibited in the galleries of the North.

Of trapezoidal plan, it dominates Piazza Umberto I: on a small fortress of the tenth century, the structure of the twelfth century was enlarged in the thirteenth century, the central tower with the civic clock is owed to Paolo Guinigi and in 1675 the terrace on the square and the monumental arch were added. Ludovico Ariosto resided there from 1522 to 1525 as governor of the extended province; municipal seat until the war, it was severely bombed in 1944 and then restored. It houses the Palazzo di Atlante, a museum dedicated to Ariosto that combines contemporary art and traditions of Garfagnana, with a multimedia installation in the bell tower on the first two episodes of the Orlando Furioso, Follia d'Orlando and Â"Astolfo sulla Luna" .

With Santo Stefano Belbo is the most lively village in Piedmont: in the hamlets dominates Barbera, among farmsteads, ciabòt, bourgeois villas and campestri churches, and survives the small production of Uvalino linked to Count Filippo Asinari of San Marzano, who introduced Chardonnay in Piedmont. Between Costigliole and Isola d'Asti extends the Nature Reserve of Rio Bragna.

Set up in 1997 in two rooms of the eighteenth-century Palazzo Loreti, seat of the town hall: one reconstructs the peasant house with kitchen, room and shelter of the animals, the other exposes the agricultural tools donated by the elderly, each with its dialect name.

Ceramic city at the gates of the Regional Park of Matese, rebuilt after the earthquake of 1688 with a regular and wallless system: Piazza San Martino, the Cathedral of the Holy Trinity, the Civic Museum of Ceramics and, in the surrounding area, the Hannibal Bridge, the gorges of the Titerno and the Leonessa.
Next to the castle, in a complex wanted by Cristoforo Caetani in 1400, it preserves the fresco of Our Lady of the Cerase.

Ethnographic museum in the master house of the doctor Giovanni Porcu Duras and his wife Rosina Satta Mulas, with furnishings designed by the sculptor Francesco Ciusa. It exhibits traditional gavoesi clothes, about 100 jewels and amulets in silver filigree of the goldsmith Nanni Rocca and the collection "Jocos" of more than 3,000 objects among traditional toys, musical instruments (including on tumbarinu, the drum of the carnival) and scale reconstructions of agropastoral workplaces. cumulative ticket with the Museo del Fiore Sardo €7, reduced €5.

Built in 1913 on the initiative of the parish priest to connect Pieve to the port, salt for about 6 km from the lake (65 m) to Pieve (423 m) along the deep gorge of the Brasa stream, between tunnels and narrow hairpin bends, sometimes dug into the rock and sometimes overhanging. At the opening a correspondent of the Frankfurter Zeitung called it the most beautiful street in the world. It is recommended to moderate speed and avoid holiday weekends.

Residenza dei Visconti Venosta: left wing rebuilt at the end of the 17th century, right wing rebuilt at the end of the 19th century by the Marquis Emilio, Minister of Foreign Affairs, and public park of 20,000 m2. Donated to the Municipality in 1982 by Marquisa Margherita Pallavicino Mossi, it preserves historical environments, period furniture, the doors of an ancon of Cipriano Valorsa (1597), a Redeemer on the Sepulchre of Scuola Ferrarese of the sixteenth century, the library and the family archive. Only with guided tour at 10.30, 14 and 16, recommended booking.

Neoclassical church built in 1841-1842 on the area of the ancient castle of the Community and open to worship in 1852; the interiors were decorated between 1878 and 1887 by Giovanni Valtorta, Achille Secchi and Luigi Morgari, and there is a Crucifixion on canvas by Francesco Sampietro of 1852. Next to it, the coevo municipal palace preserves in the council room part of the fifteenth-century structure of the old castle.

Building of the Sixties on an overhang over the cove of Ficocella, built for the finds found in the territory since 1948: materials of a Greek settlement and a necropolis of the sixth century BC and finds of ancient wrecks. Common at the gates of Modena, documented by 962 and then feud of the Estensi of San Martino in Rio, known for over a century for the balance industry: the Museum of Libra, the Curiel lakes and the reserve of the Secchia expansion boxes, the sanctuary of Sassola and the Clock Tower.

Medieval village of Orvieto among olive groves and vineyards, with castle, walls and towers; in the territory the castles of Montegiove and Castel di Fiori and especially the Scarzuola, Franciscan convent transformed by Tomaso Buzzi between 1958 and 1978 in an ideal city of seven theatres.

At the base of the Monticolo hill, on the right bank of the Oglio, a ritual mass of the Copper Age (second half of the III millennium BC) called  "Rock of the Alabards" for the nine alabards carved almost life-size; the excavation of 2002 revealed under them a second composition of fifteen daggers. The site is free and always visitable; at the Corni Freschi there is also a climbing wall and on the Monticolo the Giant Bench n. 72.

Ethnographic Museum on the ground floor of the former Palazzo Pretorile, once home of the Austrian barracks: it tells the life in Val di Sole in the last century with original tools such as the loom and the kangaroo, the reconstructions of the stua and the cuisine and the traditional solandra house, the carpenter, blacksmith, breeder, weaver and calderaio and miniature models of the Venetian sawmills and farms. A section is dedicated to the mycologist Don Giacomo Bresadola.
The local artisans hold shops where to buy objects and know a craft handed down from generation to generation.

Already San Leonardo, documented from the sixteenth century, deconsecrated after 1800 and used as a base and slaughterhouse, was restored around 1860 by the brotherhood of the shoemakers. Romanesque portal with Malta's cross, linked to the pilgrims of the Valeria street; inside the sixteenth-century altar of the Magdalena church among the coats of arms of the Caracciolo, feudal for three centuries.

Abbey Basilica founded in the 5th century on the burial of the martyr, rebuilt in the 16th century and consecrated in 1606, one of the largest in Italy: it preserves the altarpiece of Veronese with the Martyrdom of Santa Giustina.

Among the paved streets are the medieval church of San Niccolò and, in the third quarter of Codaccio, San Leonardo, of the 12th century and remodelled in the 16th century, which even with the interior destroyed in the Second World War preserves the  "Decollation of the Baptist" (1588-89) by Francesco Vanni; just outside Porta Talassese the church of Sant'Andrea, of 1118. At the entrance of the village the Monument to the Fallen at work and, next door, the stone that recalls the killing of David Lazzaretti in 1878.

Designed and built by the architect Carlo Mollino between 1946 and 1947 at 2,286 meters, it housed the arrival station of a slittovia and was designed as a refuge for skiers; until the mid-sixties it served skiers under Mount Triplex. The Municipality defines it as one of the most important works of modern architecture in Italy: after a long abandonment it has been restored inside and outside and today it is again a refreshment point on the slopes, with terrace.

The municipality of Alto Mincio, which with the hamlet of Rivalta sul Mincio overlooks the Natural Reserve Valli del Mincio, where a fishing house has been hosting the Ethnographic Museum of the Crafts of the River since 1998. In the capital, the sixteenth-century Villa Balestra houses the museum dedicated to Ippolito Nievo.

karst cave at about 1,068 meters in the limestone-dolomitic massif of Crasto, the main one of the western side of the Fortress, partly still unexplored: stalactites, stalagmites, columns and mammellonary concretions of calcite; there live two endemic troglobular invertebrates and there were found materials of the Neolithic and early metals. Born as a guard tower of the Griffos in the 12th century, it has the current plant of the Malatestian period (1293-1324): quadrilateral plant with angular towers and the mast, the strongest tower. Giovanni Sforza renovated it in 1494 for Lucrezia Borgia (temmas and inscriptions in the courtyard, frieze of the Passion and battle scene of Friend Aspertini and students); Umberto Zanvettori restored it in 1921-23 by furnishing the noble plan, and in 1928 passed to the State. Inside the room of Francesca, the dressing room of Lucrezia Borgia, a glazed terracotta altarpiece by Andrea della Robbia and the altarpiece of Giovanni Santi, father of Raffaello, with the oldest image of Gradara.

Started in 1257 by Fra' Filippo da Campello at the opposite end of the historic centre compared to San Francesco: a Latin cross plan, three rampant arches, a square bell tower and a cycle of frescoes on the legend of the saint.

The road of Bagnolo leads to Ponte dell'Olio between churches, villas and remains of fortifications; Chiulano, of Roman origin, is the highest hamlet of the municipality and a famous viewpoint, Bicchignano a panoramic point just below the pass of the Bagnolo.

Opened to worship on 12 September 1909 in place of the ancient parish of Moconesi and consecrated on 28 February 1916 by Monsignor Giovanni Gamberoni, of the diocese of Chiavari; the parish also included Moconesi Alto, which broke off on 1 November 1929.
