Romanesque church whose origins date back to the 10th century, built where in the Trajan age there was a temple of the lovers of Hercules and the Emperor, as attested by the  "Decree of the lovers of Hercules," epigraphed on the limestone walled inside. Three-nave basilica plant with semicircular apse, columns that hold round arches and light that grows from the rose window towards the presbytery; the facade has a rare masonry opus spicatum and transenna in travertine and terracotta with Greek crosses and of St. Andrew. Restored in 1885 and in 1970-71, when under the apse emerged traces of a larger apse considered early Christian; it received the "Meraviglia Italiana" stamp. Open Saturday and Sunday 8-18 secondo italia.it.
Built for Arsenal workers, opened in 1869; example of late 19th century architecture.

Municipality of the coast to the east of Palermo, with the Hellenistic-Roman city of Solunto on Mount Catalfano and its necropolis, Villa Filangeri seat of the Town Hall, the harbours of Santa Flavia and Porticello and the ancient port of Solanto with the castle.

Rebuilt in the middle of the eighteenth century on the site of a church considered of 1300, of which remains the fourteenth-century bell tower. He keeps in a bronze urn, in the chapel dedicated to him, the body of St. Valentine, patron saint of Palmoli, an eighteenth-century organ carved and gilded and two water saints carved with a snake and a fish.

The oldest church in Maratea (XI-XII century), in the historic centre, is the tallest building in the village and contains frescoes from the fourteenth and fifteenth centuries.

Outdoor gallery of frescoes and contemporary sculptures that decorate the houses of the village Bonda, started in the eighties by the Vercellian painter Gastone Cecconello (1942). It is visible outdoors every day without reservation; on the upper pedestrian street of the village is the Association Amici della Bonda.

The ancient Piazza Grande, wide and tree-lined: on the side of the castle of the Pico, whose fortifications were lost with the explosion of the powder keg of 1714, remain a seventeenth-century porch and the facade of the Galleria Nuova next to a neo-Gothic tower of the twentieth century and the Teatro Nuovo (1905). On the south side, the 1468 Palazzo Comunale with portico on marble columns, flanked by the Palazzo della Ragione, with Gothic elements of the late fourteenth century, and Palazzo Bergomi, fifteenth century with ornate terracotta decorations; to the north is the oratory of the Madonna della Porta.

The central square with the Palazzo del Podestà in the middle of the thirteenth century, to merlons with swallow tail, and the Fontana Sturinalto of the end of the thirteenth century, reduced version of the fountain of Perugia; around the Palazzo Comunale and the Loggia of San Francesco.
The castle built around the year 1000 with the church of San Lorenzo and the terrace belvedere; in the village the house where Carducci lived, today museum.
Baroque Basilica of the seventeenth century built on a medieval church of 1372, of which it retains the apse and the late-Gothic octagonal bell tower of 1463; the stone façade remained unfinished.

The capital of the Acaja princes since 1295 and the French fortress between the Five and the Sixteenth Century, at the foot of the Valdese valleys: the historic porticoed centre, the Cathedral of San Donato, San Maurizio on the hill and the Museum of Cavalry.

In the thirteenth century Palazzo Lazzarini, with its precious stone portal, the museum collects mainly paintings on table and canvas from the sixteenth to the eighteenth century coming from the local churches, including the Madonna del Soccorso attributed to the Tolentinate Marchisiano di Giorgio, a series of portraits of illustrious men from the 16th century collection of Paolo Giovio and objects of the Frumentary Mount founded in 1475. Recently, an archaeological section was added with findings from 700-600 B.C.

Designed by Emil Strub and in service since 1903, when it was the longest and steepest funicular, it is a symbol of the country: it climbs in about twelve minutes (845 meters according to Italia.it). Church in Gothic-Aragonese style in the center of the village, in front of Palazzo Boyl; it holds the clothes with which, according to legend, was dried in 1675 the statue of St. Paul that would exude blood.

Of thirteenth-century origin, several times rebuilt (in the Baroque age): it contains a wooden ceiling with coffers dating back to the sixteenth century by Benedetto da Montepulciano, an eighteenth-century altar and frescoes of Giottesca school dated 1394 with the Stories of the Passion.

The municipality describes it as one of the most evocative areas of the city, with small restaurants and bars of Lombard cuisine and lakes and evenings often animated by events on the banks of the Ticino; there are the Town Hall and the archaeological museum, a few minutes walk from the station.

Parish church on top of the village, next to the town hall, renovated several times since 1515; it has a Romanesque bell tower dating from around 1200, several works of art, a large organ and a permanent monumental nativity scene that can be visited in the sacristy.
The symbol of the city of the two seas.

Monumental and social center of the village, of medieval plant, dominated by the Town Hall with next to the Civic Tower and surrounded by gentle palaces, with a fountain in the center. In Palazzo Comunale the Sala della Giunta contains nineteenth-century frescoes and paintings by artists including Simone De Magistris and Corrado Giaquinto.
The tombs in the rock and the boulder in the balance.
The peasant life of a century ago in one room.

Ferruginous and sulphurous waters already known in ancient times, as shown by the votive bronze found in the surroundings, frequented by the pilgrims of the Via Romea in the Middle Ages and valued by the Ubertini in the seventeenth century. The municipality has built the Park Buca del Tesoro, a green area along the river with a fountain with three taps to draw water; near the village also the springs of Rio and Galastri.
The saint of the ancient hospital.

Municipality of the lower Sangone Valley known for the Rea Botanical Garden of San Bernardino, section of the Regional Museum of Natural Sciences with over 2.000 species; on the territory the Sanctuary of Our Lady of the Star and chapels like Santa Teresa d'Avila, frescoed by Francesco Gonin, overlooking the lakes of Avigliana.
Listing in extension: the guide covers for hour 1 of the 3 places of culture recorded by the Ministry of Culture in this municipality, as well as churches, squares and nature.

Built by the Normans at the end of the 11th century at the intersection between Campania and Puglia, summer residence and hunting of Frederick II, then residence of Mary of Hungary from 1284 and feud of the Doria until 1952: ten towers, seven rectangular and three pentagonal, and four entrances; it resisted the earthquakes of 1851 and 1930.
Carts and babes in a baroque villa.

The village preserves the thirteenth century plant, with two streets connected by cobbled staircases and vaulted passages; in the Rione Maggiore (Borgo Inferiore) the houses are narrow between narrow streets. Votive frescoes from the sixteenth century are scattered throughout the country, near the port there is the large seventeenth-century coat of arms of the Mandelli with three rampant red chepards, and the Imperial Mint founded in 1622, today incorporated in a hotel, preserves the road that fed the sweat. Corte Branca, with its portico, is the most expressive historical building in the country.
In Palazzetto Leo, four floors of art, weapons, musical instruments and objects especially from China and Japan, with prints ukiya-e, a section on samurai and sculptures of Gandhara.
Lawns and woods above the city.
MiC card indicates closed every day; contact the museum (0973 686576) before visiting
A few tens of meters from the abbey, a site destined to productive activities in the late Roman age, with paved mosaics and a thermal system. Private area, available upon reservation (085 859 0003).
One of the smallest theatres in Europe.
The Miracle of the Host of the Genoese.

Lake turquoise at the foot of the village, in the valley from which the Volturno is born, with the chain of Mainarde in the background; offers numerous activities for visitors and on its banks there is a restaurant of Molise specialties.
Ham in its microclimate.

Church rebuilt by the Dominicans at the end of the seventeenth century, with a fourteenth-century table of the Madonna and Child of Barnabas of Modena. The Mausoleum of Maiorano (1st century BC), a square structure of about 9 meters on the side linked by tradition to the Maggiorian Emperor, killed in Tortona in 461, is incorporated into the canonical church.
In the fortress of the fourteenth century, seat of the Municipality, the archaeological museum of the Siena Chianti.
The view of the countries of Irpinia.
Just outside the village, it was built by Spinetta Malaspina; today it is the house of the sculptor Pietro Cascella.
A second stage of the Robbiano route of Arcevia.
In Piazza Dante, with an altar dedicated to Saint Francesco Caracciolo, work of Baciccia.
Günther's baroque dome.
A piece of the aqueduct wanted by Augustus and Tiberius for Brescia.
In the refectory of the monastery, the Last Supper of Andrea del Castagno with the Resurrection, the Crucifixion and the Deposition of 1447.

Former talc mine: the first tunnels were dug at the end of the 19th century and the extraction ceased in 1968. The underground path, about one hour long, shows the evolution of mining techniques; inside there are an average of 10 °C, plenty of humidity and stretches with water, and the helmet with light is supplied at the entrance. Only by reservation (two visits per month on Saturday and Sunday); you leave your car at the junction for hamlet Flizzo and walk about 15 minutes on dirt road.

Established on 29 September 2008 in the restored buildings of Borgo Castello, the castle complex destroyed by the earthquake of 1694, then inhabited village and municipal property after the earthquake of 1980. The route goes from the finds of the Fossakultur of Oliveto-Cairano and of Roman age to the half medieval majolica and the Renaissance majolica, up to the production of the nineteenth and twentieth centuries, to the historical bricks, industrial ceramics and the works of contemporary craftsmen.

The main street closed to traffic that crosses the whole city, with boutiques, jewelers, artisan and antique shops, between side alleys; near Porta Catania a sign indicates the narrowest alley in Italy, 43 cm wide.

One of the oldest and largest hospitals in Europe, born to welcome the pilgrims of the Via Francigena: the Hall of the Pilgrimage frescoed in the fifteenth century, the original statues of the Fonte Gaia and temporary exhibitions.
The perimeter of the Venetian Cream.
The agropastoral life of the Vastese inside a castle.
On the trail of the Nun of Manzoni.
A sandy strip about 6 km between the hill of Ansedonia and Mount Argentario, with the Duna Feniglia Nature Reserve.
Church of the XIV century in the homonymous square, which preserves frescoes of the eighteenth century; on the same square stands Palazzo Costantini, with tower and three portals with sharp arch.
Characters, machines and handprinting in one of the most complete printing museums.
In the former stables of Palazzo Rocca, from the prehistory of Tigullio to the furnishings of the necropolis of the Iron Age, up to the Roman and medieval ages; set-up expanded in 2021.
Walk on the lake in front of the islands.
One of the most evocative cemeteries in the region.
Parmigiano Reggiano and its peasant civilization.
The eighteenth-century organ of the country.
A fifth century A.D. mill built by reusing a block of a funeral monument of the first century, with a stretch of coeva road and a gate of the late Dolomites walls.

In a former wash-house and barn of the 1930s, it is the first place to welcome the country: multimedia stations on the history and techniques of the handicraft production of terracotta and brick of Castel Viscardo; book guided tours to the kilns of the territory. Info: tel. 0763 361010.

Small church matrix of the parish, at the foot of the hill of Motta beyond the Alpone, built in the second half of the XII century with a single nave with mixed brick and stone walls like the great churches of Verona of the time; before it the assembly of the free municipality documented in 1208 was gathered. It contains apse frescoes between the end of the fourteenth and early fifteenth centuries with an Annunciation, a fifteenth-century Saint Agatha, Madonnas and votive saints of 1491 and eighteenth-century wooden statues. Open on the second Sunday of the month, 9.30-10.30, with voluntary guides; suggested free offer.
Ancient church in the lower part of the village, with a marble triptych of the sixteenth century.
The Lotto Church, today theater.

Born in 1992, it reconstructs the interior of a traditional house with about 1,500 objects collected in the abandoned villages of the valley of Unerzio: on the first floor work tools and objects of daily mountain life. Opening on request (tel. +39 0171 99017).
The sixteenth-century cathedral whose project Michelangelo worked on.
Norman apses.
18th-century building seat of the civic library and permanent exhibition Magic transparencies.
The medieval heart of the "vina franca" on Francigena.
The nineteenth-century villa with the park in the heart of the village.
The Capuchin monastery at the gates of the village.
Roman villa and abbey on an island with no more water.
In the crypt of the Basilica of St. Bartholomew there is the Diocesan Museum and the treasure of St. Bartholomew.

In the traschette of the alleys you can taste the flavors of the Roman Castles, such as pairs and wild boar sausages with wine. The pig, IGP since 2011, is seasoned with rosemary, garlic and black pepper; the festival, born in 1950, is held on the first Sunday of September with the porchettari in costume and the traditional launch of sandwiches.

The capital of the Highland of the Seven Municipalities, rebuilt entirely after the Great War: visit the Military Shrine, one of the main ossuaries of the First World War, the Astrophysics Observatory founded in 1942 by the University of Padua and the municipal museums, from the Naturalistic Museum Patrizio Rigoni to the open-air museum of Monte Zebio.
Baroque and Rococo church built between 1620 and 1660.
The heart of the village recovered and valued, with houses and small streets always in order; from the hamlet Villa (1234 m) you go up to Serre and Durandini.
Natural area with trails of varying difficulty and guided activities, known for canoeing, rafting, canyoning and climbing on natural rock walls; the park consortium was born in 1995.
The widest view of the Langhe.
Emerald-colored water a stone's throw from the village.
The monument to the composer who for almost a century and a half dominates Piazza Stesicoro, enclosed among noble palaces, at the beginning of the walk towards Villa Bellini.
The Renaissance of Tasso in Castelvetro.

First regional park, established in 1982 on 1,270 hectares between 110 and 470 meters, already hunting reserve of the Farnese and the Bourbon: oaks, chestnuts, pine trees, firs and beech trees, streams, lakes and meadows, accessible only on foot or by mountain bike. The seat is in the neoclassical Casino dei Boschi, designed in 1789; on the side of Collecchio you enter from the parking lot of the Serraglio in via del Conventino.
The baroque synagogue.

Borgo della Tuscia halfway between the lakes of Bracciano and Vico, which owes its bloom to the Justinians: the Palazzo Giustiniani Odescalchi frescoed by Albani, Domenichino and Tempesta with the park of 40 hectares, and on the hill the church of San Vincenzo Martire with the first Christ Portacroce of Michelangelo; all around a beech of over 400 hectares.
In the Chilean Theatre (1920-1931): two tablets by Antonello da Messina of 1460, works by Mattia Preti, Andrea Cefaly, Francesco Jerace and a painting by Renato Guttuso of 1949.

The seat of the ancient Pieve del Bleggio is one of the rare sacred buildings in pure Renaissance style of Trentino, rebuilt in the sixteenth century by the Lombard architect Antonio Gras on the model of Santa Maria Maggiore in Trento; a Romanesque crypt leads to the temple of the XI-XII century. Frescoes by Carlo Donati and, in the chapel, a wooden altar with Pietà and scenes of the Passion that has guarded the Holy Cross considered miraculous since 1624. Open every day 9-17.
The Announced Virgin of Matthew Civitali.
A pasture at the foot of the Odle.

The seaside resort of the Ionian coast of Crotonese was built on the area of ancient Krimisa, between Punta Alice and the Lipuda stream, between the vineyards of Gaglioppo from which Cirò DOC was born; it preserves the remains of the temple of Apollo Aleo, the civic archaeological museum, the sixteenth-century Castello Sabatini and Blue Flag beaches.

Cylindrical powder bowl in stone blocks of about 7 meters in diameter, built between the end of the fifteenth and early sixteenth centuries with brick vault, to store dust and ammunition of the fortress; probably connected by tunnels to the towers. Recently restored, it is the only circular powder keg known in Friuli Venezia Giulia.
In the underground tunnels of Santa Maria della Scala, the state archaeological museum of the city, which can be visited with the route of the complex.

Rocca probably built by Federico da Montefeltro on a project by Francesco di Giorgio Martini: they remain the base of the mast and the sandstone wall, still intact, from which you can enjoy a very wide panorama.
The city of the arcades.

The loggias of the palace of the Municipality close the perspective of the course and symbolize the autonomy of the city maintained also under Venice; for centuries seat of assemblies and proclamations, with the walls adorned with coats of arms and bas-reliefs.

The largest island of the Pontine archipelago, reachable by ferry from Formia, Terracina, San Felice Circeo and Anzio: Bourbon port, Grotte di Pilate and Cisterna della Dragonara of Roman age, the coves of Feola and Frontone, the path of Monte Guardia and, by boat, Palmarola and Zannone.
Exhibitions in a monumental building.
The little church of the plague at the entrance of the village.

Cities at the northern end of Lake Garda, between Rocchetta and Monte Brione: around Piazza III Novembre with the Apponale Tower and the Pretorio Palace are tightened the medieval center and the fortress of the twelfth century, seat of the MAG, while above the city watches the Venetian Bastion and towards Ledro rises the Strada del Ponale; the church of the Inviolata is presented as the most important Baroque church of Trentino.
Romanesque chapel with bell tower of the fourteenth century, restored with important conservation works; it recalls Villa Sant'Eusebio, name of the village from the 10th century.
The ancient Agacium in Valpelline, the land of Fontina and pastures, dominated by the octagonal tower of the Tornalla.

It is the most famous complex of Merate: U-shaped building with a large terrace garden, inhabited for centuries by the same families, hence the name (Brivio Sforza, Trivulzio, Barbiano di Belgiojoso d'Este). The FAI opened its doors to the Fall Days on October 11-12, 2025, with a path between facade and porch, Italian garden, English park, French garden and the carpinata that leads to the viewpoint.
The cloisters of the city of bread.
In Pian de' Valli, at 1,623 meters: consecrated in 1964 and completed in 1975, it has a bell tower of 52 meters and in the apse a mosaic of the Mystery of Creation.
Village with medieval structure with 13th century brick tower, equipped with clock under the Este.
Just outside the old town, the church with the convent and the Romanesque bell tower.
Sanctuary elevated to minor basilica in 1964 by Paul VI: it preserves the relic of the Saint and is the center of Aloisian devotion and destination of pilgrimages. Open every day 8-12 and 15-18.
Among the most loved beaches in the province.
The walls of the Roman colony.

Mountain town on the border between Tuscany and Emilia-Romagna, between woods, valleys, rivers and springs; it crossed the Via Francesca della Sambuca, variant of the Francigena between Pistoia and Bologna, which rises from Pàvana to the fortified village of Castello di Sambuca, while the Itinerary of the Stone of the Ecomuseum connects Torri, the Torraccia and Treppio.
The church in the oaks.

About 9 km from Ussita, at the foot of Mount Bove: ski resort between 1,340 and 1,980 m with 11 slopes for 14 km (including Canalone and Saliere), chairlifts, snow park and the Saliere, Christ of the Snows and Cornaccione refuges; in summer the bike park with chairlift of Selvapiana up to the Rifugio Cristo delle Nevi.
The Eliseo-Praitano collection.
The source of the Catusa is considered one of the most beautiful of the Park of Pollino; along the river an evocative landscape of beech trees.

Wild promontory with a Spanish tower, the highest of the Nurra, reachable by a winding path; a panoramic terrace about 200 meters away looks at the Piana Island and the Asinara. Pilgrims and hawks of the queen fly there.
Nineteenth-century portals to discover alley by alley.

The Roman Brixia and the Lombard UNESCO heritage since 2011, with the Capitolium and the monastery of San Salvatore Santa Giulia; the Castle on the Cidneo hill, the squares of the Loggia, Paolo VI and Vittoria, the two Duomi and the Pinacoteca Tosio Martinengo.
Paths from Camogli and Ruta towards San Rocco, with the parish overlooking the Paradise Gulf, and Punta Chiappa, a fishing village with the drums of the Second World War.

In Villa Castelli the Doge's Palace houses the Civic Museum with the findings of the Magnogreque necropolis of Pezza Petrosa, whose archaeological park is just over 2 km from the village. In the countryside you can visit the Trappeto del Duca, an ancient underground oil mill overlooking the Ionian-Salentine plain.
A 17th-century church of private foundation.

Hiking trail (E) of 8 km, about 2 hours and 30, with 400 m of climb, walkable, by bike and horse, which starts from the last houses of the village along the road to Monte Morra. Crossing karst fields with outlying rocks and wide view of the Aniene valley, Marcellina and Palombara Sabina, go back Valle Cavalera between secular beech trees and agrifogli, where you will meet horses in the wild, up to the Pratone, karst field with sinkholes and swallows at the foot of Monte Gennaro.
The Challant stables.
The cliff rises steeply for 660 meters from the gorge of the Val Sarentino, near Castel Roncolo, with the chapel of San Giovanni on top; a rewarding excursion.
From the convent to the prison to the museum.

Opened on 29 September 2002 in the Convent of the SS. Trinity and recognized Museum of regional interest in 2010, collects painting, sculpture, graphics, photography and multimedia works of Italian art and bell from the second half of the twentieth century. Among the funds: almost all Barisani's graphic work (from the period ...Mac ... 1950-58 to organic abstraction), about fifty drawings and watercolours by Guido Gambone (1945-69) and 22 works by Peter Ruta made in Italy between 1947 and 1963. The price depends on the exhibition in progress; barrier-free.
The bridge over the Neva.
Egypt in the heart of Sannio.
A small Romanesque two-tone stone.
The crescent harbor, heart of the island.
The village is part of the Strada dell'Olio and typical products of Sabina and VisitLazio defines extra virgin olive oil as its yellow gold.
The pope on Vatican radio, at his house.

The village of the Dauni Mountains, 732 meters, with a medieval old town of temple memory, the Tower of the Grand Prior of the twelfth century, historical fountains such as the Mutant Fountain and, from Muraglione, the view of the Tabletop up to Gargano and Tremiti.
One of the oldest frescoes in the province and views of the city.
The karst forest of Majella.

Remains of the medieval fortification lined up with the Ferrari, Ghibelline family who ruled the Lower Ossola, and dependent on the castle of Vogogna: there are two granite lunettes with the anvil, the pinnacle and the hammer of the Ferrari and an ogival portal in serizzo surmounted by a Gothic window. It rises on a hill in the village, at the border guard; the access is free and free.

At the foot of Montello, the karst hill theater of the Battle of Solstizio of 1918, Volpago del Montello preserves in Venegazzù the eighteenth-century Villa Spineda and the church of Giordano Riccati, and in Selva a church with canvases of the Guards and Fontebasso.
Lake beaches at altitude with views of the Lagorai.

Baroque mother church on the Corso Umberto, rebuilt after 1693; its dome is among the first in reinforced concrete of Sicily. Inside stuccoes of the Serpottian school and a statue of the Bagnasco Palermo; the nineteenth-century statue of the Santissimo Salvatore comes out in procession at the end of August.

City of the Lametina plain born from the union of Nicastro, Sambiase and Sant'Eufemia: the Norman-Svevo castle on the hill, the convent of San Domenico with the Archaeological Museum and the coastal tower of the Knights of Malta.
In 1224, with walled the Roman funeral plaque dedicated to Valeria Terza by her husband Caio Elio.

Church of the hamlet of San Tomaso that the Touring indicates, with the castle of Susans, as one of the two notable historical-artistic sites of the municipality: it preserves frescoes of the XIII and XIV century.

Of medieval origin: under the floor the walls of the church built between 1200 and 1300 in the Villa Nova di Pavone have emerged. A destination of pilgrimages, it preserves an 18th century altarpiece with the Virgin attributed to Valsesian masters. Open during functions.
Mountaineering and contemporary art.
The fountains and the risings of the Lower.
The Dukes' mother church, with the organ restored.

Built by Campanari at the beginning of the fourteenth century in via Umberto I and expanded from the seventeenth century, with the representation hall and a glass chandelier of Murano; municipal since 2019 and open to the public.
The ruins of the Pico pantheon.
Country churches on the streets of transhumance.
The fountain of the Norman princess.

The Italians conquered the summit on 23 July 1916; on 23 September 1916 the Austro-Hungarians made a mine shine that killed the occupants, and the imperial troops remained on the Cimone until the end of the conflict. Above the crater rises the ossuary with a high cusp that guards the remains of many fallen; among the beech trees remain walkways, trenches and galleries, partly recovered from the Ecomuseum of the Great War.
The village has numerous fountains: the fountain of Pescarella is known for its sweet-tasting water considered beneficial; the fountain of San Nicola was renovated in 1952.
The garden of the monks, between redwood and ginkgo.
The sunset on the Strait.
The palace of Piazza Venezia where lived since 1818 Maria Letizia Ramolino, mother of Napoleon, with the green balcony; today space for art and culture.
The walk of the Anconetani to the sea.
The "borgo degli artisti" is on a tufa spur in the Treja Valley Park, among the naturally fortified most evocative villages in Italy.
A small eighteenth-century church in the village.
The architectures escaped the earthquake of 1693.
The remains of the Arduini castle that dominates from above the square and the village.
Romanesque church of the 12th century along one of the paths.
In the footsteps of the Walser to the pass.
Place of recollection and memory in Piazzale XXVI July, of which in 2025 the centenary was celebrated.
The inscription that inspired the pirate museum.
Convent with a 17th century cloister that houses the town's civic museum.
The highest view of the lake.
Nineteenth-century villa built in 1847 by Bernardino Branca, creator of Fernet-Branca, on the lake in Pallanza: exhibitions and events all year round in the villa and park.
Fifty kilometers of trails a stone's throw from the sea.

Tower of the Town Hall 27,85 meters high, with an evident out of lead that makes it one of the most hanging towers in Italy; the origins would go back to the 8th century and around the Mille was consolidated outside, taking the current cylindrical shape.
Church with Romanesque bell tower, where in 1575 Giorgio Castelrotto, captain of Primiero, suspected of bringing the plague, took refuge.

The medieval village on the cliff with alleys and houses in tuff, in contrast with the straight Renaissance streets of the Farnese, the Apostolic Palace, now Town Hall, and the Fountain of the Unicorn.

In the Villa Comunale Generale Dalla Chiesa, built in 1762 above a small cave and restored in 1929; it houses a nineteenth-century painting by Saint Francis of Assisi and has a small olive grove and a chestnut tree behind it.
Two oratories of the fourteenth century with frescoes, in the localities of Monteforte (oratory of Sant'Antonino) and Riva di Biscia.
Church designed by the architect Pilotti of Ascoli Piceno, with in the apse a mosaic of Gaudenzi, of the Vatican school, which depicts the Paschal Christ between Saints and Blesseds of Piceno.
Castle at 387 meters on Monte San Pancrazio with the church of San Nicola, with a sober façade, from the end of the 15th or beginning of the 16th century.
A curious passage under the roofs.

Country of the valley of the Bradano with the neoclassical Fontana Cavallina surmounted by a Roman Ceres, the Sanctuary of Maria SS. delle Grazie, the Palazzo Marchesale De Marinis and, about 15 km, the Norman castle of Monteserico.

The village of the upper Val Venosta dominated by Castel Chur, built in 1259 and for over 500 years by the Trapp family, with its famous armory; in the village the Vuseum, the museum of the Val Venosta, from which a path along the Leitenwaal and Berkwaal routes rises to the prehistoric site of the Ganglegg.

Building with several factory bodies, originally part of the walls: the oldest walls (XIII century about) preserve multi-lobed rosettes and an ogival bifora in Amalfi style. Residence of the Spinelli princes, in the sixteenth century it was the meeting point of intellectuals such as Gregorio Calorprese and Pietro Metastasio; today it is of the Municipality, it houses the Municipal Library with eighteenth-century paintings of biblical subject and events in the garden and in the halls.
Small stone village near the waterfall, a subject loved by landscape painters of the nineteenth century.

17th century church dedicated to the patron saint San Martino di Tours, with eighteenth-century paintings by Petrini da Carona, Croce di Varese, Valtorta and Maroni, the ancient marble main altar of the Viggiute Giovanni Maria Giudici and Giovanni Rizzi and the baroque sacristy carved by the hermit friar Antonio Rigola, author with the same collaborators of confessionals and pulpit. The stone bell tower of Viggiù, dating back to 1804, is the highest in the area.

In the Middle Ages the bridge made Cuorgnè an important shopping centre, a necessary passage for merchants from Ivrea to Avigliana and the Valley of Susa; the oldest document that cites it is of 1439, and in 1469 the construction of a more lasting bridge on the site of the current Ponte Vecchio was entrusted to Giovanni di Piacenza. Many times damaged by the floods (1491, 1780), it had thirteen stone and lime arches; after the floods of 1845-1846 it was decided to rebuild a hundred meters further downstream, with works started in 1850 on a project by engineer Edward Capello.
The feudal palace became a civic museum.

The most important Baroque palace in the city, the work of Baldassarre Longhena, since 1902 seat of the collection of modern art of the Municipality, started in 1897 with the second Biennale; on the third floor the Oriental Art Museum, with unified ticket.
no time: entrance during liturgical celebrations, guided tours on the occasion of FAI Days and Open Villas

The village overlooks the south coast of the island, with pavements, balconies and benches carved into the local granite; Piazza Comando was built at the end of the 19th century for maritime military command. On July 22, the feast of Santa Maddalena has a procession at sea.

On a plateau at 972 meters dominated by Maiella, with a view to the sea, the site is frequented at least from the IV-III century BC; the visible structure dates back to the middle of the I century BC, after the birth of the Carricini municipality. Damaged by the earthquake of 354 and restored, the city remained inhabited at least until the sixth century. The excavations, begun in the 1940s, brought to light the acropolis with two temples and a sacellus, the theatre, the baths at the ancient source and the paved forum with the basilica julio-claudia, the tabernacles and the epigraph in bronze letters of the patron Ernenni Capitone and his heir Erennia Proiecta. The area is freely accessible.
The flora of Apuane and Appennino in one garden.

On the hill, perhaps already home to a temple dedicated to Mercury, the Benedictines of Subiaco founded in the eighth century the church and monastery of San Zosimo; in the first half of the thirteenth century the complex passed to the Friars Minor, who placed it under the protection of San Michele Arcangelo, from which the name of the hill. It was the destination of pilgrimages as an Anthony's sanctuary and there is a finger of Saint Anthony of Padua; in the cloister there is a stationary marble cross carved on the back of a sacrificial stone.
Scientific museum and astronomical observatory indicated by the Region among the attractions of the city.
Rationalism just a stone's throw from the cathedral.

Already the Collegial Church of San Pellegrino, it is known for its bronze portal and the imposing bell tower; it is dedicated to San Pellegrino Martire, the town's companion, and to Sant'Alberico Crescitelli.
Ancient paths once crossed by mules and chariots, which connect the villages with each other and with the sea.
The fortress of the Borgia on the village.
The lawn of the choice of the Reformation.
In the heart of the decumans.
A rare example of a city built by industry.

The museum is housed in the ancient Waldensian temple of 1556, the only place of Waldensian worship in the valleys that survived the persecutions of the seventeenth century, and tells the history of the valley from prehistory to today, with sections on talc mines, minerals, flora and fauna, agriculture and milk processing; re-established in 2001. Next to it stands the modern temple inaugurated in 1962, at 1455 meters the highest of the Waldensian valleys, with eighteenth-century benches and a large stone mosaic. In summer open on weekdays 15-19 and holidays also 9-12; in winter on request.
Symbol of civic power, among the most significant medieval public buildings in Tuscany.
In the single ticket (€7 full, €5 reduced)
The castle that dominates the Vallo di Lauro.

It occupies some rooms of Palazzo Frangipane, an ancient noble building of municipal property with construction phases of the XVI-XVIII centuries. On the ground floor local fauna, Mediterranean shells and crabs of the Tuscan Archipelago; in the large octagonal hall of the upper floor one of the most important European collections of trilobites, with ammonites and remains of marine and terrestrial reptiles (plesiosaur, mosasaur, dinosaur) ordered by Cambrian to Oligocene, as well as minerals and a showcase of experimental archaeology. The archaeological and palaeontological finds are not currently exposed. Open on Sundays and holidays (times indicated in a different way from the card), other days on request.

Established in 1997 and inaugurated on 20 May 1999 in the presence of Paolo Conte, it tells the accordion industry that made Stradella famous in the world: the origins of the instrument and the 44 factories active in the city since 1876, when Mariano Dallapè opened his first laboratory. Three sections in five halls (historical context, didactic part on the instrument's operation, street models in chronological order) with the first instrument built by Dallapè, the precious Organfisa \liturgica \"the organ sound and the reconstruction of a craft workshop. Free admission on the first Sunday of the month; reservation recommended also to individuals.
On the right bank of Chisone, with a small natural lake, one of the most intact alpine villages in the valley.
The Madonna survived the 1944 fire.
Planetary and telescopes under the castle sky.

City of the upper valley of the Cesano, on a large terrace at the confluence with the Cinisco, known for the Golden Bronzes by Cartoceto, a Roman equestrian group exhibited in the former convent of San Giacomo. The centre preserves the Duomo, Baroque churches, the Ducal Palace, the Town Hall and the Teatro Angelo Dal Foco; in autumn the National Fair of Fine White Truffles is held.
The valley under the monumental bridge, which preserves the evidence of the ancient volcanic activity of the area.
It combines a UNESCO oratory and one of the masterpieces of Byzantine ivory.
More than a century of town gang.
A baroque palace inside a 14th century castle.
The medieval gates of the village.
Small port in the homonymous resort along the approximately seven kilometers of the coast of Muggesa.
Borgo delle Crete Senesi closed by the walls of 1379, with two doors, Senese and Romana, and two museums dedicated to sharecropping and sacred art.
The village that gives its name to the great red of the Langhe, with the crenellated tower symbol of the village and the regional wine shop in a deconsecrated church.
The rye barn.

A large spring basin between Polcenigo and Caneva, at the foot of Cansiglio, a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 2011 among the prehistoric palafittic sites of the Alpine arch. Research since the 1980s has revealed a Neolithic village with huts on the banks and on small islets, dated with dendrochronology to about 4500-3500 BC; the finds are at the Archaeological Museum of Western Friuli in Torre di Pordenone. On site the tracks are poorly legible: italia.it recommends a guided tour; the area also applies to the natural environment.
The palace where you taste the wines of Monferrato.
Church of very ancient origins, erected around the middle of the fifteenth century on the plant of the Romanesque-Byzantine church of St. Nicholas.

Remains of the Etruscan Vatluna, at the most splendor in the 7th century BC and rediscovered at the end of the 19th century by Isidoro Falchi: the walls of the Arce on the acropolis, the districts of Poggiarello Renzetti (with the Via Decumana and the Casa Medea) and Costa Murata, the Domus dei Dolia and, along the Via dei Sepolcri, the tombs of the Belvedere, the Pietrera (the largest funeral monument of Vetulonia) and the Diavolino II.

The small Lake Baccio, of glacial origin at 1554 m, can be reached in half an hour from Lake Santo under Mount Rondanio (path CAI 523); the circular Lake Turchino, at 1600 m, is three hours from the parking lot of Lake Santo.
A view of the hills of Sangiovese.
A rural church of the sixteenth century.

In Scapoli survives the artisan construction of the zampogna, handed down by a small group of artisans to the new generations; the instruments are sold in the shops of the district Fontecostanza. The village hosts the International Festival of Fampogna with market exhibition and on 22 April the archaic Falò of San Giorgio.
It dates back to the fifteenth century and belonged to the abbey of Farfa; above the door a bezel of the sculptor G. Sassetti (1904).
The Walser Chapel.

In Palazzo Lodispoto on Piazza Duomo, about 400 typewriters from all over the world and a section dedicated to Adriano Olivetti.
Church known for its imposing staircase.
Church of the capital that preserves an ancient crucifix in polychrome wood of Romanesque art of the XIII century.
The ancient entrance to the castle.

It was built in the cistern of a Roman villa and preserves the Tauroctonia fresco with Mitra that kills the white bull, from the second half of the second century A.D.; it was discovered by chance in 1962 during works in a cellar at the foot of the historic centre. It is one of three Italian mitrei with a frescoed tauroctonia, with the Mitreo Barberini of Rome and that of Santa Maria Capua Vetere.
Church of the 11th century, next to the cemetery, which houses a valuable 16th century fresco.
The music complex designed by Renzo Piano and delivered to the city on December 21, 2002.
See closely how Calvisano's caviar is born.
One of the most significant monuments of Molise, well preserved, with contemporary art in the rooms.
The only museum in the world dedicated to umbrellas and parasols, in the village of the umbrella makers.

Wanted by Novello Malatesta and opened between 1452 and 1454, it is the first civic library in Europe: the classroom with three naves with the plutei and the codes has arrived intact until today. It has been registered in the UNESCO World Memory Register since 2005.
From Romanesque to Neoclassical.
The sandy beach is quite short, with pines, palm trees and oleanders, with the sea dune in front of the archaeological park; the bike path crosses the village and reaches San Benedetto del Tronto.

Country of the Valley Grana guardian of Provencal culture: in Santa Lucia (Sancto Lucio de Coumboscuro) the ethnographic museum of the Coumboscuro and the Roumiage de Setembre, in San Pietro the headquarters of the Ecomuseum Terra del Castelmagno with the \'babaciu' of straw, and in the woods the ring of the Sarvanot Path.
A thousand-year-old castle with inside the museum of Sergio Leone.
visits only with guided tour and by reservation

Continuing along the coast you reach the ancient port of Solunto, with the fortress of the 12th century and the Gothic castle of the Princes of San Vincenzo, which has performed the function of trap and loader.

Romanesque church in Piazza della Repubblica, with ancient origins and visible traces of the restorations of the centuries; inside frescoes of the Sienese school and a fifteenth-century baptismal font.
The golden ciborium next to the Roman forum.
A quiet stop.
Thirteen towers remain in the center, the most important tower of the 12th century clock, today bell tower.
One day in the 13th century, with a view of the valley.

Neo-Gothic castle on an artificial platform supported by a large bastion, surrounded by a forest with winding paths, built on the former farm of Diego Martelli: it was wanted since 1889 by Baron Fausto Lazzaro Patrone, then passed to the Birindelli and in 1938 to Count Ugo Pasquini; since 1979 it is of the Municipality and is managed by the Armunia Foundation as a center of culture.
Gorge of the Molassa stream visible from the road between Barcis and Andreis, part of the Forra del Cellina Nature Reserve; you can explore with the Valcellina Train, currently not in service.
The breach of 1870.
It preserves a 12-log organ built in 1864 by the Pavese organaro Luigi Lingiardi and the instruments of the Passion of Christ used in the traditional ceremony of the Entierro.
Exhibitions for a fee, price according to the exhibition (eg. €16 full, €14 reduced to beginning 2026)
Fishing village next to Egnazia.

Cycle track on the old provincial railway track, inaugurated in October 2000 as part of the Modena-Vignola route through Castelnuovo Rangone, Spilamberto and Castelvetro, with plates of texts by Kerouac at the former tollgates. Since June 1998, parks, bikes and historic center have hosted 22 glass bulletin boards with poetry, pages of novels, songs, letters and diaries.
The seventeenth-century Capuchin monastery.
building in serious state of degradation and abandonment since the 1970s (FAI)
Behind a sober façade is the acese church with the largest frescoed surface, with a terrace overlooking the Ionian Sea.

In the hamlet of Serrano the parish church of San Giorgio Martire, probably fourteenth century and rebuilt in the second nineteenth century, the monument to the fallen with San Giorgio on horseback by Francesco Oronzo De Vitis and Palazzo Lubelli, residence of the barons; in Stigliano the chapel with cross of Santa Marina, of 1762, with below frescoed rock crypt.

On the remains of a early Christian basilica, then church of a female Benedictine monastery: the mosaic floor in situ, mosaics of a second basilica and a collection of funerary stems of the IV-V century, visible also from above.
Church of the XVII century consecrated in 1614 by Pier Francesco Ubertini; the bell tower with the clock is of the mid-nineteenth century.
A treasure of sacred art popular on four floors.

In the upper part of the village, it is indicated among the oldest sacred buildings of Varesotto. Leggiuno is the first place to know a document with the term "plebs": at least since 846 it was the seat of the Pieve di Santo Stefano, a role maintained until 1965.
The largest collection of dolls in Europe, inside a castle.
A bath in the summer waterfall.
The secret cloister.

Lake about 1,080 m was born over two thousand years ago by the sinking of a karst doline (on the bottom of logs dated to 210 BC), of about 64,000 m2 and 17 m of depth, bathing and several times Blue Flag; half of the Central European aristocracy between the eight and twentieth centuries, it stayed there several times Sigmund Freud. Ring of about 30 minutes suitable for strollers, the Freud Path from the village and two equipped beaches (Bertoldi and Marzari) in summer.

The parish church of the historic centre, whose foundation dates back to 1246 for an inscription on a stone of the bell tower. It was banned in 1851 for its poor condition and was restored for about twenty years and reopened before 1870; damaged by a fire on August 16, 1891, it was reconsecrated on May 14, 1896. It has three naves with vaulted barrels lunetted in the central nave, stone portal with bezel and oculus, and a square bell tower in three orders with cusp.
In Piazza Castello, dates back to the first half of the 6th century BC and is among the oldest in Magna Grecia; destroyed in 209 BC, it is called popularly Poseidon Temple.

Hills and vineyards of Montepulciano give Rosso Conero, to be tasted from cellar to cellar; the Festa del Rosso Conero is held the first week of September with refreshment points, stalls, street games and tastings, and in summer they organize tastings also in the caves.
In the seventeenth century Palazzo Martinetti, born in the seventies of the twentieth century thanks to the donations of contemporary artists and works from churches and convents.
The ancient walls designed in the sixteenth century to protect the city, to be walked in a beautiful walk, embraced by the waters of the Sile and the canals.
He's been telling the story of the woman for the last 200 years.
The works of the illustrator who gave the colors to Pinocchio.
A 13th-century fortress overlooking the valley, with mighty walls, a 24-metre-high mast and a polygonal tower with Guelph merlons. The Park of the Fortress hosts the Night of Mysteries (18 August).
The works and masks made of mache by the artist from Cotignolese, in his home laboratory.
Benedictine Abbey documented since 1029, consecrated in 1253, with the facade completed in 1268.
Monument to the statesman born in Maglie, located in front of the house of his family.
Two walled villages on the Valconca; in Trarivi the ancient parish church has become Museum of the Eastern Gothic Line - Church of Peace, and in Valliano there is a small ethnographic museum.
Understand how Rome designed the Padua countryside.
The large natural park between Pisa and the sea, one of the ideas to discover the less known side of the city.
Church dated 1572 on Romanesque foundations, renovated in Baroque age; next to the medieval house of the fourteenth century.
Urban park near the sea with kiosks, rides, children's areas and the swan pond.
The Baroque façade of the Duomo.

Three free beaches on the eastern branch of Lake Como: Pradello, with grassy shore and ample parking five minutes from the station; Park Church Rotta, with bar, cabins, deckchairs and services, accessible to people with disabilities; Poncia, small green beach with cabins and showers.
It is the center of the small old town and houses the altarpiece depicting the Madonna delle Grazie.

Ring of 10 km, about 3 hours, hiking difficulty, from Piazzale Crosara between the districts of the ancient town of Azzarino: the stone cross of 1884 in Purga, the Gal Cross in ammonitic red at 1170 meters, the nineteenth century church of Contrada Campe, the sundial and the fresco of contrada Riva, the 'barbari volti' fifteenth century contrada Cross and the barn of Ballarin with San Giorgio and the dragon in contrada Fontani.
To understand how the land of the delta was born.

Borgo dell'Alto Monferrato mentioned since 1184 as "Lelma" ("Lelma"), a fief of Spinola from the 15th to the 17th century: on a spur above the stream Piota the fifteenth-century castle and the cottage, the parish church with the table of Barnaba da Modena, outside the village the Romanesque parish church of San Giovanni al Piano frescoed by the "Maestro di Lerma" and the sanctuary of the Rocchette on the salt road.
A late 15th century roundabout.
The 18th-century parish church with the classical nineteenth-century façade.
the Municipality warns that the Museum-Biblioteca is closed for works in progress

Etruscan site of steel production between the beginning of the 6th and the end of the 5th century BC, linked to Populonia and Vetulonia, where the hematite of Elba was worked: an industrial area with ovens and a housing; the land conserves slag, coal and cookware.
Late-Gothic frescoes in a country parish.
The temple where the Synod opens every year.
Outside the walls of the Garden of Ninfa, it reconstructs the original environment of the Paludi Pontine and hosts events next to the literary paths of Ninfa; it is open from October to May.

The village was born as Castrum Brachiani, quoted from 1234, with shell shape; the Orsini closed it with a new belt between 1470 and 1490, of which remains the bastion of the Belvedere della Sentinella overlooking the lake and countryside. Outside it brings the Palazzo della Comunità of 1619 to Piazza IV Novembre, still seat of the Municipality, and on Via Principe di Napoli the aqueduct wanted by Livio I Odescalchi.

Modern building with Romanesque-Gothic lines, designed by Napoleon Pagliarulo after the demolition in 1913 of the previous Baroque church and inaugurated in 1920. Under the canopy of the main altar the monolith with the Madonna Panagia, Byzantine fresco perhaps of the twelfth century repainted in the seventeenth century, that tradition wants found by a farmer in the district Bread; a large fresco of the counter-facade tells the discovery. Patron Festival on the last weekend of May with the race "currature" .

Country between Lake Garda and Lake Cavedine, inhabited already in prehistoric times, dominated by Castel Drena with a 25-metre-long mast overlooking the Marocche, expanses of boulders left by the post-glacial landslides. Around, a historic center of stone doors and alleys, the tiny village of Braila, the centuries-old chestnut groves with the park of sculptures Drena 3000, the ferrata of Rio Sallagoni and Malga Campo.

The thirteenth-century church rebuilt in neo-Renaissance style, with the baptismal font where according to tradition Leonardo was baptized on 16 April 1452 and the cycle of sculptures by Cecco Bonanotte on the History of Salvation (2010).

Founded in 1982 and managed by the Naturalia Cooperative, it has sections of paleontology and paleoanthropology (vegetable and animal fossils even millions of years), entomology, herpetology and ornithology (with live animals), mineralogy and malacology, mammology, embryology and teratology, as well as aquariums and terrariums. Inside the Provincial Fauna Observatory recovers and rehabilitates injured wild animals, including sea turtles and raptors. Hours: Tuesday-Friday 9-13 and 15-17, Saturday and Sunday 10-17, Monday closed.
The medieval heart of Soave at a slow pace.
The ramps where Alfredo Binda was training.
Built between 1603 and 1608 by the Doria family, it includes church, cloister, tower of defense and princely palace.
A noble estate of the expansive courtyard, a jewel of rural architecture along the cycle path towards Bondeno.
A Romanesque hermitage at the top of an off volcano.
High granite mountain for experienced hikers.

At the end of the eighteenth century, the Strassoldo family built the village of Colmello di Grotta as a residence and a place of work for about ten families of settlers, who lived there until the early sixties of the twentieth century; restored by the municipality, the complex has been a museum since 1993. It reconstructs kitchen, bedroom, cellar and stable, blacksmith shops, carpenters, casket, carraio and shoemaker, the cycle of vine and corn, the breeding of silkworms, the birth of rural coffers and popular religiosity. Open on request.

Borgo arbëreshë 450 meters in the Pollino National Park, inside the Raganello Gorges Reserve, repopulated by Albanian refugees at the end of the fifteenth century: comignoli and speaking houses Kodra, churches of Byzantine rite, the ethnic museum and the Devil's Bridge on the Raganello.
A small museum in the birthplace of the artist.

Established in 2005, it brings together the sites of Serabine I, II and III, the Horn of Serabine and Bedolina, two areas at about 100 meters of elevation gain connected by an ancient ridge path. The engravings are in much of the age of the final Bronze and Iron; on the plateau of Bedolina there are the topographic maps, with the famous Map of Bedolina. Admission fee; in summer open every day except on Thursdays, in winter Saturdays and Sundays; for Bedolina the keys are withdrawn at the ticket office.

In the heart of the Roman grateful north-east of Padua, Borgoricco has in the civic center designed by Aldo Rossi its symbolic place, with the theater and the Museum of the Roman Centuration; in the territory, the eighteenth-century parish church of San Leonardo, the ancient parish church of Sant'Eufemia and the oratory of San Nicolò a Favariego, built in part with Roman material.

Opened in 1998 in a former elementary school in the historic center: the first room reconstructs the ecosystem of the lake with fossil finds and pictures of the Reserve in the four seasons; agricultural and fishing gear, including the
A thousand years of city history in one building.

The sanctuary, called Sancta Maria ad Nives, houses the table of the Madonna della Neve (145 x 108 cm), attributed to an anonymous southern painter of the 16th century Raffaellesque school, inspired by the Little Holy Family of Raphael of the Louvre. On the site of the ancient mother church, destroyed by the earthquake of September 8, 1905, stands a small church of Our Lady of Lourdes, behind which a small road leads to the rock settlement. Wheelchair accessible.

The sunset on the gulf from the promenade.
The tower and the treasures of the lost church.
The Calabrian baroque in tuff.
Bathrooms and water sports on the Garda.

In the former Mulino Spagolla sul Brenta, inaugurated in 2002 and expanded in 2005: windows, relics, photographs and dioramas tell the war on the front and the life of the communities, with the uniform of the Austro-Hungarian aviator Josef Kiss and the memorabilia of General Gabriele Nasci; the second section reconstructs an Austro-Hungarian trenches and an Italian gallery and displays medals of both armies.

On the banks of the Tirso, in Caddas, Traiano had the main Roman thermal complex built on the edge of the Forum Traiani market, exploiting a spring that flows at about 54 °C, already sacred in pre-Nuragic and nuragic times. You can visit the large rectangular tub of the tepidarium, once turned into a barrel and porch, the lateral collection tanks, the nymph with niches for statues and ex-vote, and a second circuit with calidaria, frigidarium and changing rooms; in the area also two statues of the god Bes. Dismantled in part in the Middle Ages to build churches and convents.

In Villa Guerrazzi, known as "La Cinquantina" (the Fiftyth century building), opened in 1980 and re-assembled in 2003: it tells the Lower Val di Cecina from the Paleolithic to the Roman villas, with the Montescudaio cinerary (VIII-VII century BC), the princely set of Casale Marittimo, the jewelry of Belora and, in the garden, the Etruscan tomb of Casaglia rebuilt.
The sculptor Mastroianni at his house.
The memory of the massacre.

The Gothic castle.
The Romanesque Benedictine of Assisi.
The room attached to the Olympic Theatre that hosts meetings and conferences of the cultural program.

The porcelain museum founded by Carlo Ginori in 1737.

A Benedictine church of the 12th century, where in the 16th century the Vitelli founded the Confraternity of the Blessed Sacrament, entrusted in 1577 to the Roman basilica of Santa Maria sopra Minerva; from here comes the Last Supper of Calvaert today in the Collegiate.

Built in the second half of the fifteenth century on the site of a source considered miraculous, Gothic with Renaissance portal in terracotta: in the crypt a seventeenth-century tub still guards the source under the image of the Madonna del latte; frescoes from the fifteenth to the seventeenth century, including a cycle of Giovanna d'Arco of the Pesenti brothers of Sabbioneta, and in the second left chapel the funerary stele of Parmigianino, died in Casalmaggiore in 1540. It is reached on foot in about half an hour along a tree-lined avenue.
Medieval complex built by the Knights of Malta, with the Round and the archaeological museum.

Country of the plain of Cuneo dominated by the Castle of Solaro, fortress thirteenth century of the Marquises of Saluzzo then of the counts Solaro, today seat of the Town Hall, next to the great parish of Saints Peter and Paul in modern Baroque style, inaugurated in 1904.
The monumental scene of the sanctuary.
Wall sections in polygonal work in the place Leveta, probably built by Equi.
Baroque church in the oldest nucleus, with the mosaic church of Ligurian pebbles and a rose of the winds.

Medieval village between the Cimini Mountains and the Tiber, with artificial caves, Etruscan tombs and walls dug in the cliffs, grown along the Amerina street of which today is a stop of the Way: it dominates the Castle Orsini and the Romanesque Santa Maria Assunta, and with Civita Castellana is the most famous center of Tuscia for ceramics, told in the museum of Palazzo Celestini.
A good starting point.

Founded between the 5th and 6th centuries, it has a basilica plant similar to the large churches of Ravenna and 18th century interior; in the crypt a 6th century sarcophagus, indicated as the largest of the Marches, with Christian symbols, crosses, laurel crowns and two peacocks.

Thematic path for families partly dirt and easy to cross, starting from via Cossano Belbo: panoramas on vineyards, hazelnuts and woods, installations such as "Bice la frona felice" (the happy frog), "Fruteto Magico," the Fairy Terraces of Gnomo Rob (locality Navirotto) and the Tree of the vine, the painted Cisterna, thematic alleys with tiles and painted antinas, 16 points linked to the work of Fenoglio and a path of meridians and frescoes of Tore Milano. It can be used with pushchairs, not entirely in wheelchairs; recommended from spring to autumn.
The great Marian sanctuary of South Tyrol, among woods and meadows.

Insect of turquoise water and white sand halfway between Palau and Santa Teresa Gallura, at the mouth of the Liscia, connected by a tongue of sand to the Isle of Gabbiani (Isuledda), natural area of about 18 hectares with dunes of lavender, lentisco and juniper. Very windy, it is a reference for windsurfing, kitesurfing and sailing with international competitions; low backdrop, parking also for campers, accessible to people with disabilities.
Lake Iseo from above.

Fortress built by Celano from 1392 at the behest of the counts, enlarged in 1451 by Leonello Acclozamora (noble floor and four corner towers) and completed as residence by Antonio Todeschini Piccolomini, grandson of Pius II, Count of Celano since 1463; it has a central court with well and loggia portico. Damaged by the earthquake of 1915 and rebuilt until 1960, since 1992 it houses the Museum of Sacred Art of Marsica, eight rooms of paintings, sculptures and goldsmiths from the 6th to the 18th century (two wooden doors carved from the 12th century, the triptych of Alba Fucens, the cross Orsini of 1334), and the Torlonia Collection with the findings emerged from the drying up of the Fucino, including a relief of the 2nd century A.D. with a city and its territory. Open from Tuesday to Sunday 9:30-18:30, closed on Mondays.
Listen one by one to the four voices of the tenor.
The chapel that houses the Sailing Christ by Giuseppe Sanmartino, carved in 1753 in a single block of marble.
The majolica dome.
The view of the Tyrrhenian Sea from above.
The castle founded by Frederick II of Swabia in the 13th century, now home to the rich Civic Museum of the city.

Founded in 1750 by architect Giulio Galliori, the works stopped in 1768 due to lack of funds and ended in 1783, date engraved on the choir; the façade, which had to be covered with stuccoes and marbles, remained unfinished. A unique nave with three chapels on each side, dome at the crossroads and interior entirely frescoed in the style of Lombard Rococo illusionism; in the apse a neoclassical circular marble temple with six Corinthian columns above the main altar.

Borgo dei ora nell'Ascolano, where for over half a millennium the caldera have worked copper: in the Palazzo Canestrari are located the Museum of sacred art and, in the underground, the Ramai Museum; in the village the Collegiata di San Paolo, the sixteenth-century loggia of the Palazzo del Priorato and, at Christmas, the mechanized crib in the caves of San Francesco.

Opened in 1976 and transferred to the former hospital of the SS complex. Annunziata (1355): Roman finds of the II-III century A.D. and medieval (ceramics, glass, Arab majolica, tombstones), the crowds of the duchy of Gaeta (X-XII century) and a gallery from the XII to XVIII century with separate frescoes of Saint Lucia and works of Luca Giordano, Sebastiano Conca, Giovanni da Gaeta, Beinaschi and Paolo De Matteis; also exhibited the Standard of the battle of Lepanto attributed to Girolamo Siciolante. MiC timetables: every day 16:30-19.
The canal that led to Bologna.
Archaeological area with the remains of the latepublic walls.

Country at the foot of the Matese Molisano, where Palazzo Rogati hosts the permanent artistic nativity scene created in 1961 by the Barcelonaese Juan Marì Oliva and a paleontological exhibition with fossils of the Cretaceous, photos and local memories and a section dedicated to zampogna; on the hill of the medieval village stands the parish church of San Pietro in Vincoli with the circular bell tower.
Included in the ticket of the Ceramic Museum
A village that stood still in the sixteenth century.
The seventeenth-century baroque of the village.
The stone pastures of the shepherds.

It rises on the ruins of the Constantinian basilica and is dedicated to St. John the Baptist and St. Pancrazio; behind the façade of 1772 by Carlo Buratti a crypt preserves columns and capitals of the original early Christian basilica. Current appearance since 1913.
Two Ferrara painters in a small village.

Country of about a thousand inhabitants of Sarcidano, on the right bank of the Flumendosa and overlooking the lake: the nuragic complex of Adoni on a relief near the town and a center with arch of Roman times, the Gothic-Aragonese parish of San Giuliano and the murals of Pinuccio Sciola.
It rises in the area of the ancient feud of Lupara, strategic node of the Tratturo Ateleta-Biferno, one of the routes that led the shepherds from Abruzzo to Puglia through Molise.
The city of oil under the streets.
A new city of the 1930s remained as it was.
The theatre built in 1740 on a project by Antonio Cugini, rebuilt after the fire of 1851, with the dome painted by Anselmo Govi in 1927.
The house where the author of the Gioconda was born, with his pianos.
The emperor's water cave on the sea.
In Palazzo Vitari, a permanent collection of Otto e Novecento dedicated to Calabria and the South, with an archive of works, posters, catalogues, photographs and videos.

Erected from the thirteenth century on the ruins of a fortification more ancient and enlarged over the centuries, it dominates the promontory and the medieval district, which surrounds with its walls.

In the historic centre, in the ancient seat of a monastery of hermits, a small group of lightning stars built on the ruins of the church of Santo Stefano; here the icon of Santa Maria delle Grazie was found, today in the homonymous sanctuary just outside the village. It houses the Town Hall and the Carabinieri barracks.

Above Crevenna, a 15th-16th century complex enlarged in the 16th century by the Capuchin friars, with a chapel linked to San Carlo Borromeo, frescoes by Michelino da Besozzo and others, a cloister from the late 15th to early 16th century and a avenue of cypresses. Continuing on foot towards the ...Crus Pisina the mule track is steep up to the Sasso Erba, rock gym, then easier; in the wood before the viewpoint there are picnic tables and a barbecue, and next to the cross a small altar and a large bell on iron structure.

It preserves a large wooden altar of the seventeenth century; there were found tombs of the sixth-sixth century. The Boyls donated the litter used for the statue of Jesus in the ritual of the Holy Week of S'Icravamentu.
A small ancient world dedicated to the Salame di Varzi.
Baroque on a Romanesque portal.
The backstage of the frescoes.
The Veneranda Biblioteca Ambrosiana with the Codex Atlanticus of Leonardo and the Pinacoteca with its Portrait of music.
The 31 km cycle path connecting Vicenza to Padua along the Bacchiglione river.
Anatomical waxes, unique in the world.
The view of the village suspended on the arches.
frescoes of the fifteenth and sixteenth centuries.
The largest coastal tower, guarding the port.

About 1,100 hectares long 8 km of coast between Fasano and Ostuni, from Torre Canne to Torre San Leonardo: posidonia prairies, juniper dunes with specimens of 500-600 years, paleodune, humid areas retrodunal like the Morelli River and age-old olive groves with underground mills along the Via Traiana. La Casa del Parco, in a former railway station, rents bikes; bike and walking tours by reservation.

Romanesque basilica of early medieval origin on the promontory above the port, with the remains of the walls and the protohistoric casteliers of Muggia Vecchia and Santa Barbara; wide panorama of the Gulf of Trieste.

The best preserved fortified village of Friuli Venezia Giulia, a national monument since 1965, rebuilt for anastyles after the earthquake of 1976: Gothic cathedral consecrated in 1338, 14th century walls with moat, the chapel of San Michele with the mummies and museums of Palazzo Orgnani Martina.
The Romanesque church and the rare eight-sided cemetery.
not open to the public, visit by reservation through the Museo dell'Agro Veientano (Italy.it)
The best view of the old town starts from the pier near the port.
The symbol of the country.

Remains of the "Castrum Sancti Dometrij" in villa Sancti Joannis is mentioned in a document from the first decades of the fourteenth century, on a rocky spur where around 1100 was built the first church of St. John. The 100-metre-long trapezoidal belt has an entrance ramp and three lines of walls towards the Valley of Hell, while seven lines of step walls protect a mule track.

Inaugurated in September 2001, it occupies three rooms in the center of the village of Bestagno: two ancient communal ovens, where bread was cooked throughout the country, and a cellar. One oven is set up as it was originally, the other collects tools for the cultivation of olive and vine with their dialect names; in the cellar more recent objects like an old projector and a turntable. The findings were collected by the parish priest Don Ramoino and given in comodato to the Municipality in 1997; the DMO cites it as a parish museum with ancient sacred art and everyday objects. Tel. 0183 279026.

Church at the intersection between Via Sant'Afra and the road to Nigoline, next to Palazzo Barboglio: traces of a building probably not after the fifteenth century, but was rebuilt in the current forms in 1707 by Giuseppe Barboglio and brothers. The Porta Livorno, an ancient entrance of the port recently brought to light, is flanked by the statue of the samurai Hasekura Tsunenaga, which in November 1615 brought to the pope a proposal for a trade agreement between Japan and Mexico.

Set up by the Oppelide Foundation in the 14th-century palace opposite the Fortress, it exhibits fossils and minerals that illustrate the evolution of life through geological ages, coming from the Elce valley and from various countries even outside Europe; many specimens are rare or unique.

Medieval fortified village, once closed by walls that made it impregnable, the point of arrival of the Via Francesca. The ruins of the pentagonal tower, one third of the original, remain in the fortress; the church of Saints Christopher and Jacopo is Romanesque, renovated and enlarged in the eighteenth century, with portico of the early nineteenth century. It can be reached with 2.1 km of asphalt road from the SS64 in the locality Bellavalle.

The octagonal square of 1600 at the intersection of Via Maqueda and Cassaro, with the allegories of the seasons, the Spanish kings and the patron saints; called Teatro del Sole because one side is always in the sun.
At sunset, with the Gregorian songs of the monks of San Miniato.

Borgo dell'Alto Casertano along the river Lete: the medieval fortified village of Prata Inferiore is dominated by the castle of the Pando, today a cultural hub with the historical military museum and the museum of peasant civilization.
The city's mother church, reborn after the destruction of 1918.
The seventeenth-century church of the capital.
The mountain at whose feet Boves stands, with walks in the woods and more challenging routes on foot or by bike, including a bike park for the descent.
A unique Romanesque jewel in Sardinia.
WWF oasis of 15,000 m2 on the border with the territory of Saluzzo, rich in trees and vegetation and frequented by numerous species of birds.

Castagno with three stems of an estimated age over 3000 years, 19.42 m tall and with a circumference of 10.51 m, considered the oldest known; according to tradition, Queen Joan of Aragon recovered with her knights during a storm, and Goethe and other travelers described it. In 2021 he was one of the Italian finalists of the contest        \ Tree of the year Â Â; not far away is the great Castagno della Nave.

In the 13th-century Romanesque tower of Castel Thurn, annexed to the current town hall, former residence and seat of judicial hearings around 1341, passed to the Municipality in 1911 that restored and opened it to the public. It exhibits sacred art: ancient altarpieces and consecrated tables of the sixteenth century, statues of saints of the first Baroque and religious paintings that tell the history of the Val d'Ega.
A stop on the path of Medici villas.
The lighthouse on the head at the extreme south of Ionic Calabria.
The anti-corsar tower overlooking the Tyrrhenian Sea.
The symbol of Conversano.
Ancient bridge built by the Romans in the first century BC
Inaugurated in 1995 at the foot of the Parioli Mountains, one of the largest on the continent.
The best preserved Occitan Alpine architecture in the valley.
Very clear water among granites in altitude.

Parish built in the 15th century on a previous Romanesque church and renovated in the Baroque period. On the wall opposite the side door, above an architrave dated 1470 with the Agnus Dei, opens a Gothic window with sharp arch; inside the polyptych of Agostino Casanova painted around 1540.
Boccaccio is buried here.

Symbol of Teglio, on a hill south of the village among the pine trees: it is what remains of a medieval castle built on the ruins of a previous Roman foundation, with square plan with slits and raised access. From its position it dominates the Valtellina; the interior is visited with guides only in some periods of the year, by reservation at the Infopoint in Teglio.

It was founded in the 12th century as a fortified outpost of the bishops of Albenga, it was of the Fieschi from 1505 to 1547 and between the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries took the form of a Renaissance palace; in 1736 it passed to the Kingdom of Sardinia.
Orange Flag town at the gates of the valley, where the arch of Augustus, the amphitheatre and Porta Savoia tell the Roman follow and the castle of the Countess Adelaide dominates the village.
The cathedral with the large dome, the fourth in Italy in size after San Pietro, the Pantheon and Santa Maria del Fiore; Leonardo da Vinci contributed to the project.
Small oratory in Piazzetta Ruggero VII, recognizable from the sailing bell tower.
Baths and mosaics of a first century Roman villa.
Borgo Bandiera Arancione dell'alta Valle Gesso in the Natural Park of the Maritime Alps, with the first center of the Italian Alps dedicated to the wolf and the great alpine lakes.
The oil told inside a medieval farm.
For a day of relaxation.
The viewpoint of the village among holm oaks, springs and nuraghi.
site indicated as not visitable and temporarily closed (Trentino Culture)

Sacred area of about 740 m2 fenced by large blocks of stone, in panoramic position on the valley of the Fiumarello and close to the tratturo Castel di Sangro-Lucera: a small temple flanked by two colonnaded arcades, of which remains the high podium with molded frames and the cell with floor in cottage and white tiles. The coins under the cell (the most recent one denarius of 104 B.C.) date from the construction; the lamps attest to the use at least until the second century AD. Discovered in the 1990s, it is still the subject of excavations by the University of Leiden and Wisdom with the Superintendence of Molise.

The fifteenth-century church in the old village, the first stage of the itinerary of the historic centre; it preserves a seventeenth-century wooden altar by Giovanni Battista Polana di Roncone, purchased by the parish in the second half of the eighteenth century.
The mother church overlooking the city.
Swordfish feluches.
The gates of the medieval castle.
The square of the "Balcony of the Romagna," with the Column of hospitality: the noble families tied the horse to the ring and fought the guest.
In the upper Tanaro Valley, towards Liguria, the four historic villages of Garessio and, in Val Casotto, the hunting palace of the Savoy born from an ancient Carthusian, UNESCO World Heritage.
The minor churches of the Greek village.

Municipality of the Sirente-Velino Park with the hamlets of Albe, Forme and Corona, where stands Alba Fucens, a Roman colony of 303 BC with hole, basilica, thermal baths and amphitheatre, dominated by the church of San Pietro obtained from a temple of Apollo.
