The look on the gulf.
A mountain village between Maiella and Monte Rotella.
What's left of the castle.

Built in 1363 by the Roeros and completely rebuilt by the Isnardi in 1647; it was plundered in 1544 by the imperial troops of the Marquis of Vasto and in 1691 the French of Catinat burned a branch of it. It has a round decorated tower, loggia, hall of honor, scenic portal and a large garden; inside frescoes and trompe-l'oeil, a tunnel, a well with wheel for water and prisons.
Built in the first half of the 14th century by Francesco I Ventimiglia, it dominates the village from the top and is an example of late medieval architecture, already the residence of the family.
The sixteenth-century palace of the Farnese.

House donated to the Municipality by the notary Giuseppe Cesarini (1895-1977) in the Palazzo Pergamini-Negri, with bourgeois furnishings of the Thirties-Quaranta (red living room, pink living room, dining room). Twenty-one rooms of ancient, modern and contemporary art with works by Giorgio Morandi, Gino Severini, Achille Funi, Marino Marini and Francesco Messina, and more than 60 paintings and graphics by Anselmo Bucci.

The nucleus from which the village was born: from the first tower with fence it passed to a rectangular castle, transformed in the sixteenth century from military structure to noble residence; in 1747 it counted 54 rooms and in 1753 there was annexed the church of St. Maria, in part transformed into a private chapel designed by Paolo Posi. He passed to Ceccano, Caetani, Aldobrandini, Ginnetti, Orsini and Doria Pamphilj, who in 1811 placed the stone coat of arms on the portal; the Municipality bought it around 1930. Today, with the clock bell tower, it houses the EtnoMuseum, the municipal library and the hostel "Il Tarlo Baronale."
The Italian Warrior at his home, and view of Rocca Calascio.

Cylindrical building at the foot of the hill of the convent, indicated by Feel Florence as the largest glacier in Europe; today it is waiting for restoration and can be seen from the outside along the CAI 00 path.
The Palazzo Comunale houses a collection of works by Carlo Maratti, a painter born in Camerano and remembered as one of the peaks of the seventeenth century.
The village life of the Fontanabuona and a rare book about Colombo.
A village of transhumance remained as it was.

A first church was attested in 1023; the fifteenth-century building was renovated from 1659 on a design by Gerolamo Quadrio and the façade was completed in the early twentieth century on a design by Virginio Muzio; since 1922 it is a minor basilica. Three naves with eight chapels: the pulpit (1711-1751) by Gian Battista Caniana with Andrea Fantoni has four tarpaulins in Carrara marble, the Chapel of the Octagonal Rosary (1679) houses the canvas "Agar" and "Ismaele" of Piccio, the altars painted by Piazzetta and Cignaroli and on the singing house a Serassi organ of 2242 reeds.
18th century plasters in a mountain hamlet.
From the lake to the Lagorai trails.
The illusion of Borromini.

It was born from the legacy of the surgeon Vescia, who collected the artifacts during his stays in the United States: donated by his wife in 1989, the collection of about 400 pieces was arranged by the Municipality in 1990 in the former nursery school of Cavona, and in 2020 it was enriched by the collection of Fabrizio Colonna from Alexandria. It exhibits exhibits of the pre-Columbian civilizations of New Mexico, Arizona and northern Mexico, Winchester rifles, Navajo capes and native American handicrafts, as well as vintage documents of the American Civil War. Free admission with optional free offer; tel. 0332 650107.
A medieval village still enclosed by its walls.
€5 full, €2 reduced; free on the first Sunday of the month; only electronic payments
Thermal plant with facade of 1914, recently renovated, offering thermal treatments with sulphurous waters.
The underground porch.
The garden where the botany was born.

Probably the Fortress Norsina already known around 952, takes its name from the sons of Tederigo, vassals of the Aldobrandeschi (1239); it passed to Siena, to the Salimbeni in 1369 and in 1618 was a fief of the Malaspina. The village is camouflaged between large boulders of riolite, 'i bossi', with arched door, alleys, arches and stairs; the remains of the casero near the Clock Tower, the wash-houses of the early twentieth century and, outside the center, the liberty Villa del Paradiso.
The protected area close to the city, suitable for outdoor activities.
the Scabec tab indicates it temporarily closed until new provisions

Founded in 1499, commissioned according to the tradition by Pope Julius II, it was enlarged with side chapels and in the second quarter of the nineteenth century assumed the neoclassical structure of the façade. Inside the altarpiece of the Crucifixion and sixteenth-century frescoes by Bernardino Campi coming from the oratory of the castle (commissioned by the Carthusians in 1576, the oratory was demolished in 1836) and fifteenth-century cibories in the presbytery.
Neolithic tombs dug into a single granite mass.
Pastor crosses and views of the Alpone Valley.
A post-war shrine in Boario.
The shape of the city fortress of the upper Tronto.

Itinerary of 10.1 km (about 4 hours and 45, 1,403 meters of climb) from Lungiarü to the valley of the mills to the refuge Genoa (about 3 hours and 30), with alpine meadows and views of the Odle and the Zillertal Alps, and for the path 4B from the Fork of Putia to the top of the Sass de Putia at 2.818 meters, with summit cross and panorama of the Dolomites. The last stretch is equipped: for experienced hikers and without vertigo, the set of ferrata is recommended.
A hamlet chapel.
Tratto della via delle Gallie built between 31 and 25 B.C.
The facade of 22 meters.
The sanctuary of the Queen of the Po, linked to the memory of the flood of the river.
The English botanist's museum.
The first temple of Akragas.

The municipality of the plain of Sibari: the archaeological park where Sibari, Thurii and Copia overlap, the museum of the "Toro cosante" (cooking toro), the prehistoric caves of Sant'Angelo and the historic center between the castle and the Stone of San Marco.
The oldest face in the center.
The city of majolica: the International Museum of Ceramics, the arcade squares and neoclassical palaces.
The Town Hall with important archive documents and stone houses of the Podestà, the Rabbi and Santa Rosa, exiles here in 1250.

Built in the first century BC to supply Formiae, the fish ponds and villas of Cicero and Mamurra, more than 10 meters below the village of Castellone: about 1,200 m2 and 7,000 m3 of capacity, four naves divided by 60 pillars about 6.5 meters high with pseudo-cruise vaults, from which the nickname of underground Basilica was identified with precision in 1860 by Pasquale Mattej, it was probably model for the Mirable Pool of Bacoli.

Fortified village born in the 11th century as a castle-house, a simple defensive belt, and still closed by walls Guelfe merlate (XII-XIV century) interrupted by towers; you enter from the large portal next to the bell tower, between paved alleys of river pebbles and rustic houses. The tower houses a photographic collection on the nature reserve surrounding the village and contemporary art exhibitions.

Country of the Vercellian plain that took its name from Galileo Ferraris, the 'father of the three-phase current', remembered by the museum in the family house and by the monument in the square; to see also the eighteenth-century parish church of San Lorenzo, the medieval tower, the archaeological museum MAVO with the Roman necropolis and the temple church of Santa Maria d'Isana.

About 10,500 hectares in the Gargano National Park, between Vieste, Vico del Gargano and Monte Sant'Angelo, UNESCO natural heritage since 2017 according to Italia.it: firs, oaks and beech trees, more than 200 animal species, trails of various difficulties, the Umbrian Lake and 25 picnic areas.

On a height at 334 meters, about 40 hectares in two areas joined by a saddle, dominating the Coseries stream: the site was inhabited by the Enotri in the IX-VIII century B.C. (necropolis in the nearby Piano Agritto) and in the IV-III century B.C. by the Brettii, who built a fortified settlement of strong Greek influence, recognized with excavations of the 1950s. The walls with towers, gates and walkways remain and the monumental East Gate, among the best examples of Hellenistic architecture of Magna Grecia, the theater is dug in the rock, the long wall is , houses and the urban system with plateau and stenopoi.
At the entrance of the village, with altar and frescoes.
A perched village, inserted by the regional portal among the historical villages: in the Middle Ages its position in the high hills allowed to alarm and protect Muccia.
Baroque architecture completed in 1732, with Greek cross, with stuccoes by Antonio Trentanove and the Transit of St. Joseph by Antonio Zanchi.

Founded in 2006, it tells of the tradition of stone processing in the country, where in the eighteenth century a school of stonemasons was born and where the stonemasons still work. It exhibits prehistoric finds of Alto Molise, inhabited already in the lower Paleolithic and Neolithic, including jewels and idols collected by the spouses Pietro Patriarch and Fortuna Ciavolino, who dedicated it to his nephew Chiara Marinelli, who disappeared young, and a handcrafted crib of polished stones.
The oldest Sondrio.
The most important of the churches of the village, in the historic center together with the church of the Rosary and the mother church.
A Visconti castle still inhabited, with collections that are not expected.

The most important element of the park is one of the major karst formations in Italy, with about 30 km of galleries. In Costacciaro are located the School of Speleology and the National Center of Speleology, in the former Clarisse monastery, and the Didactic Village linked to the speleological Hiking Centre; among the experiences proposed the crossing of the cave.
17th century church in popular baroque style; the saint is celebrated in May and October with a procession in which the faithful cross a river bringing the statue to the sound of the launeddas.
The two medieval bridges.

Small stone building on two floors of the early nineteenth century, home of the Vellini family, arrived from Piedmont in the mid-nineteenth century, and since 1928 artisan workshop: subjectic with the frame to iron the animals, courtyard with the sandstone moles, forge with mantice, forge and anvils; on the first floor the work of the blacksmith and the history of the family.
The small town of artists.

Comital castle with stone cores among the oldest in the country and parts of the XV-XVI century, rebuilt in neoclassical style by architect Francesco Valentini in the second half of the nineteenth century.

Borgo on the Varesina shore of Lake Maggiore, among the first towns of Verbano, divided by the river Giona in Borgo Inferiore and Superiore; thirteenth-century plant with the Imperial Tower, the Mandelli Castle, the Madonna della Punta on the promontory and the Parisi Valle Civic Museum on the lakefront.

Hills, vineyards and Ivrea Naviglio on foot or by bike.
Frescoes in the castle varanesco.
Coastal nature in the Circeo.
Church on the road to Piobbico and the Passo di Bocca Serriola, with frescoes from the fourteenth century under the loggia.
Wild valley closed by the Beauregard dam, where wool drags are still woven on wooden frames.
Carbide lamps, trolleys, helmets, picks and mine phones.
Three thousand years of Bari history.
Vittoria is linked to the only DOCG on the island, the Cerasuolo di Vittoria, the grapes of Nero d'Avola and Frappato; the wineries of the territory are visited to know the vinification.
The oldest church in the country, partly in the rock.
Art, archaeology and industrial archaeology together.

Dedicated to a Spanish martyr, it is the centerpiece of the most heartfelt festivals in the country, celebrated twice a year, Monday and Tuesday after Easter and in mid-July, with processions, singing in Sardinian and distribution of the blessed basil.
Romanesque captains on a cliff above the valley.
The sea of Campobello.
entrance by car and motorbike with closed number from May to end of October
On the main square of the historic center, of Benedictine origin of the fourteenth century and several times restored.

Manierista palace, owned by the municipality, with courtyard with classical facades designed by the ducal architect Ercole Negri of Sanfront and Italian garden; in 1620 Prince Vittorio Amedeo of Savoia chose him as residence. It hosts temporary exhibitions and is connected to Palazzo Taffini through the courtyard.
The zigzaged diamond façade, a unique of the Salento Renaissance.
Inside the cathedral, masterpieces of sacred art.

The main shopping street, with cafés and about 250 shops in the village; towards the north the Ciàsa dei Pupe, a house frescoed with the faces of Leonardo da Vinci, Shakespeare and Dante, and near the Basilica, in the former inn Stella d'Oro, the Sibille fresco of the first half of the fifteenth century.
The place of the memory of the Martyrs.
In the ancient church of St. John, most likely the first cathedral of Asti, the museum of the works of the episcopal complex; you visit the crypt, the deepest point of the church.
A fourteenth-century terracotta portal.
The historic park of the city inhabited by peacocks, ducks and turtles of water, with fitness trails and a view of the old city, the port, the Poetto, the Molentargius and the Seven Brothers.
Our Lady of the Apennines miracles.
The country shrine between menhir and cumbessias.
Neogothic, rebuilt at the end of the nineteenth century on the remains of a seventeenth century chapel; feast on July 26.
Short walk with views of the valley.
Etruscan sarcophagi.
Panoramic path dedicated to the botanist born in the territory.

The village, which traditionally was born from the inhabitants of the ancient Marcellinum climbed on the hill, dominates the Vallo di Diano. Among the historical buildings the church of the Assumption of the early eighteenth century, the church of Sant'Andrea of the fourteenth century, Palazzo Cestari of the seventeenth century, Palazzo Gerbasio of the eighteenth century with stone portal and Palazzo Abatemarco of the second half of the nineteenth century.

The city of Promessi Sposi on the branch of Lake Como, between the Adda and the mountains: the bell tower of San Nicolò 96 meters high, Villa Manzoni, the village of Pescarenico, the Viscontea Tower and the Azzone Visconti Bridge.
The medieval bridge with an asymmetrical profile, with a large central arch and three minor arches, which legend wants built with the help of the devil.
Byzantine church in Bidda 'e Susu, where at the beginning of September is celebrated the most heartfelt feast of the country.
The tools and knowledge of the campaign.

The centre of the Tanagro valley rises on the ancient Volcei, with an archaeological heritage from the Neolithic to the late Roman era: the national museum in the former convent of the Hermits, the urban archaeological park between the streets of the center and the Norman castle with its mast.

Late-Imperial bridge collapsed in the earthquake of 1088 and rebuilt in the thirteenth century, on which stands the cathedral; in the basement a museum path tells the bridge and the first sanctuary of the Miraculum.
Tower by the sea.
Frederick II and the Peucezi in the same building.

Military complex of the 13th century, of the federician and angioin age: it is the monument that best tells the past of Lucera. The palace inside had no doors and housed one of the ticks of the kingdom; some underground passages have not yet been completely discovered. The MiC has allocated 3 million euros for restoration and enhancement.
The only access to the village is a long pedestrian bridge suspended over the calanchi.

Opened on 3 June 2009 in the former slaughterhouse and in the ancient communal wash-house, it combines didactic laboratory, geological and scientific museum with multimedia installations and interactive models on the energy of wind, water and oil, born from the oil wells of Ripi, among the first deposits discovered in Italy. The visit lasts about an hour (up to three for schools and groups) and can be completed with the oil field in Petroglie, a few kilometers away. Reservation required.

Labyrinth of paved alleys with river pebbles, stone houses with barrel vaults and about 800 portals carved by local stonemasons; in the Portella district there are traces of the Roman walls and, in the village, remains of medieval walls and towers.
The ancient fortified residence of the bishops, of 1091, with the Cathedral Museum and rare stratigraphic excavations.
A piece of the Middle Ages almost intact above the Garda.
The heart of the city inside the walls.

In the hamlet of San Matteo delle Chiaviche, in the golenal area, the plant built between 1920 and 1939 on a project by Piero Portaluppi collects the waters of a basin of about 32,000 hectares and, through the canals Navarolo, Ceriana and Fossola, pours them into the Oglio with a flow rate of about 53,000 liters per second; it is 182 meters long and rests on chestnut poles. It hosts the Centre for interpretation and documentation of the Viadana Ecomuseum, Commessaggio, Dosolo and Gazzuolo.
Secular chestnut groves of the Cimini Mountains.
The most heartfelt cult in the community.
The sea for families.
Sands and sunsets.
Church richly frescoed with medieval paintings.
Terracotta altars and an astronomical clock.

The villa of Moncucco, attributed to Giovanni Ruggeri and built in the first half of the eighteenth century on a land where there was a castle, has a U-shaped plan and a loggia of three arches on binated columns; from its park Paolo Andreani made in 1784 the first human flight in balloon. In the garden was rebuilt at the beginning of the nineteenth century the oratory of San Lucio, the Tempietto of Moncucco: Renaissance chapel of the first half of the sixteenth century coming from San Francesco in Lugano, carried stone after stone along the watercourses, with medallions in stone of Saltrio; in 1815-1816 Giocondo Albertolli added the Ionic pronao and the dome. The temple was restored between 1987 and 1994.
In the first dairy farm of the Valle d'Aosta, founded on 24 July 1853, with the original equipment and the phases of the production of cheese and butter.

House-museum wanted by the artist Salvatore Emblema in his hometown as a place of study and diffusion of contemporary art: about 600 m2 of interior spaces and a park of sculptures of about 3,000 m2, with the most significant works of the artist in rotation every six months. It is home to the general archive of Emblema, a museum of regional interest since 2009, and organizes educational workshops. MiC timetable: Tuesday-Friday 9-18.30, Saturday and Sunday 10-14, Monday closed (to be confirmed on tel. 081 8274081).
You can see the grave even when the original is closed.
The church of Gian Lorenzo Bernini built since 1658 for Alessandro VII Chigi and Cardinal Camillo Pamphilj.

The complex was built at the end of the thirteenth century in a shelter and documented since 1349; from 1431 it passed to Tizzoni, Facerio, Bossi, Natta, Nuvoloni, Striggi, Fassati and Bruschio and finally to the Cozios, Counts of Salabue, who transformed it into a residence of representation filling the moat. After 1935 the Davico had it modified by the architect Gianni Ricci and decorated by the Italian painters Alfredo Parachini and Vittorio Accornero, who around 1948 redesigned the hanging garden with geometric flower beds, bosso hedges, roses and a stone well. You can see it from the outside.
Housed in the nineteenth-century palace of the Court, it is divided into two sections dedicated to the archaeological history of the city and the territory.
A house in Nuceria with mosaics and frescoes.

The parish church in Piazza Sant'Ulrico, with Renaissance and Baroque elements and refined wooden sculptures, including the statue of St. Ulric of Ludwig Moroder and the altarpiece of the Adoration of the Magi by Josef Moroder-Lusenberg. The nineteenth-century neo-Gothic nave was dismantled in 1988 and replaced by an octagonal building.

City on the Gulf of the same name with the Norman Cathedral of San Bartolomeo and the late Roman villa with great mosaics; in the hamlet of Tindari the ancient Tyndaris with the Greek-Roman theater, the sanctuary of the Black Madonna and, at the foot of the head, the reserve of the Lakes of Marinello.

In front of the Duomo, founded in 1504 and enlarged in the eighteenth century: the octagonal church with double loggia was consecrated in 1531 and the monastic church annexed preserves late medieval and Renaissance frescoes; today it houses the Santa Chiara Postgraduate Institute.

The center of the Val Borbera is located around the seventeenth-century Palazzo Spinola, which houses the Museum of Resistance and Social Life and the Museum of Sacred Art, opposite the parish church of Sant'Antonio Abate and the seventeenth-century fountains.
The museum that tells the whole story of Salò.
The city of the Palio.
A 14th-century church in the center.

An abandoned village in the woods at the abbey, with a square tower, bastions and an ogival Gothic gate; the fortification dates back to 890 to defend the abbey from the Saracens and was strengthened in the fifteenth century and 1570.
A village collected with a Liberty theater.
The villa with the panoramic park on Tigullio.
Built between 1274 and 1295, with a Latin cross with three naves, dedicated to the patroness.
The solitary Romanesque ruin in the vineyards.

It is located in the former Dominican convent founded in 1465, annexed to the monumental church of San Domenico. Sixteen rooms exhibit works from the seventeenth to the twenty-first century, including works by Mattia and Gregorio Preti, and an important collection of Italian multimedia art from the mid-Twentieth century; from 2023 it is part of the National Museum System. Closed on Mondays; from Tuesday to Sunday 9.30-12.30 and 16-18 (October-March) or 16-19 (April-September).

The "Chiave delle Alpi" is 333 metres along the Mera at the confluence between Val Bregaglia and Val San Giacomo: a historic centre with elegant palaces, ollar stone fountains and via Dolzino, the Collegiate Church of San Lorenzo with the baptismal font of 1156 and the Peace of the Treasure Museum, the Parco del Paradiso and the Marmitte dei Giganti, and the crotti of Pratogiano.
A noble palace that incorporates a more ancient castle.
The scarecrow told in an old mill, suitable for children.
The large brackish lagoons of the Po Delta Park, with fishing houses and flamingos, to visit by boat or by bike on the banks.

The largest high altitude alpine pasture in Europe: 56 km2 between 1,630 and 2,350 meters, with about 350 km of trails. On the way to the reserve, private traffic is forbidden from 9 am to 5 pm: you can go up with the cable car from Siusi or by bus from Castelrotto.
Francis' bond with Gubbio.

Dedicated to the submersion of 1950 and to the fate of Curon Vecchia and Resia: it tells the trauma of the loss of homes and land and reconstruction with historical photographs, models, sacred objects and statues of the ancient churches and testimonies of peasant life; some rooms reproduce a traditional stube. In summer guided tours by reservation.
A medieval convent on the Roman road.

Upon the site of a synagogue after the expulsion of the Jewish community, it was consecrated in 1559; during the restorations of the nearby house of the archisinagogus a stone with the seven-armed candlepiece emerged. It preserves a fifteenth-century wooden crucifix of German school and a Callido organ with 472 reeds.
Tools, clothes and photographs of the life of farmers, shepherds and cavators of the territory.

In the historic centre, the ancient medieval village of Terravecchia can be reached through the Porta del Sole, an eighteenth-century gate considered the most remarkable architectural monument of Fara, or from the parish church of San Remigio; along the way you will find the old communal wash-house.
12th century frescoes in a rock crypt.
The noble palaces of the silk village above the Gulf of Squillace.
The view over the sea and lagoon from an 11th century tower.
The story of the village told in the House-Torre.
Medieval atmosphere and views of the hills.
View of the village and the Lanzo valley.

Borgo probably arose in the thirteenth century, with a castle of the Aldobrandeschi then became a monastery; from the sixteenth century it passed to the counts of Santa Fiora, which drew its current layout. Under the Lorraine, the public offices of Grosseto moved there in the summer (the extant). It preserves numerous medieval buildings and views of the countryside.
The Piazza dei Carraresi, lords of Padua from 1318 to 1405, with the church of San Clemente and the Palazzo del Capitanio with the Clock Tower.
from 13 December 2026 to 21 March 2027 closed on Sunday, guided tours only on Saturday
the MiC card (updated to March 2021) indicates the museum closed daily; contact the Municipality (tel. 0557991271)

13th century castle on a hill at 430 meters, in good condition, formed by two complexes: houses leaning against a church, defended by a rocky bastion and a large square tower, and a residential building with fireplace and frescoes of Lombardelli around a courtyard. Contested in the fourteenth century between Malcorini and Muffati and in the fifteenth century between Ladislao d'Angiò and Orvieto, he passed to the Valenti, the Avveduti and in 1816 to the Society of Jesus.

On a spur that controlled the roads between the Ovadese Oltregiogo and the Alexandrian plain; the nucleus is a circular tower of the XII-XIII century, long prison, with five rooms connected by a helical staircase in the wall and the graffiti of the prisoners. Transformed into a residence by the Trotti in the mid-15th century and passed in 1570 to the Grimaldi, it preserves the late eighteenth-century chapel with trompe-l'oeil and stuccoes and a garden of the mid eighteenth-century in three parts (Italian, romantic grove, secret garden of medicinal herbs) with a view over the valley of the Orba. Guided tours by the owners at 15 and 16.30 on some Sundays from April to October.

Borgo about 15 km from Parma along the Via Francigena, with in the center the Rocca dei Sanvitale of the thirteenth century, now Castello della Musica; in the south of the village the museum of the Voteval Bronze Age and in the village the museum of the printer Ferdinando Libassi.
Gateway to the historic center near the castle; the base of a stumped shoe suggests an angioin construction of the 13th-XIV century. It is one of the monumental properties of the Puglia Region.
The ancient city on the Pancrazio hill, along the banks of Crati, with narrow and winding alleys; since the last decades of the nineteenth century the new city has developed in the plain below.

Built by Ibleto di Challant just before 1390 on a cliff above the village, with a cubic plan that combines all functions in a single building; in the sixteenth century Count Renato adapted it to firearms.
The symbol of the city on the sea.
16th century frescoes of Pastura.
Chiaveghino's canvases.
The frescoes of Stabiae in a palace.
A surreal theatrical city next to a Franciscan monastery.
The view from the highest point.

Frazione along the state road between Castelnovo ne' Monti and Vetto, overlooking the Pietra di Bismantova: the church of San Lorenzo is mentioned in a document dated 1112 and the village preserves a majesty of 1642, the tower house of the Bazzoli and eighteenth-century buildings.
A historic oil mill to tell the oil of Sila Piccola.
The complete tour of the lake by bike.

Ancient foundation with buildings dating back to the 15th and 16th centuries (Piazza Meneghin, Via Campi Noga) and eighteenth-century houses with characteristic loggias facing the east; among the oldest remains the fountain \'d'Girun Â and a Celtic head walled in the facade of the parish house. Among the alleys, reachable only on foot, the monumental press "d'Armensc" dated 1809 and built with medieval technology; there is also the parish church of the Blessed Virgin of the Rosary.
The nineteenth-century town hall of Pallanza, with the portico of 32 pillars in pink granite of Baveno.
The behind the scenes of the oldest infiorata in Italy.
Palazzo eighteenth-century today seat of the Town Hall, with wrought iron balcony, porch in the inner courtyard and double ramp staircase; the council hall has frescoes from 1830 about.
It also turns in batana, with a free service of volunteers near the Treppanti.

Immediately south of the ancient city; a limited excavation identified its limits and at least two phases: probably built in the second century BC with at least two entrances (north and south), it was expanded and renovated between I and II century A.D. Like Pompeii's, it looks like it's got no basement. You can reach it from the exit Lake Tangenziale or by bus EAV 914 from Fuorigrotta.
Houses in stone and earth.

Ancient Castellum Pastina in the Ausoni Mountains, closed by a walls of about 650 meters with fifteen surviving towers; in addition to the village with the collegiate church of Santa Maria Maggiore and the Museum of peasant and olive civilization, is known for the Pastena Caves, open to the public since 1927 and among the major caving complexes of Italy.
A lake with an alpine look in the heart of Sardinia.
The most collected and medieval side of the city.
Protected area since 1980 in the hamlet of Mercurago, among peat bogs, pastures and woods; the Lagoni are part of the UNESCO heritage site as a prehistoric palafittic site of the Alps
Canova's Ebe is worth a visit on its own.
A village school of the late nineteenth century remained as it was.
The Passion of Laino between costumes and photos.
The most photographed arch of Cilento.

The center, with its ancient porticos, preserves the installation of the Gonzaga era, where you can read squares and civil and religious buildings of the fifteenth century; Petrarca stayed there in 1350. The church of San Giorgio, Baroque, preserves Romanesque elements including the apse.
The valley of granite and clear waters most loved in Lombardy.
Rooms frescoed by Siciolante and Paul Brill in the palace that designed the city.
The garden by the sea.
The crenellated tower of the 13th century that is part of the complex linked to the cathedral and medieval history of the city.

The square, once surrounded by gardens, was redesigned by Swiss architect Mario Botta; in the center stands the bell tower, 36 meters high. Around, the historic centre offers palaces, hidden courtyards between alleys and squares, decorated facades and stone portals, the Cathedral of Saints Peter and Paul, example of Baroque architecture with works by local artists, and the former Hospital designed by Rodolfo Vantini in the nineteenth century, today the municipal library.
Sanctuary built with its own hands by Don Lorenzo Dresco (1808-1878), the "priest stonemason"; it offers a wide view of the valley.
The alpine baroque on the way to Formazza.
To be seen from the outside during the tour of the center.
the MiC card indicates "Closed" every day of the week; contact the parish (0968 403720) before the visit
Contemporary art in the countryside.
The seventeenth-century sanctuary in the woods above the village.

Reachable from Porta Marina, it was rebuilt in 1679 on a Gothic church of the fourteenth century; it houses the tomb of the explorer Giacomo Costantino Beltrami, the fifteenth-century fresco of the Madonna della Colonna and, in the sacristy, a Decollation of St. John the Baptist and a Nativity.
The nucleus of the settlement arbëreshë preserves the surviving kalives, ancient stone houses with wooden roof and tiles.
Walls, walkways and panorama from the sea to the Sibillini.

Romanesque church with three naves, with four portico columns of ollar stone built between the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries and bell tower of 1597, once a civic tower; in the octagonal baptistery the Romanesque baptismal font of 1156. Inside paintings by Pietro Ligari (1738) and the Madonna with Child and Saint Anthony by Giuseppe Nuvolone (1657), which also frescoed the cupola of the chapel.

Rebuilt in Baroque style by the Brancaleoni in 1784 after an earthquake; it preserves the altarpiece of the Rest of the Holy Family during the escape to Egypt by Federico Barocci and statues of prophets and biblical characters attributed to Federico Brandani.
Renaissance frescoes reappeared from under the lime.
Stone alleys and terraces on the valley.

Renaissance style chapel covered with polychrome marbles, with the coats of arms of Carpi, Modena and Fiorano, in the church of Spezzano, where in 1929 the remains of the Risorgimento patriot were transferred condemned to hanging in 1831.
The viewpoint of the Fontanabuona, from the sea to the Alps.

Inaugurated on 3 October 1999 for the Jubilee of 2000 on 160 m2, it contains sacred furnishings and vestments of the parish where Giuseppe Sarto, future Pius X, was parish priest from 1867 to 1875: on the ground floor cups from the eighteenth to the twentieth century, including the golden cup with patena donated by Pius X in 1906, a 1754 piss, processional crosses of the seventeenth century, reliquaries, an 1867 monstrance and ex-vote; on the first floor vestments from the fifteenth to the twentieth century, including a sixteenth-century planet in red velvet and one of 1904 donated by Pius X, wooden furnishings and the Madonna della Roata, a rare example of dressed statue.
The Palladian façade in the conifers.

The Franciacorta municipality is surrounded by vineyards and morainic hills overlooking Lake Iseo; in the village of Bornato there are the castle with the Renaissance Villa Orlando and the ancient parish church of San Bartolomeo, as well as the permanent collection of the Nativity scenes of the World.
You enter from the Roman Gate, monumental entrance with clock that once had a drawbridge; inside, streets and squares of houses in tuff with the typical external stairs (profferli).
A monument to a 19th century town revolt.

Borgo on a hill at 495 meters in the first hinterland of Nebrodi, with a square overlooking Aeolian, Nebrodi and Etna: the Mother Church with the Chapel of the Rosary of Bartolomeo Travaglia, the Temple of San Cono with the Museum of Sacred Art in the catacombs, the church of SS. Salvatore with works of the Gagini and the convent of the Minor Observers.
Ligurian wines.
The large English park with lakes and neoclassical buildings, former residence of Vittorio Emanuele III, larger than Villa Borghese, with the bunker of the royal family.
The symbol of the old town.
From the Benedictine monastery to the castle of Del Carretto, with the plasters of Rubino.

Fishing village reached by the scenic coast, with the church of San Gregorio Magno and a small square of fishing houses; from the square starts the Goletta trail, a medium difficulty trekking that was once the only connection with Capo d'Orlando.
Sands and cliffs of the western Elbe.

Three marked cycling routes, yellow (7.5 km), green (10 km) and blue (12 km), and the network with numbered nodes of the Verdicchio Castles to combine walking and cycling routes between rows and villages; the tourist office rents e-bikes.
Along the promenade by the sea, the gates of the Naval Academy next to the church of San Jacopo, up to the stairway of Antignano.
The villages of the valley on foot, among woods and waterfalls.
The Ferrari myth where it started.
MiC card (updated 2021) marks every day as closed and indicates guided tours by reservation

The forest surrounds Tambre and has been an ancient dominion of the Serenissima; its trails run on foot, on horseback and by mountain bike, and in the heart of the forest there is an 18-hole golf course.

The oldest church in Monterotondo, in the Santa Maria district; the annexed monastery, wanted by Giacomo Orsini in 1448, was demolished in 1932. It preserves a Holy Family attributed to Savonanzi and the equestrian relief of Giordano Orsini on a fifteenth-century tomb; it was restored in the early two thousand years after the damage of the earthquake.
The entrance to the Castle district.

On the islet of Peddone in front of the old port, in a building reminiscent of a moored ship. On the ground floor wrecks of roman onerary ships, trees and rudders, the reconstruction of two ships set on fire in the vandal attack of the fifth century, a medieval wreck and the plastic of the port of the second century A.D.; on the first floor the history of the city from prehistory to the modern age, with Nuragic, Phoenician and Greek materials, a granite stele with the goddess Tanit, the heads of the emperors Domitian and Domitia, a Hercules and an Egyptian statue of Osiris. Tuesday-Saturday 8-13 and 16-19; audio guides and guided tours, groups over 30 people by reservation.
The places where St. Pius lived.
The first theatre built in Liguria in the Napoleonic era, protected among the monuments; you can visit it free of charge when it is open.
The large square with the Duomo, the Baptistery, the Town Hall and the statue of the Crostolo; under the porticos of the Broletto you pass to Piazza San Prospero.
The contemporary in a noble palace.
Mountain road built by the Austrian army in 1918, challenging and panoramic, with hairpin bends in the gallery (five galleries) going up to the San Boldo Pass.
A Gentileschi in the heart of the village.

In the Palazzo De Castellotti-Paganelli are located the Museum of lace tombolo (seven rooms of ancient and recent lace, including a dress worn by Naomi Campbell, with path for the blind), the Archaeological Museum "G. The Museum of Popular Traditions and the Pinacoteca Comunale. Open Saturday and Sunday.

The museum collects works of 20th century painters working mainly in Veneto, with a permanent collection dedicated to the regional landscape: coast and lagoons, reclamation plains, hills and villas of the mainland up to the Alps; during the year it hosts temporary exhibitions of painting.
Outside the centre, the castle houses the Wine Museum with restored tools.
At the entrance of the village, it stands on a small early Christian church; the present building is of the eighteenth century.
Roman arch leading to the forum, today Piazza del Mercato; next to, the remains of a temple transformed into the crypt of St. Isaac under the church of St. Ansano.

Former municipal alpine pasture at 1321 meters turned into a refuge by the Graglia alpine mountains, reachable from San Carlo by a dirt road; stop of the marked paths towards the Mombarone, Salvine and Netro.
Nature and prehistory in an ancient glacial peat bog.
The square with frescoed porticoes with the monument to Cavour, the artificer of the canal for rice fields, dominated by the fifteenth-century tower house of the Angel.
The story of the Umbria Plestini.
The three masks at the entrance of the country.
On the salt routes between Piedmont and Liguria.
The village under the cliff on the upper valley of the Albegna.
Temporarily closed for demolition, expansion, handling and safety of the finds (Archaeological Park of Gela); from open every day 9-19, tel. 0933 912626

In the Corte di Giarola, an ancient medieval agricultural complex near the Taro and the Via Francigena, tells the tomato from the Americas to the red gold of Parmense: the arrival in Italy around 1600, the birth of the preserve, the Experimental Station of the Conserves of 1922, the reconstruction of an ancient factory with vintage machinery and the seven stages of processing, up to advertising, sculptures, paintings and recipes. Open from 1 March to 8 December Saturday, Sunday and holidays 10-18; from December to February only groups on request.
The palace in the woods.
The St. Martin riding Domenico da Tolmezzo, masterpiece of the Friulian wooden sculpture.
The most important Roman city of Basilicata.

The park, along the State Road 210, covers about 30 hectares with the urban area of the Roman city, the necropolis and some suburban villas. The theatre, of Augustan age, is isolated in the countryside under the shadow of an oak tree, at the bottom of a short driveway: it has a cavea of 49.20 m of diameter and preserves, thanks to recent restorations, the average and the caveaima, part of the scenic building and the proscenium with circular and rectangular niches. About the middle of the second century A.D. was embellished with statues donated by Antonia Picentina, priestess of the Diva Faustina; it still hosts summer theater seasons and the TAU/Ancient United Theaters.
The mother church of the Medici village.
Flamingos and mills in the salt tanks.
The almost uninhabited stone village.

Symbol of the city, built at the end of the 14th century on the site of the acropolis of ancient Caelium, with fifteenth-century towers joined by walls; in the 15th century the Sanseverino transformed it into a noble residence with frescoes and coats of arms. From the Norman tower and the mast you can see the low Adriatic; in the atrium the well to which, according to tradition, was drawn in the drought periods; the frescoed rooms of the sixteenth century overlook a park with medieval gardens. Guided visits.
private property, open only on request
Modern art in a medieval castle.
A walk through the woods through legends and trees.
The church where Spallanzani rests.
Ancient frames still at work.

An ancient place of worship that testifies to the first inhabited nucleus, cited in 1662 as an ancient parish; demolished in 1872 because it was dilapidated, was rebuilt by the Municipality in 1874. It is reached with a naturalistic path on dirt; on August 7th the statue of the saint arrives in procession from the parish.
€10, reduced €2 (EU citizens 18-25 years), free under 18 EU; cumulative with Doge's Palace of Urbino €16
The sanctuary of the patroness overlooking the valley of Ofanto.
The 16th century Crucifix and the view over the valley of the Messa.
Handicrafts of the live broom.
Our Lady from the sea and Maria Goretti.

Opened in October 2006 in the former agricultural cooperative near the station, it is dedicated to the village of Marmot, the oldest neolithic lake village in Western Europe, submerged at 7.5 meters deep in front of the promontory: there emerged rectangular huts, ceramics, five pirogues and instruments in obsidian Lipari. The strong piece is a 9,5 m long 8,000-year-old piroga; a small room projects a teaching cardboard and film on recovery.
The lake environment between reeds and groves, reachable with a short walk suitable for strollers.
The walls of the Messapians in the open.
On the main square.
The octagonal church of the nuns.

The paved streets of the village go up towards the fortress on the ridge of tuff; downstream the village stretches at the level of the river, in the upper valley of the Conca. In July the castle hosts the Mons Cerignonis reenactment with procession and egg palio.
A bathroom with history.
The large nineteenth-century parish church with the bell tower of over 50 meters.

A hilly village of medieval origin between the valleys of Calore and Ufita, the birthplace of Salvatore Ferragamo: the castle with cylindrical towers, the walls painted by street art since 2011, the mother church with the urn of San Crescenzo and the Sanctuary of the Madonna della Neve.

On the third and fourth floor of Palazzo Fascie Rossi, it tells the history of the territory from the Paleolithic to the Bronze Age, at the Roman era and the Middle Ages, until the development of the city in the twentieth century, with the bond with the sea (fishing, yards, tourism). Organizes conferences, presentations, activities for families and exhibitions; building with elevator. Info: IAT 0185 478530, info@musel.it.
A sanctuary on the rock along the salt road.
The medieval heart of the city, under the arcades.
The museum dedicated to charlatans, symbol of Cerreto.

It tells the history of the territory from Prehistory to the seventeenth century with over 4,000 archaeological finds, plastic, reconstructions of environments, holograms, video and virtual reality. The route is divided into two locations: the section of Roman archaeology on the ground floor of the Municipal Library "P." Angelani and that of pre-Roman archaeology, with frescoed rooms, on the first floor of Palazzo Orsini. Accessible even to disabled people.

Cave excavated in the limestone rock where according to tradition lived around the year Mille san Domenico, Benedictine monk of Sora venerated for the miracles of his pilgrimages; you arrive there crossing a bridge in medieval style. The portal of the church has Byzantine-style designs and a bifora overlooks the lake with clear green waters, populated by germans, geese and folk.
Wide beach and suitable for families.
Historic district known for its alleys and ancient streets.

Municipality between Montalbano and the Padule di Fucecchio: high up the walled village of Larciano Castello with the tower and the Civic Archaeological Museum, then the village of Cecina with San Niccolò, Castelmartini with Villa Banchieri and the Garden of Memory for the massacre of the Padule of 1944, and in the plain the center visits to the reserve and the museum of the peasant civilization Casa Dei.
It has a large Gothic portal of Andrea Lombardo dated 1471 and a wooden crucifix of the fifteenth century.

Borgo sulla via Flaminia nato dai sovrivati della romana Pitinum Mergens, is known as the capital of truffle for the national autumn fair; its territory includes the Furlo Gorge, with the tunnel dug under Vespasian in 76 AD and the state nature reserve, and the remains of the abbey of San Vincenzo al Furlo.

Remains of the Roman city of Iulium Carnicum: the civil basilica of the first imperial age with the cryptoportico and the staircase on the first floor, the base of a portico with Tuscan capitals, a stretch of the paved square with statues bases and the podium of the temple.
The Romanesque outside the walls.
One of the largest collections of Roman stele of Sardinia.

Oratory of the sixteenth century in a narrow valley between Opagliolo and the tip of Casario, built above the Fountain of San Giulio that flows from the rock under the porch: according to legend the saint stopped there to pray before crossing the lake. After the visit of San Carlo Borromeo on 12 June 1573 it was transformed into a church; it has roof in piods, arched portico and a single altar dedicated to San Giulio. It was a destination of pilgrimages and several times visited by Bishop Odescalchi, then Pope Innocent XI.

On Mount Saraceno (Caraceno), about 1,000 meters above the valley of the Trigno and about one kilometer from the village, remains the traces of a Sannite settlement with fortifications of the fourth century BC, dismantled by the Romans after the third Sannite war; the sanctuary rises little lower. Visit Molise indicates them as a stop for archaeology enthusiasts and indicates paths through meadows, shrubs and woods with a view of the valley.
The Calvary of the Ossola.
A wrecked forest at the foot of the Cusna.
The garden and the rose garden of a late nineteenth century villa.

In the heart of the Valley of the Moon, one of the best preserved nuraghi of Gallura and probably the largest structure of the Bronze Age of the area: mixed type, corridor and tholos, with two entrances and a labyrinth of tunnels and corridors fruit of several construction phases.
From the Roman Spinazzola to the geology of the Murgia.

Small church of the first half of the 12th century, created for the spiritual assistance of those condemned to death and then a place of worship for pilgrims and needy. With the memorial stone it is one of the historical symbols of the plain of Richinvelda, where in 1350 the patriarch of Aquileia Bertrando of Saint Geneis was killed by the Friulian nobles; from 3 April 2018 it waves every day the flag of Friuli.

Roman thermal complex on an isolated hill about 5 km from the center, overlooking the Tyrrhenian Sea. Built in the Sillan Age (90-78 BC) on sources already used by the Etruscans, it reached the maximum development with Trajan and was expanded under Hadrian: a republican part in opus reticulatum and an imperial one in brick, with apodyterium, caldarium, frigidarium, tepidarium, library and gym. Rutilio Namaziano described it in 416 A.D.; it was abandoned during the Greek-Gothic war. In the park the botanical garden Horti Traianei; management Pro Loco, open every day 9:30-13.
The legend of the star.

In the Castello Brancaccio, it was the first demoethnoanthropological museum of Lazio: about two thousand objects, largely donated by the inhabitants, on pastoralism, agriculture, school, popular religiosity and domestic life, with reconstructed environments, photographs, letters and toys; of particular interest the part on religious and festive traditions. A recently opened archaeological section exhibits remains of Roman aqueducts that carried the Aniene water to Rome and finds of excavations on the Sublacense street. It is part of the Demos system and Medaniene network.
The most spectacular spas in Rome.
In the Palazzo Comunale (or of the Elders) more than 300 works including paintings, sculptures, ceramics and jewels, from the thirteenth to the nineteenth century.

Basement building shaped as a protohistoric mound next to the excavations of the Paludi, conducted from 1985 to 1998, which brought to light a palafittic village on the banks of the ancient Fucino, the largest prehistoric excavation in Abruzzo, and a burial necropolis of the final Bronze Age with burials in excavated tree trunks. The collections tell the Marsica from the Bronze Age to the Roman era, with workshops for restoration and anthropology.
The baroque of the parish of the village.

Great neoclassical church with Greek cross at the Porta della Croce, designed by De Mattia di Treia, with the dome frescoed by Virginio Monti; it preserves a polychrome wooden crucifix of the sixteenth century.

Borgo della bassa Reggiana was born around its fortress, now seat of the Town Hall, with a long porticoed road, the church of the Madonna with paintings of Lionello Spada and Palma the Younger, the Museum of Mask tied to the Carnival of Castlein and a museum of vintage shutters.

Opened in 2012, on the centenary of the company, in the headquarters of the Cimbali Group: it is indicated as the largest contemporary museum in the world of professional coffee machines, with about 300 pieces from the Cimbali and Maltoni collections (over 100 exhibited) from the end of the nineteenth century to today, and one of the most rich documentary collections on coffee. Among the acquisitions the Faema bike by Guido Reybrouck of the 1960s; audio guide app in 10 languages, barrier-free.
Renaissance fortress and residence in Urbino style.
The De Bardonnèche Castle.

Torbous-pallus basin of 89 hectares: an ancient lake almost entirely buried in an intermorenic depression, with a mirror of residual water surrounded by reeds, humid meadows and peat bogs. It hosts 129 plant species, some very rare, and 7 species of amphibians; since 1975 in summer the waters are dyed red for the bloody Euglena algae. Protected by the Municipality in 1974, today Special Conservation Area; you can visit along the perimeter paths with information panels.

A hilly village in the province of Campobasso overlooking the valley of Fortore and Lake Occhito, with alleys, arches and stairs; it is known for the Castle of Capua, whose Renaissance residence preserves the cycle of frescoes painted in 1550 by Donato da Copertino, and for the "Maitunate" (Maitunata) the New Year's songs door-to-door.
Nineteenth-century parish church on the main square; it preserves the statue of the Madonna dei Portenti, considered miraculous by the inhabitants. Feast of the patrons on May 3.
Shadow and walks a stone's throw from the village.

A fraction arose on the remains of the ancient Lavinium, which the tradition wants founded by Enea; there rises the Castle Borghese, in the Network of the Historical Houses of Lazio. In the 1960s the peasants of the estate and various figures of culture lived there.
Visitable only from the outside

4,500 hectares, of which about 4,000 are evaporation tanks: the largest salt pans in Europe, born where the sea flooded the low parts of the ancient Lake Salpi and developed especially in the nineteenth century under Ferdinand I of the Two Sicilies; protected since 1977, they host many species of aquatic birds such as herons ashes, gauzes, nitticolar and sgarze tuft. Guided tours only by reservation, every day from sunrise to sunset, for a fee.
A stone country village above the valley of Nesa.
Not accessible to people with disabilities

Around the village you can reach on foot the medieval ruins of the upper castle, the oldest of the two fortresses of Attimis, and the lower one, which with the castle of Zucco is the most recent of the territory; nearby there are also the fortresses of Partistagno, Zucco and Cucagna. The castle of Partistagno has seasonal openings with guided tours: check the calendar with the museum.

The ancient Diano, Sanseverino city perched on a hill overlooking the Vallo di Diano: Aragonese castle, cathedral with fourteenth-century tombs, Franciscan churches and a network of small museums in the old walled town.
Gnocchi and pappardelle with wild boar.

Educational fruit grove on the grounds of the Parks Authority, between the Curiel lakes and the Secchia expansion box, with about sixty local varieties of fruit, vines and native trees arranged as an Emilian plantation; next to the municipal vinegar mill of Casa Berselli.
Underwater mosaics with goldfish.

Municipality of the Ticino Park that gives its name to the culture of Golasecca (XII-V century BC): the archaeological area of Monsorino, state since 2001, is the most important monumental testimony in northwestern Italy, with funerary stone circles; finds of the Iron Age are exhibited in the small museum of the town hall.

Borgo della Sabina on a hill between the Farfa river and the Riana ditch, born around the Castellum Novum of the late thirteenth century: the whole town is the path of the Museum of the Sabina Oil, between Palazzo Perelli, an eighteenth-century mill and the medieval remains of San Donato, with the Farfa Gorges just a stone's throw away.

On a relief between the valleys of Bisenzio and Sieve, with the remains of a German settlement: the height, for the Allies Hill 810, was disputed for days between the 334th German Division and the 34th US Infantry Division.

The municipality includes the entire Aeolian archipelago except Salina, a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 2000: in Lipari the Castle with the acropolis, the Cathedral of St. Bartholomew and the Archaeological Museum         . Luigi Bernabò Brea , Marina Corta and the viewpoint of Quattrocchi; and then the Vulcano Fossa, the Sciara del Fuoco of Stromboli, Panarea, Filicudi and Alicudi.
St. Mark's Lion Hunt in town.
Next to San Giovanni Fuorcivitas the church of San Filippo Neri and the Fabroniana Library.
The sanctuary of the legend of the painted stone.
The daily life of miners, before or after visiting galleries.
The cross of Frederick II.
The view from the top of the village.
A millennial Byzantine church.
A rare strip of Tuscan marsh as it was before the Bonifice.
The Callido organ in the oldest church in the country.
The gardens of the villa, indicated by the Region among the attractions of the city.
An intact early medieval iconostasis.

Rebuilt building in the seventeenth century incorporating multiple tower houses, houses a multimedia space, virtual archive of collective memories, dedicated to the knowledge of the artisan, agricultural and food and wine work of the population of Trasimeno.
Walk through the noble buildings.

Small sandy cove surrounded by lush vegetation, home to the famous Trabocco di Punta Cavalluccio; it is the rocky stretch of the coast dotted with overflows, some of which house small restaurants on the sea.

The only church of the Madonie with an elliptical plan, perhaps a mosque transformed by the Normans, enlarged in the second half of the eighteenth century; it houses a St. Joseph by sculptor Filippo Quattrocchi. You will arrive from Piazza Fontana.

Built in the 12th century by the archbishops of Milan on a limestone spur above the southern shore of Lake Maggiore, it was contested between Torriani and Visconti, enlarged by the Visconti and in 1449 entrusted to the Borromeos, who still own it. In the Hall of Justice an exceptional cycle of frescoes; you can also visit the Historical Hall, the Hall of the Maiolicas (300 rare pieces), the Castellana Tower with views of the lake and the Medieval Garden; the Ala Scaligera houses exhibitions. Season 2026 from March 12 to November 8, every day.
Towers, moat and the frescoed chapel of the Contrari.
The Gothic in the historic center.
About 7 kilometers of sandy beach, with equipped and free stretches.
Taste the wine where you can make more in South Tyrol.
Museum in the historic center that exhibits the art collection of Giuseppe Ottavio Eliseo and Michele Praitano destined to Campobasso and Molise; the visit is by reservation.
Small church north of the town, in the hamlet of Sant'Andrea, which preserves outside traces of a building of the middle of the 11th century and inside frescoes of the 15th and early 16th century.
A century and a half of artists in love with a country.

Tower: every day, entrances at 00:00, 20:40. From 7/9 to 31/12/2026 first entrance 10:00, last 18:20; 24 and 31/12 last 16:20; closed 25/12. Collections: Mar and Thu 14-19, Wed and Fri 10-19, Sat-dom-Feasts 10-18:30.
The Roman city under the Scaliger palaces.
To be checked: visitor center and boat for a fee
Cooperative winery that produces mostly DOC wines and some grappas, with visits for groups by reservation.

From the second half of the eighteenth century the archipelago was fortified: on the island the Square Tower and the Fort San Vittorio (Old Guard), at the beginning of the nineteenth century the Fort Carlo Felice guarding the Pass of the Coin and the Fort San Giorgio in Santo Stefano; between the late nineteenth century and world wars Nido d'Aquila, Punta Tegge and Punta Rossa. You can see them along the coastal road; the anti-air stations are visited with the guides of the park.
The town hall in front of the Bo.
The trap on the sea.
Church of the sixteenth century to which in 1643 were added the octagonal drum and the spire; the terracotta spire collapsed with the earthquake of 1976 and was rebuilt in copper in 1986.
The "Ringhiera dell'Umbria" is a panoramic village of Sagrantino, with frescoes by Benozzo Gozzoli and Perugino in the former church of San Francesco.
Walk through churches, palaces and fountains of a mountain village.
The places of the villa that welcomed Cicero.
A small museum in the heart of Chianti.
A noble villa still inhabited by the family, with its monumental garden.

Municipality of the Mantua plain on the lower Mincio: in Governolo la Chiusa and the Conca di navigazione del Berazzolo, among the major testimonies of hydraulic archaeology of the Po Valley, host the Museo Diffuso del Fiume; in Barbassolo the Romanesque ...Pieve of the two wells of the Saints Cosma and Damiano.

Canyon limestones (cave) of the territory: Cava d'Alfano, Cava Ddieri and Cava Bagni; in Alfano, Passo Ladro and Cardinale there are prehistoric necropolis with monumental tombs of the early Bronze Age. The source of the Cardinal feeds the river that supplies the country with drinking water; in 1898 about 200 liters per second were channeled for irrigation and mills, and Greek hydraulic works from the end of the 8th century B.C. carried its waters towards Syracuse.
A strong Habsburg on the lake.
One of the most beautiful squares in Italy, designed by Giovan Battista Aleotti as the courtyard of honour of the palace, with the church of Santa Maria della Snow and the civic tower.

Among the most important archaeological sites of Sardinia: founded by the Phoenicians in the 8th century BC, then Punic city and Roman town since the 1st century A.D. You can visit the thermal baths, the forum square, a temple, the house of the tetrastyle atrium with mosaics, the amphitheatre and the sanctuary of Esculapio; remains submerged visible with snorkeling. A cumulative ticket with the Patron Museum: entire € 5.50.
It preserves in the chapel of St. Nicholas pictorial cycles of the fourteenth century, among the oldest in the city, an altar of Juvarra and paintings of G.A. Sweet, Molineri and Claret.

Founded in 1282 by Peter, bishop of Capaccio and adviser to Charles II of Anjou, transformed in 1685-1686: Gothic traces, a frescoed Annunciation of the fourteenth century in sacristy and three great canvases of the Solimena.

It consists of a geological section and a paleontological section dedicated to mining art, with drilling machines, lamps, masks and instruments for gas detection; also suitable for schoolchildren and families with children.
It keeps valuable paintings, including the Madonna del Cardellino of the workshop of Pinturicchio.
Orchids and wetlands where the Belbo is born.
The Viterbo Renaissance under a golden roof.
Along the Metaurense Provincial Road, it was the country residence of Federico Bonaventura; in 1578 it stayed there Torquato Tasso, which here composed the "Canzone al Metauro" .
One of the great cultural centers of the Middle Ages.

Historical chestnut tree restored in 2009, already praised in 1673 by the historian Michelangelo Mariani: the inhabitants planted the trees on the municipal soil with a privilege of Roman origin that gave them the property of fruit and wood, used for timber, tannin and chestnuts. Today we see secular chestnut trees, terraces and circular walls of containment.

Roads with ancient palaces, sunny squares, small museums of local history and craft shops that preserve traditional crafts, on a plateau overlooking fields, vineyards and green areas. It is the country of origin of the director Frank Capra, to whom the Borgo Film Fest is dedicated.
A walk between Renaissance churches and the Norman castle.
The great pictorial cycles of the Padan Renaissance.

The old town, perched on the hill, is a network of alleys, squares and panoramic points; the houses have walled numerous blocks of Roman and medieval stone, and Roman tiles with inscriptions are marked by signs. From the viewpoint and from the balcony of Largo Porta Maggiore you can see, according to the side, Abruzzo or the Adriatic Sea; there is also an alley 34 cm wide. In the squares remain street art and crochet works of the Yarn Bombing.
The zebra side is the facade.
The artist who told the reclamation.

The territory of Preone is classified as a geosite of supranational interest for the fossil fauna of more than 200 million years ago (Triassic); in the early eighties there were recovered the rare remains of the Preondactylus buffarinii, one of the most ancient species of pterosaur. From the village, close to the exhibition, starts the short trail to the Ring Lunas Stavolo with panels on geology, paleontology, fauna and vegetation.

An arched cove about 200 meters south of Capo Bellavista, one kilometer from the port, with fine sand between silver and gold, granite rocks and bottom that slopes gently, guarded by the tower of San Gemiliano; several times Blue Flag FEE.
The large 18th-century church in Palladian style overlooking the square preserves works by Girolamo Denti, Giovanni da Mel (1531), Cesare Vecellio (1580-90) and Luigi Cima.

Borgo sul'Oglio in the Oglio Sud Park, defensive outpost in Gonzaghescan age: from the medieval Porta Torre, the rest of the castle of San Genesio, the streets open in checkerboard towards Piazza Matteotti; it is the home of Furga, the first factory of Italian dolls, told in the Civic Museum.
Alleys wide a person.
Museum of peasant tools and ancient prints on wine that covers four centuries of wine history.
Small church on a hill, in white stone and basalt, reached by a panoramic staircase.

On the site of Siris the settlers of Taranto founded Herakleia in 434-433 BC: in the park remain the acropolis with the grid of the streets, houses with environments around courtyards, late Hellenistic peristyle houses with mosaic floors, the artisans district with furnaces, the sanctuary of Dionysus with the foundations of the temple and agora with the altar and the sanctuary of Demeter on two terraces.
A 19th century theatre in a 1304 building.
A dip in the river in the summer.
The tower of the Fieschi that dominates the country.
The church from which the village was born.
The chapel of the castle became a baroque church.
A Norman tower in the woods.

In the center of Cuccaro, the museum of the Colombian Study Centre is dedicated to Christopher Columbus and to the kinship, supported by studies and documents, between the Colombo family of Cuccaro and the navigator. Visit by reservation by phone to the Municipality (0131 771928, 9-13 hours, Saturday included).

Archaeological area identified with the ancient coastal settlement of Cirellae, probably founded by the Greeks and grown as a commercial center thanks to the port; remain the Carafa Castle, the Mother Church and the Convent of St. Francis of Paola. Not far away is the modern Teatro dei Ruderi, home of summer festivals.
The baths on the sea.
The river that comes from the rock.
Middle Ages above a Roman house.

It documents the life of workers and craftsmen of the Iblean plateau: the collection was born in the early 1970s with photographer and artist Nunzio Bruno and grew with the help of the ethnologist Antonino Uccello; established in 2001 by Province and Municipality, it is open since May 2004. Six climbs on the ground floor on wheat processing, breeding, pasteurization and crafts, with the carrador shop and a lathe of 1880.

Versilia's seaside resort was born around the Fortino Lorena in 1778, today the seat of the Museum of satire and caricature, with the pier from which the marble of the Apuans was embarked, the fine sandy beach and the villas of Vittoria Apuana and Rome Imperiale; between the museums the house-atelier of the sculptor Ugo Guidi and Villa Bertelli.

Environmental nature trail in a botanical and ornithological area, site SIC and SPA, where lives the rare carnivorous plant Utricularia vulgaris; managed by the association A.S.T.E.A., with guided tours on request (tel. 339 5247689).
The façade of the town symbol.
Listing in extension: the guide covers for now 2 of the 8 places of culture recorded by the Ministry of Culture in this municipality, as well as churches, squares and nature.
The ice of a time.

It is located in the Geodynamic Observatory built in 1886 by Michele Stefano De Rossi next to the ancient Fortress, one of the first Italian seismological observers and still active; between 1922 and 1935 William Marconi used it for broadcasting experiments. Managed by the ENG in agreement with the Municipality and inaugurated as a museum on 26 February 2005, it presents Earth Sciences: Geology of the Albani Hills, seismology with seismic station, geodesia with GNSS station, astronomy with telescope, geochemical monitoring of volcanoes and remote sensing. Guided tours by reservation from the museum site; you park at the Campi di Annibale and follow the directions.

Example of the sixteenth century Tuscany, probably designed by Antonio da Sangallo the Elder: facade with eight pilasters with Ionic capitals and dorics and large central rose window, inside with a single nave with a valuable baptismal font in marble. Caldana is one of the medieval villages of the municipality, surrounded by imposing walls.
The door of the coat of arms.
The organ of Agostino Traeri.
Linked to the witch trial of 1587-1589.
Renaissance palace built in 1536 by the merchant Donato Legari; the Gonzaga also lived there.

Small village in the hills that has preserved the medieval character, with the walls that enclose the monuments; next to the parish stands the neo-Gothic town hall. From the road that exits the village opens the view of the village and the massif of the Amiata.
The Piedmontese baroque of the Buniva and the village's symbol well.

Built around the year 1000 in a panoramic position above the village, it is one of the best preserved buildings of the ancient Marquisate of Ceva, with a high tower that dominates the shelter; in 1796 there were aquartiered the Napoleonic armies. On the first floor the Bonaparte Museum preserves the largest collection of original prints and etchings by Giuseppe Pietro Bagetti on the first Italian countryside of Napoleon; in the tower a museum of marbles and local stones, with a wide view of mountains and valleys. From 21 March to October 2026 open on Saturday 14-18, Sunday and holidays 10-18; schools by reservation with CoopCulture.
Spa park run by an association along the Via Francigena: one bath is free, the others require a contribution.
Erected in 1636, with a beautiful wooden coffered ceiling and a walkway destined to the tomb of the Della Corgna.
The Medieval Terni.
The place where Saint Anthony of Padua lived, a pilgrimage destination.

Born from the collection of Sergio Sanvido (1928-2015), restorer and collector of bicycles, donated in part to the Municipality in 2007: from the precursors, like a celerifer in wood of late eighteenth century, two Michaux and the bike Grand-bi, to the bikes from work, from city, military and as a child, to the bikes from race tied to Bottecchia, Coppi, Bartali, Saronni, Moser and Pantani, with accessories, shirts and covers of the Sunday of Corriere. Autonomous visit with tablet or app; open 10-13 and 15-18 on weekends from April to October (also on Fridays in July and August).

It belongs to the Basilica of Maria SS. Assunta, in the heart of the historic center, and collects the heritage of the basilica's deposits and churches, convents and monasteries closed by the 1866 Eversive Laws: paintings, sculptures, silvers (calics, pissides, monstrers, reliquaries, turboli, crucifixes), missals, antiphons, nativity scenes, waxes and sacred vestments.

Main rest of a nuragic complex with two nuraghes and a village of the Bronze Age: the tomb, in granite blocks on irregular rows with the body still intact, was disassembled and rebuilt not far from the end of the twentieth century for the construction of the Nuoro-Lanusei highway.
Erected in 1824 instead of an older one, it is located on the second floor of a group of houses and was restored in 1994.
Stone villages of the Apennines.

Large areas of ecological rebalancing at the border with Reggiolo and Guastalla, where in spring along ditches and canals bloom the lawn violet and the dread. The CAI 608, open in 2017, starts from Ponte del Pastore: about 10 km, two and a half hours on foot, easy and suitable for everyone.
Early Christian church with three remarkable frescoes: the oldest Visitatio Virginis, from the 8th century, a Last Supper from 1100 and an 11th century Tree of Jesse.

The municipality has 5,891 hectares in the Madonie Park and numerous geosites of the Geopark Madonie UNESCO, with hiking trails, bike paths and equestrian trails; there pass the Trail Italy and the path of the Madonite Sanctuaries. In the hamlet of Piano Battaglia there are ski slopes and ski lifts.

The village rises along the hill with towers, squares and alleys with colorful facades; the Castle Ruspoli, of the tenth century, is indicated as the oldest in the area. The Pullarella is the surviving part of the original medieval village, once accessible only from the entrance of the castle; in the village the Fontana della Medusa (2008) by Luciano Mastrolorenzi recalls the bronze decorations of the ships of Caligula.
Nature and history on the pass between two valleys.
Two thousand years in a few steps: the Arch of Augustus, the Bridge of Tiberius, the Domus of the Surgeon, the Temple Malatestano, Castel Sismondo and the Fellini Museum, then the sea.
An example church of Gothic-angioin architecture, with the obelisk of San Domenico in the square.
The view of the Valdinievole to Elba.
The door of the travelers.
A village of ridge between very high walls and registered portals.

Completed in 1703 next to Palazzo Giustiniani, it has the local stone façade with clock and coat of arms of the Justinians; in the single nave an organ of the eighteenth century, a nineteenth-century choir in painted wood, the Mater Dolorosa, the Assumption of the Virgin and the relic of the head of St. Gratilian.

Built between 1715 and 1742 on a project by Antonio Tubino da Lugano, a Latin cross with nine polychrome altars, marble staircase and facade of Carlo Corbellini with statues of Luca Calegari; the bell tower was designed in 1603 by Francesco Dattari called Pizzafuoco. It contains a 16th century painting of Moretto from the ancient parish church, the Pietà by Giovanni Battista Pittoni, the San Francesco del Malosso, a wooden Crucifix of 1480 and the marble group of Antonio Calegari at the altar of the Rosary; decorations by Angelo Cominelli of the second nineteenth century.

Beach of crescent pebbles under crags of white tuff up to 100 meters high, used as a natural port by Greeks and Romans, who dug a tunnel lit by skylights to connect it inside. After repeated landslides the tunnel and the beach have been closed: today you can only admire from the sea or from above, from the path of the Fieno.
The museum of peasant civilization occupies the small convent of 1664 next to the recently restored Carmelo church; from here also starts the guided tour to Monte San Paolino.
A tiny village with a medieval chapel.

Historic centre of alleys to walk on a hill inside Caldera. The historical fountains are the Fontana del Piscero (1576), with beautiful views of the village, the Fontana del Ponte with octagonal plan, the Fontana di Canale, from which spring two springs of sparkling water, and the Fontana Trincheri.
The medieval square tower in front of Sant'Antonio Abate and the circular tower covered with ivy towards the sea, garrisons against pirate raids.

Under the former monastery next to St. Francis, today seat of the municipality with an internal cloister, there are underground rooms of the XV-XVI century: two large monumental cisterns (the main contains about 450 cubic meters of water) and the Sala degli Ammassi. The village has at least seven cisterns, vital during the sieges; just outside the walls, on the west side, there is also a medieval well that is over 20 meters deep.
Modica's other cathedral.
The lions' portal on the square.

Centre of Alta Langa at the confluence of the Uzzone in Bormida, of Roman origin and capital of the hazelnut Tonda Gentile delle Langhe: in the village of San Michele the square porticoed with the fifteenth-century tower that houses the Ecomuseo dei Terrazzementi e della Vite; in the village of San Pantaleo the parish and the Romanesque Madonna della Pieve.
The Romanesque on the border with Lunigiana.
the MiC card indicates "closed" every day; check the opening with the Municipality (tel. 0984 435385)

Cities at the foot of Monte Somma, with the medieval village of Casamale closed by the Aragonese walls, the castle of Alagno of 1458, the complex of Santa Maria del Pozzo with the museum of peasant civilization and the excavations of the Roman villa called  "Augustea" .
Where the Bridegroom Promised were born.

Country on a limestone spur overlooking the Valle del Marmo Platano, with the medieval district of Pianello, the castle and the National Archaeological Museum in the sixteenth century Seminary; it is linked to San Gerardo Maiella.
Sources, beech and white truffle woods.
Accessible only on request, to do a few days before (Italia.it)
The last great expansive delight, on the edge of the woods.

Funeral church on the hill behind San Michele, begun in 1716, with two small dome towers, cross vaults and stuccoes; it closes the Via Crucis of Appiano, created by the friars between the Seven and the nineteenth century on the model of the first Calvary of Bolzano, whose last figures were completed in the nineteenth century. About 25 minutes walk from the center of San Michele, with views over the whole Oltradige.
Homage to the lacemakers of Offida.
The altarpiece of Tiepolo in the cathedral of the city.
An archaeological area of the early Christian basilica.
The academy next to Bibiena.

The castle of Lerona, bulwark of Orvieto in the 12th century, was then destroyed: parts of the walls and two gates remain, Gate of the Sun and Gate of the Moon. In 1585 the community gave itself its own Statutes and in 1595 freed itself from Orvieto and Monaldeschi.
Civic museum in Piazza Celestino V, next to the Fraternal Fountain.
Alleys and gates of a fortified town.

The parish church on Piazza Orsini was started in 1527 by the Countess Vittoria Camponeschi and enlarged by Giovanni Carafa in 1549: the façade unites two bodies born separate, connected in 1562 as it recalls the inscription on the left portal, still renaissance, while the right entrance to broken tympanum is baroque, dated 1633. The interior is a single large baroque hall with large wooden altars of the eighteenth century and paintings of the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries. Open every day from 7 to 19 according to the MiC card.
The funeral complex of the Etruscan warrior princes, near a village of the 7th century BC: here emerged the Warrior Princes, among the oldest statues of European art.
Panoramic ruins and memory of the Resistance.
Open for groups by reservation
Founded in 1181 by Bardone of the Counts Fieschi, archpriest of Lavagna.
The historic centre, UNESCO World Heritage Site, home to a university founded in 1506, one of the oldest in Europe.
tours only with guide by reservation (in-Lombardy)

Biotope near the station of Rablà, along the bike path of the Via Claudia Augusta, fed by the Zielbach river: there live royal germans, herons, herons, white dancers, amphibians and dragonflies. From here starts a ring walk, suitable for families and strollers, towards Bad Egart.

A small town of the first hills of Reggio Emilia from the centre of Renaissance plant, home to the poet Matteo Maria Boiardo and naturalist Lazzaro Spallanzani; around the Rocca dei Boiardo there are piazza Spallanzani with the statue of the scientist, his birthplace and the churches of the center, while in the hamlets rises the castle of Arceto.
In Piazza Cordova, dominated by the Adelasia Tower of Norman times, is the destination of the votive pilgrimage of the Feast of St. Philip the Apostle, the black saint, in the night before May 1.
The origins of Accadia, at the entrance of the River Fossi.
The town hall of the end of the thirteenth century with portico, large hall and loggia "parlera" from which the proclamations were read.
The canal port fed by the river Bruna, with the fish market; on Saturday morning, beyond the Ponte Giorgini, the local market is held.
Paths between chalks and gullies.
The most expensive sanctuary to the Varallesi, next to the parish.
Occitan villages.

Just outside the village, on the eastern side of the Vallone near the Li Castelli farm, a crypt excavated in tuff by the Basilian monks and erected in abbey around the year 1000. It has two rooms, the first with three naves with two entrances, and frescoes of saints of Greek tradition including the Virgin, St. Michael Archangel, St. Nicholas and the Christ Pantocrator; next to an ancient mill.
