Guided tours, free parking, also hosts an exhibition of handcrafted nativity scenes; tel. +39 099 616453.
The Roman tower.

Local specialties are the tomato and the mouthpieces, sweet fried pizzas; the territory is part of the Castelli Romani DOC wine area. Ardea has equestrian traditions: here the trotter Varenne was raised.
Count the columns of the facade.
A trip from the Paleolithic to the nineteenth century: the Atrium of the mosaics, the museum of Lazzaro Spallanzani, the Palethnology of Gaetano Chierici and the naturalistic collections.
€5, reduced €3 (6-13 years), free up to 5 years
Church of medieval origin, renovated several times in the first decades of the nineteenth century, with a neoclassical appearance and imposing façade; the main altar is attributed to Filippo Juvarra.
Church built in 1300 on the edge of the gravina, reachable by a country road.
The large dome of Fontanelle.
Castagneti and a small isolated church above the abbey.
Crespi and Rotari in Piazza Garibaldi.

In the seventeenth century Palazzo Zagarese, about 3,000 objects on the civil history of Calabria and paintings from the sixteenth century to today, with works by Priests, Solimena, Carrà, Balla, De Chirico, Guttuso and Sironi.

Cycle path on the chair of the Treviso-Ostilla railway, built in 1930 for military purposes and abandoned after the Second World War, between countryside, watercourses, country churches and Venetian villas. The historic cycle path ends in Cologna Veneta; the new 23 km stretch towards Pressana, Minerbe, Legnago and Cerea was inaugurated on 4 August 2025.
The town cathedral in the heart of Nuoro, next to the Tribu and a few hundred meters from Piazza del Poeta.

On the left side of Piazza del Popolo, designed by Pietro Maggi, a Latin plant with three naves. In the transept there is the banner of the miracle of the Virgin that in 1850 would stop the plague; in the crypt a reconstruction of the Cave of Lourdes.
Film under the stars in the cloisters.
Amerigo Vespucci's family home.

Made in 1992 by the Viterbo sculptor Catia Cutigni: three life-size statues lying about 7 meters deep in the lake, under the gardens of Via della Rocca, laid by divers of the Fire Department. The village also has a needle-embroidered nativity scene and thread with scenes of local life.
The church at the foot of the waterfall, to be combined with the walk.
Monday 10-19:30 · Fri 10-16 · Sun 10-18 · closed Saturday and Jewish holidays

Rebuilt by Bishop Ugone around 1036 and consecrated in 1253, with the Romanesque façade of Umbria; the interior was renovated by Galeazzo Alessi in 1571 and the excavations revealed walls of Roman age.
Aosta Mountain.

On the outskirts of the village, well-tombs of the Iron Age (VI-V century B.C.) excavated in limestone and arranged in concentric rows, with the dead in fetal position; the bronze and ceramic kits are at the Civic Museum.
Mill of 1428-30, recently restored, the oldest still in operation in the Naviglio belt; it is fed by the Roggia Biraga, derived from the Naviglio Grande in 1428.
The symbol of Fondi, with view from the terrace of the mastium.
The eighteenth-century mother church of the country.

Fraction on the hills above San Michele, a few minutes drive away, which preserves the medieval system with many vaulted passages under the houses. Above the village is the castle of Monreale-Königsberg, dating back to the fourteenth century, once the administrative seat of the territory, which is now not open to visitors; in the village the church of Sant'Agata, of the early thirteenth century, and that of the SS. Redeemer, 1900. In the woods an easy trekking trail touches the remains of the ancient silver mines; the vineyards rise up to 650-750 meters.
A shrine very much felt by local devotion.
private property, visits to be agreed with the owners
In the territory the Domus de Janas of Spelunca Orre of the Neolithic, the tomb of giants of Paule Luturu and the Nuraghe Perda Orrubia of the Bronze Age, as well as the tomb of Pranu 'e Laccos.
In via Mannu, about 150 meters from the cathedral, preceded by a garden.
It dominates the old town; recently restored to welcome visitors, it offers views of the countryside and its crops.
Six-cinelle fountain with the inscription "salus publica suprema lex esto" in open air and always accessible.

In the thirteenth century Palazzo Gottifredo, commissioned by Cardinal Gottifredo of Raynaldo; museum founded in 1932 and reopened in 1996. Archaeological sections on the 19th century scholars of the polygonal walls and on the ancient Aletrium (inscription by Lucio Betilieno Varo, model of Etruscan-Italian temple, bronze perhaps of Hercules, paintings of the Domus of Betilienus), vases recovered by the Guardia di Finanza and demoetnoanthropological collection. Open Tuesday-Sunday 10-13, Friday-Sunday also 15.30-18.30.
Wellness half an hour from Bologna.
Museum + gallery €10; gallery only €8; museum only €4, reduced €2 (5-12 years)

Borgo is between the waters of the Amerino and Furapane sources, dominated by Palazzo Cesi, residence of Federico Cesi founder of the Accademia dei Lincei, which in 1624 hosted Galileo; in the center and territory medieval churches and baroque and castles like Casigliano.
Opened in Rome in 1883 and then transferred to Valle Giulia, on the edge of Villa Borghese.

Crossed by Lambro and among the main accesses to the Parco di Monza, Biassono gathers around Piazza Italia the Baroque Villa Verri, frequented by the Lombard illuminators, the Palazzo Croce Bossi and the Civic Museum Carlo Verri; in the historic center the parish church of San Martino.
The sculpted rosette facade.
The oldest nucleus of Alexandria, grown near the Tanaro around Santa Maria di Castello, today one of the liveliest neighborhoods of the city.

Church of Altino, which is still the seat of the bishop. The first church, built around 1850 at the villa of the Counts Bacchini, served the population until 1961, when the new Romanesque-inspired complex designed by the architect Forlati was built, on an area considered the center of the ancient city; a portico on three sides connects it to the museum and opens south towards Torcello.
18th century church in Piazza del Popolo, with baroque altars and paintings by the Ruffanese painter Saverio Lillo.
Eagles, deer and mouflons in the cliffs of Gennargentu.
The headquarters of the Ecomuseum of Biellese dedicated to vine and wine, in the recipe that was stored grapes.

Among the most important Romanesque churches in the Marche region, with Byzantine influences, probably of the 11th century on Roman remains and restored between 1925 and 1932: facade with bell tower and cylindrical climbing tower, almost square interior with three naves with four cylindrical pillars that hold the dome.

Country of the Pinerolian plain with a museum of contemporary art outdoors, Open Art Pool, born in 1991 with about seventy works in the streets, the 18th-century parish church of San Grato di Gerolamo Buniva and the municipal wing of 1699.

Museum of small mechanical sculptures in paper, wood and metal that visitors themselves put in motion, between irony and invention: the collection has about 200 automatons of artists from Japan, United States, Germany, United Kingdom, France, Canada, South America and Italy, half exposed permanently and half on exhibition itinerant. It is located in part of the small castle of Vezzano, of early medieval origin (IX century); it organizes guided tours and construction courses for children and adults. Open Monday-Friday 9-17.
Karst complex in the most important casts in Italy: over 750 meters of tunnels and a colony of over 6,000 bats. Tradition has it that he inspired Dante's Hell.
The square seen from below.

The most important natural area of Cerbaie, established by ministerial decrees of 1977 (biogenetic reserve) and 1980 (animal repopulation), between 45 and 114 meters of altitude: sea pine with cerro, oak, oak, oak, farnia and hornbeam; deer, roe deer, deer, wild boars and, in the humid zones, germans, folagues, herons ashes and marzaioles. The municipality runs an area of about 10 hectares near Staffoli open in summer, and at the Poor Town a forest road of 800 m with picnic areas. On Cerbaie a network of CAI paths for foot and bike, with sources of Leone, Sasso and Pierdo and about 2 km of Via Francigena in Galleno.
The destination and starting point of the hill trails.

The largest park in the Val di Fiemme, on a small hill just a few steps from the centre, with secular lindens around the parish church and views over the valley, Avisio and mountains; the ring tour is also available in electric wheelchairs (Montagna Senza Limiti project).
The spiral portal.
The history of the industry that made Val Trompia.

House-museum in the Floroni-Accordi palace, built on the new avenues after the demolition of the walls: the collection of Risorgimento relics collected by the Fioroni family from the last decades of the nineteenth century was exhibited in the early twenties of the twentieth century in rooms furnished with furniture, tapestries and chandeliers of epoch. Eight rooms retracing the Unity from the Napoleonic epic to the myth of Garibaldi; the ground floor tells the Medieval and Renaissance Legnago with weapons and ceramics, and in the courtyard there are the lapidary, one of the marching lions and the portal of the birthplace of Salieri. Open Tuesday, Thursday and Friday 9-12, Wednesday and Sunday 15-19.
Medieval alleyways.
Baroque on the square.

Palaces of the Cinque e Seicento with stone portals: Palazzo Colecchi, Palazzo Grilli with four corner towers, Palazzo Mansi, Palazzo Coccopalmeri, Casa D'Amata with the vineyard, the Town Hall with the clock tower in Piazza Municipio and the houses of Corso Roma with loggia and external stairs; filigree, lace, wrought iron and carving remain alive.
Two historic buildings, often with an exhibition.
Renaissance church of about 1450, with the facade rebuilt in the early eighteenth century and frescoes attributed to Francesco Cozza.
The castle built by Pier Maria Rossi between 1448 and 1460 for the beloved Bianca Pellegrini, with the Golden Room frescoed and the view of the Parma valley.
Fine sand, dunes and pinewood Blue Flag.
The Urtier stream descends in three jumps; in winter it is a destination for ice climbing, in summer of family walks.
Two confraternities in one asymmetrical church.
A short hike out of town.

At Capo Schisò was founded in the 8th century BC the Greek colony of Naxos, whose park preserves the remains of the Olympic Temple and the Archaic City. From the garden of the museum, crossed by a stretch of the ancient walls, starts the route in the ancient urban area along a rural road and then the plateau B. The Archaeological Park, established in 2007, also manages the ancient Theatre of Taormina and since 2019 the Castle of Schisò. The ticket (museum and archaeological area) is also purchased online; open every day 9-19.45, last entry 19.
Built in 1810 on a project by Carlo Barrera, it is the House of the Arts of the city and houses the civic museum.

Rebuilt around the year 1000 and repeatedly rebuilt, it has external walls rich in bas-reliefs: twelve hanging arches on human heads representing the Apostles, crucifer lambs, hunting scenes on the eastern facade, a Byzantine dolphin, priests in procession and a blessed bishop, under a large walled rose window. The crypt, discovered by chance in 1975 during the restorations, has vaults cruising on tubs columns and archaic capitals, of uncertain dating. On the north-east side, at the top of 14 steps, the Bronze Holy Door (2020-2021) recalls the perpetual plenary indulgence that according to the Leo IX tradition granted in June 1053: it opens on the morning of June 1st and closes on the afternoon of June 2nd, for the patron celebrations.
The view that opens onto the gulf coming from Imperia.
The walls of Gothic age enclose the old town; Porta Picena is one of the gates and there are four city gates.
A thousand species of plants with the gulf at their feet.
The relic of the thorn and the rites of Holy Week.

Borgo della Serra morenica overlooking the lake of Viverone, dominated by the castle built around a tower of the tenth century and rebuilt by the Glasses; around the church of San Michele with the ancon of Gaspare Serra, the country shrine of San Vitale and, among forests and erratic boulders, the lake of Bertignano with its prehistoric pirogues.
Natural area on the hills of Sasso Marconi.

The cornerstone of the Benedictine presence in Cluniac, in Franciacorta, documented since 1050, passed in 1446 to the Olivetans who rebuilt it between 1450 and 1534 with the best artists of Brescia; suppressed in 1779, it is again olivetan since 1974. The church (1480-1490, renovated in the nineteenth century) has a portal with protire and polychrome ceramic arches, eighteenth-century frescoes, Christ with Saints Peter and Paul of Moretto (1545) and a wooden choir inlaid in 1480. Three cloisters: the small (1455-1460) with terracotta frieze, the large (1480-1490) with porch and loggia, that of the Cisterna (1580-1590) with wrought iron well and three sundials of 1648; the antirefectory has the Visions of the Apocalypse of Lattanzio Gambara (1570) and the guesthouse painted by Romanino.
The ancient heart of the village, about a kilometer from the village, where village festivals and living nativity scenes are held.
The Manfredi Bridge sung by Dante.
The medieval gate of the fourteenth century from which you entered the city and the stretch of walls along Via Sottocastello with a view of the Piave valley.
The castle from which the country was born.
Hellenistic thermal structure of the third century BC, reopened after the excavations, with waters between 40 and 70 °C.
The peasant and pastoral civilization of Casentino in a medieval tower.

The city of the sickle between two seas: the Tower of Ligny on the tip, the Clock Tower with the astronomical clock of 1596, the Mysteries of the Church of Purgatory, the Cathedral of San Lorenzo, the Pepoli Museum and the Madonna of Trapani at the Annunziata, the salt pans.

Around Piazza Astrua there are the confraternity of Santa Croce, built in 1639, which houses precious reliquaries, the ancient tower and the monument to the Alps; not far from the parish church of Santa Fede, consecrated in 1601 and enlarged in 1667. The oldest nucleus is the canton of Valle; in the public gardens the monument to the stone paver.

Born in 1995 as an environmental documentation center and inaugurated in 2002 as a Visitor Center of the Park, it brings together an aquarium of 14 tanks (about 21,000 liters) connected to the lagoon, a diorama of the lagoon flora and fauna, the botanical garden       Â Via delle Erbe Â Â Â Â and two sheds for birdwatching on the terrace. Park hours: 9:30-12:30 and 16-19, in summer 9-12:30 and 17-20.
Municipality north of Udine between the Torre stream and the medieval forges, known after the war for the handicrafts of the corn pulp, told by the permanent exhibition of Piazzale Centa.
Outside the center, venerated for its icon of the 13th century.
The panoramic terrace on Sora and the valley of Liri.

The ruin of Bec Dauphin is what remains of an ancient military garrison, probably before the fortress of Vitozzi. Higher up, in Borgata Ciapella, a boina with the acronyms P and M marked the ancient border between Perosa and Meano; here probably stood the fortress built in 1597 and dismantled in 1796. Free access.
Contemporary art in the village palace.
The symbol of autonomy.
The mother church of Apricena, dedicated to Saint Martin and Saint Lucia, was entirely rebuilt in two or three years after the earthquake of 1627.

Playground, technology and environmental activity since 2011 on a hill of Arghillà, north of the city, in the area of the former Batteria Gullì, strong Umbertino: routes, educational installations, play area, amphitheatre with 800 seats and panorama on the Strait.
In the Municipal Palace, dedicated to the buffet, musical instrument obtained from a wooden barrel.
The triptych of Antoniazzo Romano.
The life of the fields under the convent.

From the hamlet of San Francesco you climb to the foot of Mount Gronlàit among farms still intact with the roofs in wooden dorms; from the Imperial Prati the path to the Valcava, lying out of golden larch trees. The Gronlàit and the Fravòrt are the two peaks of the municipality over 2000 meters.
It is reached by going down the small passage called "Galleria dell'Arte" (Galleria dell'Arte), according to the Municipality gives the best of its colors with good weather.
The space of the maison in the historic Palazzo della Mercanzia in Piazza della Signoria, among archive pieces, installations and collections.
Etruscan city on the hill above the Valdichiana, with medieval squares and one of the first public museums in Italy.
Unusual architecture.
Castle and chapel frescoed on the cliff above the Adige.
A waterfall in the city.
The fourth museum of Intesa Sanpaolo, in the historic Palazzo Turinetti in Piazza San Carlo.
Medieval remains and churches of a fraction on Sesia.

Common at the foot of the Campo dei Fiori, on the border with Gemonio, where the seventeenth-century mill in which was born and worked the painter Innocente Salvini (1889-1979) is from 1983 house-museum and picture gallery; in the hamlet Torre remain the ruins of a military tower probably of the 11th century and above Caldana, at Cerro, a path in the woods exhibits wooden sculptures.

Palace of the eighteenth century on the square, with the lion of San Marco frescoed on the walls, attributed to Pomponio Amalteo and sign of the long Venetian domination; gardens and stables are visited during Open Castles.
The Madonna del Capo.
Understand the history of the submerged country before seeing the bell tower.

In the apse of the former church of Sant'Antonio, today part of the Museo delle Orsoline, more than thirty polychrome terracotta statues bigger than the real made between 1541 and 1546 by the Abruzzo brothers James and Raffaele da Montereale; St. Joseph, Our Lady and Child are probably the work of the two masters, perhaps the rest of the workshop. St. Anthony and St. Brigid share a single façade on Piazza Mazzini. Visitable all year round.

Main city park, of about 400,000 m2, around the Royal Certosa: wide meadows, ornamental trees such as the Certosa horse chestnut, cedars, lindens and plane trees, and the Viali della Pace dedicated to figures such as Gandhi and Emmeline Pankhurst. They nest card, finches, robins and major red peaks; play areas, sports fields and dog area. Reachable by metro (stop Fermi).

Protected area on the slopes of Pratomagno, between the streams Resco and Ciuffenna, established to protect the Balze: ravines, escarpments and pillars shaped by erosion, warm tones and yellow, which Leonardo da Vinci painted in the background of some works. The most famous formations are the pillars of Poggitazzi and Piantravigne; from the village of Persignano you can admire the leaps around. In 2024 the site of the Pliocene and Pleistocene mammals of Valdarno entered among the GeoCollections of the IUGS.
The most important Egyptian museum after Cairo.
The convent museum.

On the banks of the Brescian Garda, with the medieval castle on the remains of a Roman castrum, the Renaissance Cathedral with the Last Supper of Tiepolo, the Old Port dominated by Palazzo Todeschini, one of the most important late antique villas in northern Italy and the Rambotti Museum with the oldest plow in the world; in the hamlet of San Martino della Battaglia the tower and the ossuary of 1859.
In the district of Favete, a few kilometers from the village, church founded in the 13th century after the visit of St. Francis to the nearby monastery of St. Urban.
Where was born one of the first navigable basins of Italy.
A record water jump, just in the summer.
The Spanish fortress over the country.
Golden sand and amenities for a comfortable day at the sea.
Country on a natural terrace overlooking the central valley, dominated by the ruins of the castle of Cly, one of the oldest in the Aosta Valley.
The residence of the Archduke on the sea.
MiC card does not show opening times: check before visiting

Tower of just over 10 meters square base, only surviving of the defensive-doganal system of Castrum Muscardum built in the middle of the thirteenth century where the valley narrows, to bar the road towards the Passo di Monte Croce Carnico (the tower on the opposite bank of the But was destroyed in 1840). Restored in 1993, it houses a Museo del Territorio with botanical garden; along the paths of access military works of the two wars. In 2026 open from Tuesday to Sunday 15-18 (from 10 to 23 August also 10-12).
The village of the viewers.
In the belly of the mountain, with speleological guides.

Rock monument hidden by vegetation under a rock wall, about 20 meters from the road to the abbey (335 m): pediment right by two columns, central niche and two cells, one with long side seat and the other square covered in barrels. It is believed to be the work of the monks of San Liberatore, used as graves or hermit cells.
Born in 1771 with the reform of the university wanted by Maria Teresa of Austria, since 2019 has a new path to Palazzo Botta that tells the natural world and the history of natural sciences.
the MiC card is closed every day during the hours; check opening on the mine site
With Santa Ninfa, Partanna preserves examples of rationalist and religious architecture of reconstruction after the earthquake of Belice, including the Mother Church designed by Paolo Di Stefano.

The origins date back to 1222, when Blessed Pietro Cathin, sent by Saint Francis, spread the Franciscan ideal there; the convent was rebuilt in 1380 and in 1441 passed to the Friars Minor. Between the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries lived the mystical Saint Humble. It preserves a crucifix carved by Fra Umile da Petralia, the marble statue of Our Lady of Graces (1537) attributed to the Gaggini, an organ of 1756 by Maurus Gallo and a painting by Saint Daniel martyr.

Already Ethno-anthropological Civic Museum, reopened with a new name on November 5, 2021, with the exhibition curated by Alessandra Aufiero. It tells the traditional agricultural and craft world: yokes and finishes, the corner of the blacksmith with zippers and locks, a bedroom rebuilt with rocking iron cradle, the sideboard and the tools for the oven, measures for the wheat and stadera, the corner of the shoemaker, traditional clothes and documents. It also hosts temporary exhibitions and workshops.
Alleys and steps of the bishop's city.
Out of curiosity about science.
Rectangular temple of the second century BC about on the highest point of the acropolis, of which two of the four Ionic columns of the front remain; it is well seen from the Gregorian Bridge.
Gagini, 15th century crucifix and Last Supper.

Inaugurated in 2006, it tells in chronological order the history of Massa Martana and its territory, with objects of productive activities, especially agricultural, and Roman finds from the excavations of the seventies and nineties of the twentieth century. Information: Tel. 075 889371.

One of the oldest settlements of the Diano Valley, on a promontory overlooking the valley: ancient center with double acropolis dominated by the castle, the Sanctuary of San Ciro on the temple of Cibele, the Archaeological Museum Elena D'Alto and, outside the village, the Sanctuary of the Colomba and the megalithic walls of the Serrone.
Inside the colossus.

In Fraciscio was born on 19 December 1842 Don Luigi Guanella; the house, built by his father in the first half of the nineteenth century and bought by the Guanelliani in 1948, preserves the room of family prayer, the native room and the study with the ceiling painted by the saint with a scene of paradise. Outside, a 2005 monument by Alfredo Vismara depicts Luigi with his sister Catherine.

From the sanctuary of the Fountain you can enjoy the view of the city and the Po's bend; along the bank you walk to the church of Santa Maria dell'Argine, and the Park of the Po and the Golena is indicated for cycling.
The 'camera of wonders' of the oldest university in the Western world.
The fortress belonged to Visconti, Alidosi and Riario Sforza; the museum winds through salt, walkways, mast and underground, where in 2005 an archaeological area emerged.
You can see it on a bike with Belriguardo and Verginese.

Museum of sacred art set up in the oratory of Our Lady (1600) and in the parish premises: liturgical silversmiths of Sardinian silversmiths (Cabras, Usay, Mamely) from the sixteenth century, a Gothic tower-timepiece, the Madonna of the Rosary of the sculptor Lonis, a painful Crucifix of the sixteenth century, a polychrome wooden Annunciation and numerous statues of the seventeenth century, as well as documents from the country church of San Sisinnio, the oratory of Sant'Efisio and the convent of the Mercedari. Open Saturday and Sunday 9-12 and 16-20; guided tours by reservation.
Medieval alleys a thousand meters.

The Diocesan Museum in the crypt with the lapidary from the Roman to the late Middle Ages, from which you reach the underground environments with the baptismal font of the sixth century; guided tours to the remains of Alba Pompeia.

A few kilometers away, in the Laga Mountains and in the National Park, spectacular gorges with paths between woods and waterfalls: the cave of Sant'Angelo with finds of the upper Paleolithic and Neolithic, the ruins of Castel Manfrino and the waterfall of Salinello or Caccamo; in the surrounding area also the hermitages of Santa Maria Scalena and Grotta di San Marco.
Fifteen trulli telling the city.

On the flat top of the rocky hill that dominates the ancient inhabited, with a quadrilateral plan with moat on two sides, masonry bridge and four corner towers (the oldest circular with a escarpment base); the first defenses date back to the Arabic period, then several times restored and expanded. On the same plateau, near the door, a cylindrical tower believed to be of Swabian age (XIII century); remains parts of the walls, renovated from the Aragonese to the Viceroyal Age, which until the nineteenth century enclosed the old town.
White rock for climbing and walking.
The Madonna found in the rocks of the river.
A neo-Medieval castle above the valley of the river Talla.
Started in 944, with facade and bell tower of the fourteenth century, in the Castle al Monte.
Garden with a path among about 500 spontaneous species of Apennine flora.
A labyrinth of alleys, steps, squares and stone houses overlooking the lake; in the heart of the center the lakefront and the marina with shops and bar overlooking the lake.

Borgo sul Metauro, home of the architect Donato Bramante, gathered around the bridge with three arches and the 24 m high medieval tower; the territory includes the hill of Montelce with the legendary tomb of Asdrubale and part of the Furlo Gorge.
The mountain vine.
Little Varallo.
The 14th-century Complaint of the Master of Santa Anastasia.

Of very ancient origins, born as a monastic cell at the time of San Colombano, rises about 1.3 km north of the village near the cemetery, in a panoramic position over the valley; the Romanesque bell tower preserves a bell of 1365. Along the road, above the Trebbia, a mill with two overlapping wheels.
Pass under a door of 2,400 years.
The twentieth century of Licini.
Walk through climbs and glimpses.
Mezzano's peasant life in a barn.
A square manor between the rice fields, the entrance door of the Oasis.
A break under the glass dome.

Borgo on a sandstone cliff about 780 meters between the valleys of Aso and Tenna, overlooking the Sibillini and the Laga Mountains: in the eighteenth century Palazzo Felici the Museum of fossils and minerals, then the ancient castle, medieval churches and, just outside, the monastery of San Giovanni in Selva.
The only place in Bologna to see sculptures by Michelangelo.
Along the Passirio, with the Wandelhalle decorated with South Tyrolean landscapes, the Post Liberty Bridge of 1909 and the statue of Sissi at the beginning of the Summer Walk.
It rises on a faraglione, on the 15 meters high rocks that bear the same name; from the sixteenth century it defended the country from the raids from the sea and served to spot the Saracen ships.

Parish church built between the 13th and 14th centuries, with an ancient tower of the walls transformed into a bell tower. Inside a Baptism of Jesus of the end of the sixteenth century with Castrum in the background and, in the middle of the ceiling, the Glory of St. Nicholas, trompe-l'œil that simulates the sky with saints, angels and God.
Church inside the walls that combines Romanesque and Baroque forms; in the former church is located the Pinacoteca municipale with a collection of paintings.

Establishment of the Municipality founded in 2001 for a permanent collection of contemporary art with an important section dedicated to Bruno Munari; since 2008 in the halls of a noble palace of the historic center (Firmian Palace according to the MiC), with temporary exhibitions in the Alpine territory between tradition and innovation and workshops. In 2026 open from Tuesday to Sunday in the afternoon.
The paths along the Gesso stream, reachable from the centre with the panoramic elevator of the Casa del Rijeka.
The prehistory of the Final.

The city was founded after the earthquake of 1693, which destroyed the nearby village of Occhiola: Prince Carlo Maria Carafa and Brother Michele da Ferla drew it hexagon around a large central square, with the Mother Church of San Michele and the Town Hall; the ruins of Occhiola are today an archaeological park.
A Lombard country house today municipal house.
A ring ride on the embankment with a view of the confluence of Ticino and Po.
Above Eianina, in an unspoiled area, today in ruins: it remains a rock chapel of the X-XI centuries where the Basilian monks withdrew.

Birthplace of Antonio Gramsci on the eastern slopes of Monte Arci, home to one of the smallest dioceses in Italy: the Baroque cathedral of San Pietro di Domenico Spotorno with the Diocesan Museum, the space dedicated to Gramsci di Giò Pomodoro and, in the hamlet of Zeppara, the Museum of traditional toy of Sardinia.
Goethe's masterpiece.
A high-altitude lake in the Mòcheni Valley.
The village of the fountains.

A natural corner hidden at the head of the Ridanna Valley: a scenic path, about one metre wide, starts from the Museum of the mines of Masseria and goes up through meadows, fir woods and moss along the Fernerbach, glacial stream, to the waterfalls. Bus 312 from Vipiteno, stop at Museo delle Mine.

Borgo della Valle Siciliana, the ancient Castrum Castanee fortified in the late Middle Ages: in the highest part of the village, on the ancient fortification, stands the church of San Pietro Martire, while isolated in the valley of the Mavone is Santa Maria di Ronzano, a Romanesque church of the twelfth century among the most original medieval monuments of Abruzzo, with frescoes of 1181.
The view of the valley of Elva.
On Piazza del Plebiscito, a Romanesque church transformed: in the façade a copy of the sarcophagus of Bella Galiana, inside the central part of a fourteenth-century triptych.
The Morin promenade between the centre and the sea is flanked by the park, where the cultural centre of the same name is located.
The processional coffers of Margliano.
Next to the Colosseum.
Walk through churches and palaces of the village.
The baroque altar of the village.
The fishing village of Sorrento.
The richest Roman collection in the province.
The treasures of the diocese of Salerno.
The main square, with the cathedral erected at the end of the thirteenth century from the neoclassical façade, still inaccessible after the earthquake of 2009.

One of the longest and most panoramic walks of Lake Iseo: from the panoramic staircase to the bridge of Via Roma, which connects Sarnico to Paratico, to the public gardens of Lazzarini near the historic center; the Garibaldi lakefront hosts Christmas markets.

The medieval wall, about 1200 meters long, preserves nine square towers. In the highest and oldest part of the village, with narrow and winding streets, stood the Fortress, of which today remains only the name of the alley of the Fortress; inside the walls there are the noble palaces Menchetti, Luzi Fedeli Gabuzzi and Pericoli.

Opened in 1999 on the second floor of the Doge's Palace as a scientific and didactic space that prepares for the visit of the reserve: it presents the natural heritage, landscape and culture of the Pianelle Park, Mediterranean ecosystem of the Murge between Massafra, Crispiano and Martina Franca.
Visitable only by reservation (Comune di Oneta 035 707117 or Fattoria Ariete di Gorno 347 3240391)
€7 full, €5 reduced (one ticket with the City Museum); Art Card with the Fellini Museum €14, reduced €10
The masterpiece of the martinese baroque, inside and outside.
One of the best preserved Roman arches.

Medieval tower, built between 1477 and 1479 to defend the village from the Turkish threat and recently restored; it is reached on foot from Via Cascina, in the area of Pra-Castello, and offers views of the city and the surrounding landscape.

Two halls in the sacristy of the parish of Saints Peter and Paul preserve about 500 works from churches and oratories of the high Valstrona, from the fifteenth century onwards: wooden sculptures, altars, crucifixes, relics, tabernacles, silver, silk vestments from the seventeenth century and paintings by local artists or donated by migrants. There are two pairs of golden and polychrome reliquary busts, a Virgin of the Pietà of the early eighteenth century carved into a single trunk and the former vows that recall the snowfall of 1888 and a shipwreck of migrants headed to America.
In Piazza della Madonna, baroque and completed in 1870, with ten chapels and numerous paintings by the Nasini family, including the Nativity of Mary by Giuseppe Nicola Nasini.

Comune del Seprio whose strategic position, at the time of the struggles between Torriani and Visconti, led to the construction of small defenses later became castles; today offers the castle of Jerago on its hill, stop of the regional tour of the Visconti castles, and a civic museum of natural history with free entry.
Catalan Gothic in a trachyte house.
See the Sibillini deer up close.
Madame Mère balcony.

In the seventeenth-century cloister of the ancient hospital, already a Dominican convent: sections of archaeology (covered from the 11th-VIII century BC to the Middle Ages), sacred art (two wooden altars from the churches of Sant'Antonio Abate and Santa Maria della Fratta, fragments of frescoes of the Tre-Quattrocento) and ethnography. Open Monday, Wednesday, Friday, Saturday and Sunday 8.30-12.30.
The peasant memory of the village, just re-arranged.
Wooden cabins and bridges at the back door.
The warrior's altarpiece in a hamlet church.

The highest and oldest part of the village, born as a strategic cornerstone: Santa Maria a Monte was the first military outpost of Valdarno and in 1327 yielded to the Florentine siege, which led to the construction of the current Fortress. From the area you can enjoy the view of the surrounding landscape.
The sixteenth-century complex on the square.

The oldest church in the village, in Romanesque-Lombard style: it houses paintings by Bernardino Campi and his school, three marble tiles from the fourteenth century and a palace of the main altar donated by Francesco I and woven in Paris.
City park known for the papyri pond and its botanical heritage.
Designed in 1715 by Agostino Ghiotti, today the seat of the Conservatory of music Francesco Venezze.
A crypt underneath the city.
The most authentic Florentine Valdarno.
The hamlet of the hospice.
Borgo della Lunigiana linked to chestnuts and shepherds, with the fourteenth-century castle and the arcade centre.
The most majestic of the Serenissima.
From the telegraph to the phone.
The medieval Ventimiglia water trough.

In the Court Priory-Gandin documents the ancient craftsmanship of the village, in particular the carpentry and the workshop of the bottai, certified in San Vito since the first fifteenth century. There are over 2,700 items from the life of the past: tableware, linen and household utensils, tools for breeding and agriculture, for masons and shoemakers, tools for weaving and spinning; a library keeps documents and photographs on the local crafts and the wine cellar the objects for the production of wine.

In the third stable of the castle, opened in 1998 and expanded in 2006 and 2018: finds of the Lomellina from prehistory to the seventh century, including Roman glass, the tomb of a warrior of Valeggio and a treasure of about 1,400 coins.
The frescoed Passion.

Cava of limestoneite that provided the column rocks for the temples of Selinunte, at 11-12 km; the work suddenly interrupted in 409 BC with the Carthaginian siege and the blocks remained where they were: over sixty cylindrical boulders and a rough capital. Visited by Jean-Pierre Houel between 1776 and 1779, in 1999 he received the international award "Carlo Scarpa" (Carlo Scarpa). Open from 9 am to 1 pm; in the afternoon only by reservation for groups of at least 20 people.
Built in 1956 for the Winter Olympics in Cortina, it is a covered facility with ice rink open in winter and summer, equipment rental, bar, solarium and baby park.
The fortified bridge.

Museum of the publishing house Rubbettino, born in 1972 from an idea of Rosario Rubbettino, who left the post of secretary of middle school: the first book, of philosophy, was printed entirely with lead, and in 1976 the first plant was born. The museum tells the story of the book in Calabria, from the processing of paper pulp to printing and bookbinding, and hosts conferences, seminars and festivals.

Facade of the first decades of the seventeenth century with four semi-pillars and tympanum, where in 1958 Giovanni Botti of Domodossola painted the Assumption during the restoration. The bell tower, about 26 meters high and detached from the church, was reopened in 2019 after the earthquake damage of 2012.
Casa Lawrence is a historic residence, the source does not indicate if it is visitable

Itinerary on foot or by bike of 14 km (50 m of difference in altitude), almost all on dirt road, along the left bank of the Cordevole da Bribano al Sasso di San Giorgio, with extension to the bridge of Tappole. It takes its name from the ancient roges, the network of channels that fed sawmills, mills, forges and a paper mill; along the path explanatory panels. Medium difficulty, suitable for families; not recommended during and immediately after bad weather.
The holiday residence of the Savoy, a UNESCO World Heritage Site, with its large romantic park and the neo-Gothic Margaria complex.
The top from which you can read the whole throat.

Built in the 13th century after the decline of the dominion of the monks of Sant'Eutizio, he saw the troops of Frederick II (1227), Charles of Anjou (1265), Braccio da Montone and Francesco Sforza passing through and was equipped with towers; the fourteenth-century semi-cylinder tower of the Fabbi family remains.
Four mounded tombs of the middle of the 7th and 6th century BC, at the foot of the hills of the Alma Valley; reachable only on foot, with information panels.
The channel designed by Leonardo to connect it to the Navigli network, now a cycle path to the Adda.
The most beautiful temple to nuragic well.

The San Marco salami, of quality pork meat with a recipe that according to some dates back to Normans; macaroni with tegamino, dishes made of black pork Nebrodi, tuma, ricotta and pecorino cheese, lettuces of fried bread paste, biscuits with milk and vermouth, accompanied by the alettine wine.
The city on the water they call "Garden of the Serenissima" .
The bronze door is rebuilt.
Laboratorio founded in 1908 by Alice and Leopoldo Franchetti for the hand weaving of linen, still active, with nine rooms of fabrics, yarns and vintage frames.

Città dei Signori da Correggio e patria del pittore Antonio Allegri: porticos of corso Mazzini, the Renaissance Palazzo dei Principi with the Redeemer of Mantegna, the Basilica of San Quirino and the Asioli Theatre.

Litorale mostly of white pebbles, with small sandy coves towards the mouth of Sangro, free and equipped beaches and waters awarded with the Blue Flag; the small Gulf of Venus opens under the abbey promontory, between brooms, fennel, orange groves and olive groves that reach almost the sea.

A rural church dating back to the 13th century in the locality Colleguidone-Casale, outside the village: the Gothic portal is dated 1315 and has a relief with the crucifixed Lamb, and on the stone walls remain graffiti of travellers and shepherds transhumant from the 17th century to the mid 19th century. The side bell tower could be of Norman age; inside a medieval fresco of the Annunciation and the semicircular apse.

In 1278 Bear Orsini tore Vasanello from the Church and built a first fortification on a falisco-Roman bastion; the fief then returned to the Orsini and in 1489, for the wedding of Orsino Orsini, was commissioned the first cycle of frescoes, probably linked to the workshop of the Pinturicchio, enriched in 1505 with references to the Della Rovere. Passed to the Colonna and in 1700 to the Colonna-Barberini of Sciarra, in 1907 it was purchased by Monsignor Luigi Misciattelli, whose heirs still own it; in 1946 the ancient stables became a ceramic factory, closed in 1978. A spiral staircase leads to a panoramic point.
The life of the fishing port.
Set up in the ancient dairy farm of Cerano, it collects the historical tools of milk processing (churches, conga, wrap and a culdera) and offers a film of the eighties on traditional crafts.

The Italian garden of Vanvitelli with meadows, pools, fountains and waterfalls fed by the Carolino Aqueduct: the Via d'Acqua culminates in the Torrione and the Grande Cascata; in the Bosco Vecchio la Peschiera grande and the Castelluccia.
Closed from 14 December 2026 to all January 2027, reopened scheduled to February 2027 with date to be defined

Romanesque church about 2 km from the Fortress of Montevarmine, next to which in the first half of the 11th century arose a Benedictine monastery today disappeared; from the 14th century it was a destination of pilgrimages for the indulgences granted by the bishops of Fermo and strategic point on the road between Ascoli, Fermo and the Aso valley.

Eighteen domus de Janas multicellular excavated in the limestone of the southern slope of Monte Mamas, divided into two groups by an ancient tracturo and used by the Neolithic final to the middle Bronze; the tombs I and II have twelve rooms each and the decorations reproduce elements of the neolithic huts. From 12 July 2025, he was one of the 17 members of the UNESCO Domus de Janas website.

Ring for families around the ancient basin of Lake Kummer, about 1,340 m near Corvara, linked to a local legend: 11.6 km with eight educational stations on the history of the lake and its territory, starting from the Bunker Mooseum (1,007 m). Not suitable for strollers and wheelchairs.
A quiet oasis just a stone's throw from San Marco.
Como and its origins, from prehistory to medieval age, in a noble building, Palazzo Giovio; it also affers the archaeological area of the Porta di Como Romana.

On top of a rock reachable by narrow alleys, with views of the valley between Verbicaro and Grisolia, it is considered the oldest monument of the village. The frescoes, covered with lime, re-emerged in the eighties and were restored by the Superintendence: St. Mark and St. Leonard, dated 1539 and commissioned by Donna Domenica De Donato, a Pietà, a Madonna with Child and a cycle of the XIV-XV centuries with saints and Madonnas; inside a small wooden statue of the Madonna enthroned.

National and regional river port from which the motorboats start on the Po; in spring and summer, on request, cruises to Mantua. In the Lido Po area the Big Bench, inaugurated in 2023, of the project of Chris Bangle; along the river passes the cycle path towards Gualtieri and Brescello.

Municipality of the upper Val Torre, Slovenian language and culture, in part in the Julian Prealps Natural Park: the Caves of Villanova, discovered in 1925, the Ethnographic Museum in the former dairy, the Pian dei Cyclamini and the nature trails of the Park.
A complete example of Lombardy farmhouse of the Lower Milanese.
Historical scientific instruments in Piazza della Repubblica.
A Roman agricultural villa overlooking the lakes.
One of the few churches that survived 1694.

only guided tours (about 90 minutes, departures 11 and 15.30, closed on Monday, groups minimum 6 people) from mid-March to early November, I meet at the office Promobellagio in the tower of Piazza della Chiesa
A surprising village.

The village preserves the medieval system: four districts of stone houses, alleys, steps and towers. It was surrounded by walls with 13 semi-circular towers; the five doors remain, open in the morning and closed at sunset: Portella, Porta San Pietro, Porta San Giovanni, Porta di Tocco and Porta Riore.
Marbles and shovels in a church of Byzantine origin.

Wide sandy beaches with dunes and Mediterranean tomboli of maquis, between two pine forests towards Marina di Cecina and Marina di Castagneto; Blue flag, equipped and free stretches, dog area, path accessible from Piazza degli Anemoni and a bike path of 5 km in pine forest to Cecina Mare.
A walk along the canal.
The ruins of the medieval village erased from the earthquake.
steep alleys and views of the Serra d'Ivrea.
The Romanesque-Gothic parish at the end of the greenway.
Typical medieval plant, grown around the castle within the walls, on a ridge of tuff between the valleys of Chiarano and Mola.

Historic house near the parish with over a thousand objects, tools and machines of craftsman and farmer work between the nineteenth and twentieth centuries, including a shoemaker shop and a corner of weaving.
Fossils and rare minerals in a 14th century palace.
From the village start numerous paths that cross thick woods up to the highest and most rugged ridges, habitat of the rare pine loricato, symbol of the park.
The village lies between three rocks, the Castle, the Piesco and the Madonna della Rocca, overlooking the river Melandro; in the historic center there are over 500 murals, which increase every year.
The park warden's case.
Churches with domes covered with majolica; in the church of San Giacomo have been recently discovered frescoes of a cycle attributable to the Giottesca school.
The symbol of the village, reborn after the earthquake.
Church known for the frescoes of the Sienese school and for a polyptych of the sixteenth century.
Two castles and three thousand years of history on the same back.

Locality at 1,260 meters at the northern end of Valcamonica, where the Oglio was born, connected by cable car to the Passo del Tonale and defined in 1912 by the Touring  the first Italian resort of tourism and winter sports.The village, destroyed by the Austro-Hungarian bombing of 27 September 1917, preserves the Baroque church of the Holy Trinity with the sacred art museum, while the hamlets rise towards the Stelvio Park, the Houses of Viso and the Passo di Gavia.
The city disappeared over the lake.
The daily life of the Roman metropolis.
A church suspended in the rock.

A stop in the green towards Lanusei.
The oldest monument of Abruzzo of the year 1000 remained almost intact.
A green break between statues and fountains in the center.
The shape of the castle above the confluence of Tanaro and Bormida.

karst area of more than four square kilometers around 900-1000 meters, made of meadows, wetlands, sinkholes, springs, caves and ditches; there is no permanent lake, but in winter the water is collected in the sinkholes in small pools often frozen. In the summer better go in the late afternoon, because there is little shade; the services at altitude can be limited.
From the woods to the pastures to a panoramic summit.

Built in the middle of the sixteenth century for Cardinal Guido Ascanio Sforza, camerlengo and governor of Proceno, demolishing the ancient town hall; on the door remains his coat of arms. His brother Paul, Marquis of Proceno, completed it with a chapel and loggia on the valley of Paglia, largely lost in the collapses of 1873 and 1890. Purchased by the Municipality in 1985 and restored, it preserves frescoed vaults attributed to the school of Taddeo and Federico Zuccari, a coffered ceiling and a courtyard with a travertine well; it houses exhibitions and conferences.
The visitor center on the Roman Rimini, meeting point of the great consular roads Flaminia, Emilia and Popilia.
Bagheria's home.
The old mill of the city.

fifteenth-century house of the Venetian podestà, purchased at auction in 1906 by Senator Ugo Da Como from Bresciano and restored by architect Antonio Tagliaferri. It preserves antique furniture, pharmacy vases, ceramics, paintings, private studio and the Red Room, and a library of over 50,000 volumes, among the largest private collections in Northern Italy, with the smallest book in the world (pages 15 x 9 mm). Admission fee.
times and prices of the source maybe not updated, check on navigareladda.it
The spectacular straight road that from the foot of the hill rises to the square of Palazzo Farnese.
The elliptical design of the medieval village.
Legends of witches in a mountain village.

Church founded in 1744 by the mining owner Michael von Jenner, in an extraordinary landscape; to see the altarpieces of Franz Sebald Unterberger, painter of Val di Fiemme. It is privately owned and the entrance fee is charged; you ask not to enter the fenced meadows. From the bus stop Ranui 5 minutes walk; parking fee.
The view from the tower of the legend of witches.

Coastal village west of Palermo, probably of late medieval origin, with a historic center of low and white houses along straight roads that go down to the sea; on the seafront Palazzo d'Aumale houses the Regional Museum of Natural History and the permanent exhibition of the Sicilian cart, while to the west the reserve of Cape Rama and Cala Rossa close the coast.
The tools of those who left the country.
The village with its peperino houses, to be visited before the Sacro Bosco, tasting the cookie of Sant'Anselmo.

The oldest villa in Stresa, built by the Bolongaro family around 1770, was the residence of the philosopher Antonio Rosmini from 1850 to 1855; the Study Centre can be visited includes the Rosminian Museum, Rosmini's room and the park. In via Manzoni there is the monument to friendship between Manzoni and Rosmini (1932), with crucifix and bas-relief by Pietro Canonica.
Where the river of Rome is born.

Borgo del Montefeltro among the most beautiful villages in Italy, 600 meters on a spur above the valley of the Conca, once disputed between the Montefeltro of Urbino and the Malatesta of Rimini: historic center with spiral with the fifteenth-century civic tower, Palazzo Massaioli and the neoclassical San Silvestro; the thermal baths fed by the waters of Mount San Paolo are now temporarily closed.
Envers municipality on the right of the Dora, with the ancient millstone quarry and ollar stone pots of Valmeriana.
The clothes of the fifteenth century unique in the world.

Made by the Alpine Rescue of Varallo with the Alpine Guides of Alagna, it has two routes: the Partusacc, ring to Mount Tovo, and the most challenging Falconera, signposted by Civiasco with path 636. At the opening of the night lighting in 2020, it was presented as the first European ferrata equipped with a lighting system.
A town founded by the Carthaginians at the end of the 5th century BC by the pond of Santa Maria, frequented by flamingos; then occupied by the Romans, who built baths, cisterns and roads.
The oldest memory of the Christian faith in Santhià.
The basilica of Blessed Angelo.
17th century frescoes and ex-vote in a country sanctuary.

On the large promontory above the city you can visit the excavations of ancient Finziade, with houses of Hellenistic age, and the castle born as a Aragonese signal tower, from which you can enjoy the view of the coast. Open Monday-Saturday 9-13, Sunday and holidays closed.
Great machine of industrial archaeology, once among the largest forging presses in Europe.
The 15th-century Madonna and the party shared with Vallata.

The polygonal tower of the 11th century, struck by lightning in 1718 and then restored, is the only remnant of the original castle and symbol of the village; the eighteenth-century palace next to it, simple and linear, follows the fan-shaped shape of the tower and preserves a cistern of 30 cubic meters for the rainwater connected to a stone fountain at the entrance.
The Greek colony of Metauros through its necropolis.

Attached to the Park Visitor Centre in the main square, it presents the environments and caves of the eastern side of Majella, from high altitudes to rocky walls, to moors, gorges and underground environments, with photos, illustrations, panels and natural finds; it reconstructs a pastoral cave with the habitat of the yellow-bellyed ululon, rare amphibian, and an audiovisual panel makes you listen to the songs of the birds of the Park. It is the starting point for the Valley of Santo Spirito and the green springs.
The works of Claudio Ridolfi in the medieval low town.
We'll her in the rock on the path of the Spirit.
An agricultural village born from the monastery.
The medieval heart.
The church designed by Lelio Orsi.

In the park's headquarters, it documents the research of the Agency with about 700 European and non-European birds, of which 140 can be observed in the park as sedentary or pass species; other sections on forest botanical, morphology of the territory and entomology. Visits by reservation (tel. 011 4320011).
Monteu's baroque, born again after the Spanish fire.
A fifteenth-century universal judgment along the Wanderer.
Stop at the Angel Quadrivio to see it in a glimpse.
A guided tour or a work.
seasonal opening: Sundays from mid-April to mid-October and every day from July 26 to August 31 (calendar 2026)
Alleys, squares and noble palaces of the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries; with the Long Tower of the Arabs, the Byzantine walls and the Aragonese Master Tower.

In the district of Cacorzo, near the snowfields, dovecote of the late fifteenth century defined the largest and most severe of the Salento peninsula; on the lintel of the gate the coats of arms of Balzo and Balzo-Acquaviva.

The first settlement, the fortified citadel called "the castle" rose in the early Middle Ages, perhaps on a Roman settlement: Basilian monks founded a monastery around the sixth century, then Longobards and Normans fortified it. Walls and much of the town were destroyed after the French attack of 1806 and few ruins of fortified houses remain.
The Romanesque church on the hill above San Vigilio.
Fire bombs picked at the counter.
The life of the Carthusians told inside the first Charterhouse of Italy.
The factory of the first light bulb of Cruto.
