The great bronze of the battle of 1860.
The historic ascent to the plateau.
The sacred and fortified heart of the colony.
The easiest view of the country.
The Venetian hydraulic work that designed the modern delta.

Designed by Francesco da Volterra in 1598, it preserves a canvas by Giuseppe Maria Crespi and an Annunciation by Pietro Rotari; it overlooks Piazza Garibaldi, whose center is the octagonal oratory of the Madonna della Concezione (1579), next to the church of the Capuchins (1673).

Sunny village of the hinterland of the Golfo Paradiso, about 15 minutes drive from the Riviera, with the motto "janua patet" in the coat of arms: here is the historic factory of Trebino tower clocks, with its museum, and the Romanesque parish church of Sant'Ambrogio.

In the birthplace of historian Carlo Botta (1766-1837), born from the passion of Giuseppe Dorma in the eighties and inaugurated in 1997, he tells with more than 1,600 finds the agricultural and artisan life of the country: tools, rebuilt environments, vintage clothes, the curious "raddrizza-corna" and two original specimens of the soundproofing machine by Antonio Michela, of which an updated version is still used in Parliament. Open on public holidays, in weekdays by appointment; it is part of the AMI museum network.
The cappuccino cloister with the well.
An open-air museum with views of half of Sardinia.
Where Alberoni was baptized.
An open-air art gallery, always open.

17th century church in pseudo-Renaissance style, with inlaid coffered ceiling. On the high altar in golden wood, a Madonna with the Renaissance Child in Carrara marble from the Gaginesque school (XV-XVI century); behind the altar a paschal candle made from a column with Byzantine capital of the 12th century. Pulpito di Giuseppe Licastro e Giuseppe Ascrizzi (1886), statues by Saverio Scutellà (1820) and Raffaele Angelo Musitano (1877), a Sorrowful Sculptor Ferdinando Perathoner from the Garden; on the façade statues by Elia and Moses by Domenico Papalia.

Small village walled on the Livenza, dominated by the municipal tower and closed by the doors Friuli and Trevisana; around the square overlooking Dogana, Monte di Pietà and Loggia of Venetian age, the Duomo born from a synagogue and the house of Gaia da Camino, cited by Dante, with frescoes fourteenth century.
Lodi's porched living room.
On the trail of Monteverdi.
The fossils of one of the oldest flying reptiles.
Mountain of Sila Small with picnic areas and a panorama that embraces both the Ionian Sea and the Tyrrhenian Sea; in the locality of Latteria, about 1,600 meters, is the Leo Grandinetti refuge.
Walking through the chestnut trees.
The peasant house where a holy pope was born.
The story of the book told by a village publisher.
Municipality of the Gulf of Poets with the seaside village of Tellaro, among the most beautiful villages in Italy, the castle of San Giorgio, Palazzo Doria and the houses of Shelley and artists.
The remains of the castle that once controlled the bay.

Ring of about 13 km (455 m of difference in altitude, between 1,127 and 1,540 m) that goes down from the center beyond the church to the farm Ebner, goes up forest roads to the saddle of Cisa, passes the farm Pausa and reaches the Krabes mountain hut, recommended stop with panoramic view and local specialties; the return runs along a biotope.

Among the most important prehistoric sites in the world for the study of Neanderthal's man: here in 1939 the skull was found known as the Circeo Man, about 60,000 years ago; the excavations returned about ten adult individuals and remains of elephants, rhinos, hippopotamuses, deer and hyenas (between 50,000 and 100,000 years ago). The visit route includes a virtual reality experience with the cave as it was 60,000 years ago and fossil holograms.

The bell tower and the Mayor capilla with star vault survived the renovation of the late seventeenth century that gave it a neoclassical appearance; in the eighteenth century it was enriched with furnishings, including the main altar. On the churchyard forms a triangle with the oratory of Our Lady with loggia and the oratory of the Souls.
Lake in a volcanic crater, which the ancients considered the entrance to Hades, with Roman remains along the banks.

Val Nure village at 329 meters, formed by two villages on the sides of the stream, San Bernardino and San Giovanni, traditionally linked to the family of Christopher Columbus: the tower-museum of Pradello, the statue in Piazza Colombo, the sanctuary of Our Lady of Quercia and the Farnese tower.
The best way to understand Lucca, even with children.

In the district of Vigo, built in the second half of the sixteenth century: under the presbytery opens, through a hatch, a Romanesque crypt of the tenth century. Inside six altars in local marble and a seventeenth-century organ by Giovanni Bertè.
In the footsteps of Dante exile.

Medieval village on the slopes of the Morrone, gate of the Majella National Park, dominated by the towers of the castle Caldora-Cantelmo; in the center the churches of Santa Maria Maggiore and San Marcello, outside the walls the convent of Minors Observing with the frescoed cloister.
The Etruscan city in nature.

The Palazzo del Marquis, called Trasmondi by the last feudal lords, dates back to the fifteenth century and lies in the center of the village; the north gate, the most interesting of the two doors of the earth, was placed on the palace, which once closed at night or in case of danger.

Sanctuary of the Bronze Age of about 7 hectares with 15 hypogeans, where more than 3000 years ago they practiced rituals of fertility, death and rebirth; later the rooms were re-used as tombs of the warrior elite. The Ipogeum of the Bronzes (discovered in 1987) and that of the Avori (2001) can be reached from a ramp and a corridor that leads to a room with a dome vault. There are about 200 burials: jewels in the female tombs, swords, daggers and arrowheads in the male ones, in addition to the burial called "Lady of the Ambres." Guided tours, including evenings, and experimental archaeology workshops are provided.

Medieval village in the Tiber River Park, documented since 1235 as a castle of the lords of Baschi: the church of San Nicolò di Ippolito Scalza with the polyptych of Giovanni di Paolo, the Antiquarium and the archaeological area of Scoppieto with the Roman ceramic factory, the Ovoteca di Civitella del Lago and the lake of Corbara.
The Football Stairway.
With Montegrotto, it forms the largest thermal resort in Europe: more than one hundred establishments with mud and healing baths, in waters rich in beneficial minerals.
An outdoor museum little known by tourists, with guided tours theme.

Civic museum dedicated to the battle of Castelfidardo, in which the Sabaud troops defeated the papal army opening the way to the annexation of Marche and Umbria to the Kingdom of Sardinia; the collection is set up in the halls of Palazzo Ciriaco Mordini and the visit is completed with the places of battle.
The oldest mentioned church in the old town.
The 16th century view of Randazzo.
The plazas of the castle disappeared.
The medieval monastery built on Roman temples.
The Longobards of Piceno.

The ancient coast submerged by bradisism: about 7 meters deep in front of Punta Epitaffio a nymph of the Claudia age, the remains of a villa attributed to the Pisoni and the 'villa with entrance to protiro , with mosaic floors, destination of divers.

Municipality of the Modena plain gathered around the castle, fortified by Modena in 1201 and reshaped by the Pio di Carpi since 1405, today museum with archaeological park; in the territory, rich in more than 80 villas and residences, Villa Gandini with the Resistance Park and the parish church of San Giacomo di Colombaro.

City of Alto Milanese with the Civic Museum Guido Sutermeister, which collects archaeology and local history in a 1928 building inspired by a fifteenth-century residence, and the Torre Colombera, a hunting casino of the Lampugnani of the mid-15th century with Renaissance frescoes.
Exhibition center inaugurated in 2016 in the Caravex house, with exhibitions on local and international crafts.
Acceptura is located in the heart of the regional park, at the foot of the rocky peaks of the Little Lucane Dolomites; the territory offers views, walks and the possibility to observe the fauna.
Gaudenzio Ferrari.
The watchman on the valley.
Late medieval and Renaissance frescoes.
The longest cave in Friuli, with an underground natural arch.
The Sassoferrato at his house.
The Genoese and the Malosso in the mother church of the country.
The large square at the north entrance of the city and the church of Santa Maria del Popolo, at the beginning of Via del Corso, Via del Babuino and Via di Ripetta.

The ancient piazza of the port and market, one of the most beautiful of Lake Iseo, opens on the lakefront of about 2 km walkable; next there is the marina, one of the largest of the European lakes, from which to leave by boat or sailing boat.

The square of red bricks was erected between the end of the XII and the first decades of the XIII century by the Municipality of Treviso on an existing embankment: about 17 meters high and about 230 meters long per side, with towers at the corners and in the midway points, escaped the demolitions of the nineteenth century and among the best preserved in Italy. Under the vault of the Civic Tower the coat of arms with the Carraresi chariot; in the evening the walls are illuminated.

Renaissance building built by Alessandro Sforza in the mid-15th century on a Malatestan nucleus and completed by the Dukes of Urbino, with a portico of six arches; today it is the seat of the Prefecture.

In the neo-Gothic building of the 1920s, connected to the Lia Museum by a steel and glass gallery: about 1,500 seals from ancient Egypt, Rome, Pre-Columbian America and the Far East, from the fourth millennium BC to today.
The cathedral with the 9th century crypt.

The oldest church of Vico, on a hill next to the castle: stone portal with date 1657, three naves and eleven altars, including that of San Valentino, patron since 1618 celebrated on February 14; quadrangular bell tower and dome with ribs.
The church of Giulia Farnese with paintings from the Zuccari school.

Municipality of the Piacenza plain, about 24 km from Piacenza and close to the Verdi lands, known for the fifteenth-century castle of the Counts Barattieri, which houses the MIM contemporary art museum and copies of the warriors of Xi'an, and for the church of San Pietro of 1522.

After the 1779 fire that destroyed it almost completely, the village was rebuilt in Hispano-Moorish style, influenced by the eighteenth-century migrants returned from the Iberian peninsula. The parish church of San Gottardo dates back to the 17th century; at the gates of the village the oratory of San Rocco houses an altar in marble of the eighteenth century. The village is a stop on the Way of San Carlo between Orta and Varallo for the Passo della Colma.
A chapel of Our Lady built in 1112 became parish church in 1170; rebuilt in 1499-1515 and again in 1894-1899 in late Dogotic style according to the design of the Viennese architect Weber.
Made by Paolo Vitelli in the sixteenth century, with internal frescoes of Emilian school; at the end of the garden the Palazzina Vitelli with a frescoed loggia.
The Roman cistern under a Gothic church.

Collegiate of the 13th century, born as a cemetery church outside the walls, with the massive bell tower on the façade and the portal to sharp sixth of the fourteenth century; under the porch the fresco of San Cristoforo painted by Andrea Delitio in 1473. The interior was transformed in 1706 into baroque forms.
The citadel of Frederick II on the Table.
At the entrance of the Arsenale: models of ships, nautical instruments and memorabilia of sunken or disused units, with the room dedicated to Guglielmo Marconi and the Polene room.
Introduction to the nature and traditions of the valley.
Symbol of the city in Piazza della Libertà, with a four-dial clock that marks moon phases, now astronomical, days and months.
A village without car with view of Lake Piediluco.
The village at heart, alley after alley.
High 45 meters on the center designed by Marcello Piacentini with Giuseppe Quaroni; dedicated in 1921 to the fallen of the Great War, it was inaugurated on October 27, 1924.
Guided tour €13
The seventeenth-century convent, now home to the GeoMuseum; the adjoining church houses wooden statues and sculptures from the fifteenth to the nineteenth century.

Since the twelfth century of the Prince Bishops of Trento, it was the seat of the bishop's captain of the Judicarians and their summer residence: a set of buildings of different eras, from the New Palace of the beginning of the thirteenth century to the Medieval Old Palace, transformed in part from the fifteenth century into a Renaissance residence with loggias, double-fores and triple-fores, enlarged in the sixteenth century by Bernardo Clesio. You can visit the chapel of San Martino with frescoes from the thirteenth century, the Judgment Room, the Bozone Tower called "Torre della Fame" (Torre della Fame), with the dark prison accessible from a trapdoor, and the provincial collections of inlaid furniture, weapons, paintings and applied arts, as well as an archaeological section. The castle also appears in the Cycle of the Months of Torre Aquila in Trento.
Finds and fossils of the territory between Agno and Chiampo.
The castle of the Baron Conspiracy.
The churches on the cliff.
Woods and great fauna of the Garfagnana.
The street of the painted buildings.

Inaugurated in 1980 in the cells of the former Dominican convent next to the church. The medieval section, born from the collection of the Sangineto, preserves the "San Ladislao" by Simone Martini (1326), two tables by Bernardo Daddi (1328), french alabaster plates of the fourteenth century and the "Madonna delle Pere" by Paolo di Ciacio; the Dominican one painted by saints of the order, the "Madonna di Trapani" (about 1650), silver, vestments and illuminated codes.

Inaugurated in 2007 and curated by historian Marco Pascoli, with bilingual Italian-German imprint, it is dedicated to the battle of Ragogna after Caporetto: panels and vintage images, a large plastic of the battlefield with trenches and sides at 31 October 1917, objects recovered on battlefields, a section on Risorgimento and Second World War and a multimedia room. Open Tuesday, Thursday, Saturday and Sunday 15.30-18 according to the Municipality.
A perched village to walk up to the tower.
The oldest church in the village, on the lake.
Medieval and Baroque frescoes in the village.
With three sighting towers and baroque bell tower.
Italy's largest inland swamp, reserves for thousands of birds: over 190 species to observe.
A church born on a mosque.
The Liberty in the center of Giarre.
according to Let's Marche historical center, monuments and municipal museums are only partially usable: inquire before the visit
Church of the village dating back to the fifteenth century.

Documented in this place from 1385, with Romanesque bell tower fourteenth century, it was almost rebuilt between 1470 and 1529, enlarged in 1684 and completed with dome and apse in 1927-1929 by engineer Bartolomeo Gallo. It preserves the bezel with eight apostles painted in 1537 by Fermo Stella da Caravaggio, the altarpiece of San Giorgio that kills the school dragon of Defendente Ferrari, a Madonna enthroned by the Spanish school, the main altar with marble balustrade (1752) and the urn of San Vitale donated in 1776 by Cardinal delle Lanze. Free entry during functions.
Mountain life told by objects.

Documentation centre opened in 1994 in the east wing of the noble floor of the castle: it collects more than one hundred decorative motifs of the plaster ceilings of the Piedmontese peasant houses, the oldest dated 1580, with salt on the extraction of the plaster, its uses in the construction and finds of the peasant life.
Sparkling water from the fountains of the village.
The triangular living room of Offida.
A Romanesque church in the center.

In the territory passes one of the main aqueducts of the area, dated to 144-130 BC and attributed to the Pretore Quinto Marcio Re; there are also traces of the Via Valeria Vetus, which climbed for Cineto Romano, Roviano and Riofreddo.
Giottesque frescoes in a Norman tower.

Founded in the early twenties of the twentieth century by the collector Goffredo Bellini in the Palazzo Monte dei Pegni. Archaeology from the Bronze Age to the Roman Age, with Celtic furnishings of the necropolis of Carzaghetto, Egyptian stele of the Middle Kingdom and Attic Kylix; incunabula and aldine, the Atlas Veneto of Coronelli (1690), sections on popular traditions, Risorgimento and Great War, painters of the nineteenth century and the life-size copy of the Assedio di Asola is attributed to Tintoretto (victory of 1516). Section of about 600 minerals visible on request.

Ethnographic museum founded in 1982 by Fr Federico Scanziani, parish priest of Cavargna from 1957 to 2004, to preserve traditions, customs and culture of the valley. The sections tell the magnans, itinerant ponders with their tools and the box "trida" , the traditional costume of the late nineteenth century, the life of the peasant-pastor, the woodsmen, the smuggling, the ancient mines and the iron workmanship and the cult of St. Lucy; the section of popular religiosity exhibits wooden statues of the eighteenth century, a monstrance of Ambrosian rite and vestments in part from the old parish of St. Lawrence.
The fifteenth-century parish church in the historic centre.
Sources and woods overlooking the Basilicata.

Rebuilt from 1772 after the demolition of the original church in 1650; Count Giuseppe Provana financed side arms and choir, which gave her the Latin crossed plant. Today it is a unique hall with four side chapels and preserves eighteenth century wooden works by Stefano Maria Clemente.

12th century castle with its medieval village, now an old restored village that houses a resort; the gate of the castle is always open to visitors. It is reached by climbing for about a kilometer from the dirt road that passes from the Laghetto di Sasso.
Romanesque, 11th century frescoes and views of the Moorish amphitheatre.
Reed and asphodel toys to try with your hands.

Next to the church built in 1969 there is the ancient romoratory, which the Municipality dates back to the third century and describes as an early Christian oratory of the Atellan era, considered the tomb of the saint before the transfer to Acerenza; on the façade a fresco of the Madonna delle Grazie between St. Elpidio and St. Nicholas. The interior has been almost entirely restored; the hermitage is open to the faithful in the week after Easter.
The mother church of the village, consecrated in 1590.
The Venetian painting is complete.

On the highest hill of the Volsini, overlooking Lake Bolsena along Cassia and Francigena: the Rocca dei Papi, the dome of Santa Margherita and the double church of San Flaviano, land of the East! East! East!!!.
Mandatory for Teatro Anatomico and Stabat Mater
A fifteenth-century chapel all painted.

Under the city a network of galleries of more than nine kilometers on several levels, dug and re-used for centuries for water, food and shelter, with air wells and light; in the guided path of the Cantinone religious figures and symbols and daily life, and the names engraved during the Second World War. Guided tour of less than an hour.
Village at the entrance of the Val d'Ayas dominated by the cubic castle of the Challant on a spur of rock.
The only valley in the region with a small salt deposit, up to Bivacco Borroz; on top the small church of Notre-Dame-de-la-Neige.

Ancient monastery of Byzantine rite in the hamlet Pattano, probably founded between the 8th and the middle of the 10th century: a document from 993 already shows it owner of vast lands up to Ceraso. It flourished between the 11th and 14th centuries under Longobards, Normans and Angioini thanks to the Greek monks, then decayed and after the papal investigation of 1458 was suppressed and entrusted to commendatory abbots.
The nineteenth-century parish church that houses a crucifix painted on a table, signed and dated 1396, by the painter Camerte Olivuccio di Ceccarello (Carlo da Camerino).

Designed by Guglielmo Cremonese and built between 1472 and 1514 on a Gothic church of the fourteenth century, of which remains the presbytery; it is home to a nullius prelature. Pulpito and organ case are decorated by Romanino with scenes from the Old Testament and an Ecce Homo; the organ Serassi is from 1825. At the center of the presbytery is the Polyptych of Mercy inlaid polychrome wood, 27 tables by A. della Corna, gift of the Serenissima.
A dead volcano with a castle on top.
A Rococo Colonna jewel.
The garden of the Habsburg holiday.
Etruscan tombs in the cliff.
A Roman pottery factory on the Tiber.

Country of vineyards north of Bressanone, sheltered from the north winds and marked by the noble residences of the bishop's officers; in the hamlet of Novacella stands the Augustinian Abbey founded in 1142, one of the major monasteries of Tyrol, in the northernmost wine area of Italy.
Hypogeic necropolis of culture Ozieri with five graves; the most important has seven sculpted taurine protomes.
The 19th-century theater still on stage.

Giant evergreen coniferous logs, similar to the present sequoias, grown in the Pliocene on the shore of the ancient Lake Tiberino and buried from the debris of the floods up to the roots; some reach about 1.5 m of diameter and have been preserved thanks to a process of chemical fossilization. Umbriatourism indicates it among the most important paleontological sites in the world, discovered by chance in the seventies during the extraction of clay. The visit starts from the Centre of Plant Paleontology, east of the country, and is suitable for children.

In Palazzo Aymerich, the ancient residence of the Marquises of Laconi: ten of the eleven halls exhibit menhirs and anthropomorphic statues of Sarcidano, Grighine and Mandrolisai, dated between IV and III millennium B.C., in three types (protoanthropomorphs, asexual anthropomorphs and menhir statues by sex); the eleventh room, on the inner court, collects vases, spearheads and blades in flint with megalithic tombs. The laconese pieces are in local trachite; the research began in 1969 in Genna Arrele.
The heart of Italian porcelain.
Borgo over the Golden Conca with the Norman cathedral with gold mosaics, part of the Arab-Norman UNESCO itinerary.
Sibari's symbol bull.

Birthplace of Rossini and UNESCO Creative City for music, between Monte Ardizio and San Bartolo: Piazza del Popolo and Palazzo Ducale, the museums of Palazzo Mosca, the Rocca Costanza and seven kilometers of beach.
One of the wildest beaches in Italy.
The front door to the Brenta.
The ancient heart.
A medieval fortified village with the portal of Pilacorte.
The great cycle of frescoes by Annigoni in a village church.
The old nineteenth-century town hall in the heart of the country.
The oldest olive tree in Europe.

The acropolis of the ancient city, with traces of prehistoric frequentation and ancient protocorinthian ceramics from the end of the 8th century BC. Open from Monday to Friday 9-13; Saturday and Sunday only by booking by email.
The Capitol hidden.
The village under the castle.
The sky of Saint-Barthélemy.
A country church with a painting of the ancient castle.

About a mile from the village: the church built by Domenico Verdile, abandoned in 1870 and reopened in 1895, is flanked by the new church inaugurated in 1987. He preserves a canvas by Mario De Tollis with the two saints.

Italia.it describes the old town as picturesque; the village, already a feud of various families and autonomous from Campo di Giove only from 1904, preserves the memory of the ancient medieval castle (Castrum Cansani) and fountains along the streets. After the earthquake of 1933 collapses and landslides from the highest wall pushed the village to move further downstream.
For the frescoes by Pier Matteo d'Amelia.
The plain of Cabu Abbas, among the highest density areas of nuraghi; the nuraghe Oes, 800 meters from Santu Antine in the territory of Giave, is almost an architectural unicum.

Erected unfinished in 1525-1527 with the offers collected during the plague of 1524 and completed in 1578 by the Brotherhood of the SS. Name of Jesus; preserves relics of St. Rocco, the city's companion, and a painting attributed to Borroni with St. Francis of Sales and St. Joan Francesca of Chantal (second half of the eighteenth century).

Country of the Campi Flegrei overlooking Procida and Ischia, in the Regional Park of the Campi Flegrei: to see the Roman necropolis of Cappella along the ancient Miseno-Cuma road, the Mother Church of the Assumption, the belvedere on the gulf, the islet of San Martino and the marines of Acquamorta and Torrefumo.
The best way to see the city.
Rest of the Roman aqueduct that supplied the city.

Born in the early 1990s from an idea of architect Massimo Palumbo with the Municipality and Kalenarte Association: 21 permanent installations between alleys, stairs, squares and outskirts, to be visited on three colorful itineraries; the last stop is the ...Poet of Casacalenda... of Kostas Varotsos, 9 meters high, in the green outside the village.
A mountain school from a century ago.
The 16th century cloister.

The village of the Isarco Valley is rich in mining and prehistoric history: the mine, one of the most important in the medieval Tyrol, the Archeoparc del Plunacker inhabited since the Mesolithic and the parish with glass windows of 1520 on the life of the miners; above the village the Villanderer Alm, the second mountain hut of South Tyrol, with the Totenkirchl, Lake Totensee and Mount Villandro, geographical center of the province.
From the village to the sanctuary.

Inaugurated on 17 August 2014, it exhibits on two floors about 1,400-1,500 pieces of perfumery, especially from the early 20th century, collected in over a century by the perfumers of the country and donated to the Fondazione "Il Camino del Profumo" by the Muzio family. The route starts from the wheel of the "arrotino," crosses the sensory botanical garden (2015) and goes from the "low perfumery" to the perfumes from the Egyptians to the Renaissance to the great modern brands. From September to July you visit by reservation (at least one day before); in August it is open every day 9:30-13:00 and 16:30-20:00.

The medieval village is spread around the three churches of Santa Maria, San Nicolò and San Martino, which correspond to the Latin, Greek and Lombard districts; not to be missed is the romantic Via degli Archi, while at the Porta Aragonese there are still parts of the walls.
The genius's vineyard.
A neo-Gothic note in the village.

In the premises of the old primary schools of Invico, documents the daily life in Lodrino and Valle Trompia before industrialization: over a thousand objects in about 400 m2 divided into rooms on hunting and territory, haymaking and breeding, wood processing, blacksmith's forge and a collection of medical instruments of the nineteenth century. In 2017 the multimedia section on dairy art was added to the adjacent peasant house; outside there is the \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\ Teaching hall and carpentry workshop for children; it is part of the Trompia Valley Museum System and of the route "The forest road" . Opening of the Sunday season (in 2025 from 15 to 17) and visits by reservation at 360 1030495.
The feudal palace and the ancient door.

The village, perched and closed by walls, has old stone houses with small windows built directly on the banks of the stream. After passing a bridge you pass under a door adorned by two bronze angels, one of which plays the harp; in Piazza Piccola there is the octagonal fountain of 1486 and, little further, the statue of King David, master of the harp, symbol of the country taken in various reliefs.

Renaissance cathedral with the bell tower, flanked by Palazzo Carli and Palazzo Ovio Gobbi from the second half of the sixteenth century, built a few decades after the church. It is known for the portal and the great twentieth century frescoes of the presbytery of the Veronese Pino Casarini; among the oldest paintings a Madonna of the Rosary of Palma il Giovane and a Madonna with Saints by Francesco Bassano, as well as works by Andrea Vicentino.

Wanted by Grand Duke Leopold II, begun in 1836, consecrated in 1838 and completed in 1841, it is neoclassical Latin cross with pronao, columns, balustrade, arch and friezes (of the sculptor Nencini) in cast iron of the Ilva foundries, among the first Tuscan examples of iron architecture; cast iron also pulpit, balustrade of the presbytery and candlesticks.
The city's civic museum of modern art, among the cultural milestones reported by Italia.it.
Prehistoric finds of a private collection.

Municipality of Parco Agricolo Sud Milano, in an area healed by the monks' bonifiche; in the historic center the nineteenth-century parish church of San Giorgio Martire and the old Belpensiero farmhouse, mentioned already in the sixteenth century, with a secular plane tree in the courtyard.
Learn a trade from the women of the Laga.
Nineteenth-century Sanctuary on Mount Argegna (1019 m), restored in 1946 and destination of pilgrimages.

Building on three floors built in 1915 according to project of the engineer. Scotti, like the other stations of the mountain section of the Turin-Ceres railway; the Lanzo-Ceres alpine stretch was inaugurated in 1916.

Born in 1983 at the invitation of the mayor Bandino Calcaterra, who asked the citizens to donate agricultural and handicraft items, he occupied the premises of Villa Annoni once destined for servitude, recovered by volunteers. In 15 rooms he collects tools and tools of agricultural crafts and artisans, documents and objects related to wars, testimonies on emigration, associationism and the first forms of social security and social assistance. According to the municipality, it opens every afternoon from May to October, together with the park of the villa.
To the north is the clear sand of Lido Riccio and the pebbles and cliffs of Punta Ferruccio, on about 20 km of Ortonese coast.
The origins of the city under the square.
The Madonna del Latte outside the walls.
The Cathedral of Giarre is a neoclassical church overlooking Piazza Duomo, with free and free access.
A beacon on the tip of the Costa Smeralda.
The ancient belt with the medieval moat and the Raimonda, Scaramuccia and Grimana towers remains.The Grimana Savorgnana Tower, along Via Altan, is one of the three gateways to the city.
The castle where Manfredi was married.
The Syracuse of the early Christians.
Give Maya to the tablet, with a final taste.
The civilization of wheat in the granary of Sicily.

Common at the gates of Cagliari with a historic center of campidanesi houses, the parish Gothic-Aragonese of Santa Barbara and the Civic Archaeological and Art Gallery Museum; the territory goes up to the forest of the Seven Brothers and goes down to the sea with the coastal hamlet of Solanas.

On Via Cassia, at the mouth of the Agna stream, it is documented by 772 as a Longobard monastery with a function of hospice for travelers and pilgrims. Benedictine from 1028 to 1429, then the Canonici Regulari Lateranensi until the sixteenth century, was then deconsecrated and used as a cellar and for the breeding of silk bucs; restored almost entirely in the twenties of the twentieth century, preserves as the only original part the crypt of the X-XI century, with carved columns and valuable capitals.
Thermal spring at the geographical centre of the city, which flows at 74.5 degrees; the water is protected by an octagonal aedicule inaugurated in 1879.
About a kilometer from the town, caves rich in stalactites and stalagmites.

Small well-preserved center on a green terrace sheltered from the Raut, Resettum and Fara mountains, with stone houses, dark wooden balconies (daltz) and external stairs; in the village the seventeenth-century church of Santa Maria delle Grazie and that of San Daniele, 1700.
A masterpiece of the Umbrian Renaissance.
Tastes of Prenestini Mountain farmers.
Deer in the holly.
On the trail of the Dominican monastery.
Closed for PNRR accessibility work
seasonal opening (from Easter/April to September-October, morning 10-13; afternoon only by reservation), the two sources Promobellagio give different periods
An 18th century stone chapel.

The oldest church in the village, documented in 1328 and probably in the late 12th century, with side portal with sharp arches, monumental staircase and eighteenth-century loggia, Renaissance chapel, funeral monuments of the Tinto family (1567), baroque altar and medieval bell tower with yellow and green brick dome.

Natural reserve on the edge of the country, oasis of Mediterranean biodiversity and stop of migratory birds around one of the most interesting artificial lakes in Calabria; the country is part of the Regional Natural Park of the Serre.
The Gothic facade of the course.
Normally closed, open throughout the month of May according to SardiniaCultura
The late Baroque parish.
The Medici origin of the country.
A stop in the popular district of Parma.

A capital carved with intricate motifs, enigma for historians: according to the prevailing hypothesis comes from the ancient Certosa of San Lorenzo, perhaps from a pagan temple that stood on the site.

Artificial lake created by the dam started in 1977 in Madonnuccia and completed in 1993, indicated as the largest in Tuscany. Above the lake rise the Castle of Brancialino, of the twelfth century, and in Sigliano the neobyzantine church of Santa Maria della Pace, finished in 1921, with panoramic views over the water.
A few steps from Viterbo, the basilica of Santa Maria della Quercia is a symbol of the Viterbo Renaissance; the entrance is free and the visits are suspended during the functions.
Fortress erected in the middle of the sixteenth century to defend the coast; for the feast of Our Lady of Montallegro is fired with lights and fireworks.
The Doria Square.

Panoramic terrace in the middle of the Corso, with chess floor, stone balustrade on the Ionian and Etna in the distance; there are Sant'Agostino with the crenellated bell tower, the baroque church of San Giuseppe with the double staircase and the Clock Tower, where there was a door of the third wall.

The medieval castle, perhaps between the 8th and 10th centuries, controlled the Via Regina at the crossroads towards the Alto Lago and Lake Lugano and was destroyed in 1523 by the Grigionese militias: the perimeter walls remain, followed by the houses of Via Castellino. On the ruins stands the church of San Carlo, built in 1614 by Cinzio Calvi as a sepulchre for himself and his wife, with a sailing bell tower in Spanish style; along the bas-relief streets of the 11th and 12th centuries, like the head of the bull of San Luca and the fountain of the Savior.
The church of the village reborn after the earthquake.
The intact medieval village.
The 14th century sister of Propezzano.
Underwater archaeology in the sea of Cilento.
Church of the historical core, among the stages of the visit on foot.
Under the loggia, the Capitolium cryptoportico.
The "Pompei dell'Alto Lazio" in the woods.
Archaeological finds, ceramics and paintings.

Country at the foot of Mount Musinè, with the Roman rustic villa of Augusta, the nineteenth-century sanctuary of Sant'Abaco, the monumental cross of 1901 on the summit and lakes of the Primavalle area.
An example of international baroque, with frescoes by Louis Dorigny and marble busts by Giusto Le Court.
A baroque village to walk through doors and squares.
The millennial abbey in the heart of Terra Murata.
The clown's house.
An author's cemetery signed Vantini.
Five jumps of water in the woods.
Some itineraries are at extra charge; tickets to the tour centre of Alberese

An ancient pieve center of the high Trebbia Valley and castle of the Obertenga brand, then passed to Malaspina, Fieschi and Doria, for a long time home of a fair frequented by all the nearby valleys: the parish church of San Bartolomeo with the Romanesque bell tower, the baroque San Martiano, the oratory of San Rocco and the diocesan Museum of sacred art.
The eighteenth century sacred Marche.
The parish church of the early twentieth century of the valley floor.
private property, you can admire from the outside
From the 15th century, in an elevated position, with the facade depicting the patron, soldier martyr of the Theban legion.
From the convent of Santa Caterina, where according to tradition he studied as a young admiral from Genoa Andrea Doria (born in Oneglia in 1466), today only the church remains.

Set up in the recovered remains of the old fortress of Villa Minozzo, it preserves texts, costumes, props, drawings, photos and objects of May, the popular open-air theatre of the Reggiano and Modenese Apennines that stage cavalry and mythical feats. It is managed by local Maggistic companies: timetables and visits must be arranged by telephone.
Emerald water and sunsets on the sea.

A village walled on a hill between the valleys of Potenza and Musone, with concentric streets around Piazza Leopardi: the fifteenth-century Palazzo dei Priori with the five-arch loggia, the collegiate church of Santa Maria Assunta with the glazed terracotta altar of Mattia della Robbia, the thirteenth-century oratory of San Nicolò and the civic collections.
Secular oaks and fauna of the Dauni Mountains.
Walk through the medieval gate and walk through the village on the Serra.

Marinar village on the Gulf of Paradiso with the basilica on the harbor and the castle of Dragonara, and in its territory the abbey of San Fruttuoso reachable only on foot or by sea, Punta Chiappa and San Rocco.
The Madonna-Sketch.

Anciently second parish church of Castelfranco, south of Via Emilia: a single nave church known for acoustics and used for concerts, with the organ of Domenico Traeri of 1743 (restored in 1987), a statue of St. Nicholas of the Scandlari, a painting of the Virgin of Elisabetta Sirani and the Romanesque bell tower with square plan.
The flora of Valvestino in the cheese factory of the village.
The treasure of a diocese that dates back, by tradition, to the end of the first century.

With Piazza Duca degli Abruzzi it forms the main complex representative of the historic center of Picciano: the monumental brick façade dominates the square, about 130 cm lower than the building, and is divided into three parts by binated pilasters, with central portal between two composite columns under a triangular tympanum and side wings with broken tympanums. The interior, of baroque taste, has an inscribed cross plan, dome on the central compartment and semicircular apse. It is the parish church (fornìa di Penne).

The Benedictine abbey that can be reached from the center by going down the stairs of Sant'Ercolano, via Cavour and Borgo XX June; its history is linked to dependencies in the territory like the Castle of Casalina.

Park in the north-east of the municipality along three lakes born from former sand and gravel quarries, the Pond of the Salici, the Pioppi and the Fishermen, which the Municipality defines an oasis of high natural value.
Enter the gallery where the fossils of Bolca were born.

Centro raccolto, percorribile on foot, with old shops, cafés and palaces of the thermal age; the parish church of the Santissimo Redentore is a neo-Romanesque building of the late nineteenth century, with a large statue of the Redeemer in the facade, the major altar and nineteenth century wooden works.
A megalite of the Bronze Age among the olive trees.

Clear waters, coves and wild landscape, with a small port and establishments; the Scoglio della Margherita houses a chapel to the Madonna built by fishermen, and the beach of Pezzolo, of golden sand and shallow bottom next to the remains of a Roman villa, is suitable for families. Deep and rocky seabeds attract water sports.

Alta Langa village along the Bormida, dominated by the imposing Castle of the Caldera with the family chapel frescoed by Antonino Ocello da Ceva; just outside, Santa Maria dell'Acqua Dolce, the oldest church in the valley, and in the village the Silk Museum in the former spinning mill and the house-museum of the writer Maria Tarditi.
The canal that crosses the center, designed by Leonardo da Vinci in 1502 for Cesare Borgia, with the houses of colorful fishermen.
The legend of Bella Galiana.
Fishing village with port, perched on a promontory around a 15th century fortress, overlooking the coast and the island of Giglio.
A crescent sheltered between granite and stain.

Italia.it recommends to go down into the crypt, decorated with fine Byzantine frescoes: it is an apse chapel of the ninth century from which starts the path of the Diocesan Museum, opened in March 2025 in the spaces between the ancient cathedral of St. John and the new of Saints Peter and Paul. Eight sections on about 500 square meters with paintings, shovels, silvers, vestments and sculptures, including fifteenth-century fragments in painted and golden terracotta by Michele from Florence. Museum open Friday afternoon, Saturday and Sunday.
In Piazza Duomo, the basilica with richly decorated interiors, among the masterpieces of the sacred art of the city.
Romanesque in the country.
The canyon at the door of the Pollino.
The wooden statues of the saints of the country.

Inaugurated in December 2000 in a large garden inside the Roman and medieval archaeological area of Aquinum, between a basalt stretch of the Via Latina and the church of Santa Maria della Libera. It tells the territory of Aquino from Prehistory to the modern age, in chronological sections (Prehistory and Protohistory, Roman age, Middle Ages and modern age), with educational panels and a multimedia location for the virtual visit.
€2.50, reduced €2, children 6-10 years €1

Built in 1545 on the hill called "Cabalan" and used until about 1882-1884, it preserves about 130 stonestones in sandstone or limestone, mostly facing Jerusalem, of families of Conegliano and Ceneda; among the coats of arms the squirrel of the Coneian, the family of Emanuele Conegliano, then Lorenzo Da Ponte, librettist of Mozart. Guided tour on the first Sunday of the month 10-12, other days by reservation at IAT.
Ancient pilgrimage site dating back to the 6th century BC, near the lake, on the descent to the water; the remains of the temple are located in the woods on the banks.
The woods for the children.
The court of the Prince of Music.
€5, reduced €2 (18-24 years), free under 18 years
Listing in extension: the guide covers for now 0 of the 2 places of culture recorded by the Ministry of Culture in this municipality, as well as churches, squares and nature.
The village seen from above.
Along the river Valle Oscura there are waterfalls and ancient mills, enhanced by the municipality as naturalistic routes, in a mountain hinterland of beech, holm oaks, firs and pine trees.
165 steps for the best glance at the center.
A curious motto about a palace of Sansovino.

Built by the Colonna on the top of Mount Ginestro, it was destroyed in 1298, rebuilt and damaged again in 1436-37; with the restoration of Stefano Colonna in 1482 it lost its military function and became a food store of the community. Abandoned in the nineteenth century, it was recovered for public use at the beginning of the twentieth century; Jacopone was held by Todi and Corradino of Swabia. In winter it hosts an artistic nativity scene with life-size characters.

Built around the middle of the sixteenth century and enlarged after 1577 with a nave and a large choir; it preserves paintings of Genovesino and F. Mouth. The bell tower was erected by the Confraternita di San Rocco Pellegrino.
A miniature San Marco in the heart of Polesine.
Built in 1100 in the castle fortress, it was demolished in the early eighteenth century and replaced by a new Greek cross church with six chapels.
Natural basin of about three hectares reachable from the center through the forest, habitat of carp, barbs and alborelle; around woods, picnic areas, a short ring path and kiosks with local products.
The cherry blossoms in spring.
Four works of land art along the paths.
To understand Ariminum before turning it.

Declared by the Ministry national monument of historical-naturalistic interest, it was realized at the expense of Carlo Ruggiero and donated to the Municipality in 1880. On the 26,515 m2, four gardens alternate with English around a monumental fountain, built with the marbles of the Alcantarini monastery destroyed by the earthquake of 1783, and the Italian villa among the holm oaks; the botanical garden preserves rare species with California redwoods, Lebanon cedars and tulip trees. Since 2008 it houses a Giardino dei Giusti.
Crivelli's polyptych and De Carolis' world.
Keep out of the door.
Seven centuries of Ruffanian ceramics under the mother church.
The wines of the San Martino Valley at the oldest winery in Bergamasca.

Protected area of about 900 hectares managed by WWF Italy around the artificial lake born in 1963 with the dam on the Tiber; a nature path with birdwatching huts, observation towers, wooden walkways and an outdoor classroom allows you to observe flora and fauna.
Low water and sunsets on the lagoon.
Walk through the woods of the high hill of Pavese.
The wine of the village.

According to tradition, the parish was mentioned as early as 1011 when Bishop Landolfo confirmed the donation of the church to the monastery of San Solutore; after 1781 it was extended to the present size, with three naves, the largest of the Lanzo Valleys. Inside an eighteenth-century Crucifix by Stefano Maria Clemente and the altar of Our Lady of the Rosary with altarpiece from 1869; next to the chapel of the Brotherhood of the Most Holy Name of Jesus. Information: Tel. 0123 696117.
Baroque church of the patron saint of Marino, which preserves the miraculous image of Our Lady of the Rosary, celebrated on October 7th.
The oldest church in Laveno, dating back to the 9th century although with numerous subsequent interventions. In the next cemetery stands the futurist artist Luigi Russolo.
The Arena of Teate next to the museum.
Villa and church frequented by Parini, Monti and Foscolo.
A medieval mountain village still intact in the plant.
The history of ancient Anxanum from the Neolithic to pre-Roman furnishings and the ex-vote of an Italic shrine of the III-II century BC.
Four-five-century frescoes and views of the Po Valley.

The sabauda tower, with a cone trunk, in blocks of volcanic stone, about 11 meters high, built before the foundation of the village guarding the canal between Sant'Antioco and San Pietro; the lower level was a cistern, the entrance is about 4 meters high and a staircase in the thickness of the wall rises to the stands, from which the look ranges for about 20 km. The ground floor houses an archaeological museum of Phoenician-Punic finds, the room on the first floor temporary exhibitions.
The sea under the center.

The neighborhood develops along Beckwith Street: the Valdese House (1889), built for the bicentenary of the Glorious Repatriation, houses in the synodal hall frescoed by Paolo Paschetto the annual Synod; around the pastoral house (1859-1861), the English-Saxon style houses of the professors, the Unionist House, the Waldensian College of 1832 (now high school) and the Pensionnat founded in 1844 as a female school.

Country at 836 meters overlooking the Ivrea Moraine Serra and its lakes, with the steep alleys of the ancient Villa, the eighteenth-century parish church of San Pietro in Vincoli, the Museum of peasant civilization and, higher up, the Big Bench of the Pinalba Alpe.

The most important site of Santadi, frequented from the 4th millennium BC to the 8th century A.D.: domus de Janas on the southern slopes, a nuragic complex on the summit with the nuraghe Diana incorporated in the double walls, and the Phoenician-punic settlement founded in the second half of the 7th century BC, of which remain the foundations of acropolis, residential district and sanctuary; at the sides the Phoenician necropolis with fossa and the Punic one in room. Partial motor accessibility, parking, recommended hiking shoes.
Set up in the former convent of the Bears.

The high core of the village preserves almost intact the features of a medieval fortified village, with narrow streets, alleys and ancient walls. On the north side stands the civic tower, also called the Town Hall or the Clock, already mentioned in the twelfth century, and there is the church of the Immaculate Conception and St. Joseph, called the new church of Castello.
In the village of Marano, it houses a permanent polyscenical nativity scene of Spanish art, by Paolo Fontana, with 19 handicraft dioramas.
The frescoes by Giulio Campi.
Discovered in 1899 and productive until the end of the eighties; a panoramic structure on the Val d'Ayas houses the museum and allows you to discover the underground world of the mine.

Two Big Bench Community Project Benches by Chris Bangle (b. 98 and 98. 99), joined by a panoramic walk. The one of Lu, yellow and blue like the balls of the ASD Beach promoter, stands on the San Sebastiano hill at the exit towards Mirabello, about 10 minutes walk from the square, with 360° views from the hills to the plain up to the mountains; between May and June lavender fields flourish.
The largest in the region, at the foot of the homonymous mountain, among woods, pastures, Alpine meadows, lakes, streams and peat bogs; crossed by the path of the Oropa procession.
The ancient water industry of the Coast.
The medieval fortified complex on Celio, "a medieval fortress in the centre of Rome."
The Gothic portal and paintings of Filippo Paladino in a church stratified over five centuries.
The story of the navigator who went around the world.

Common on the slopes above the valley of the Aterno: the fortified village of the Castle of Ocre with seven towers, the Cistercian monastery of Santo Spirito of 1222 and the Franciscan monastery of Sant'Angelo on the rock spur.
Panorama on the lake and signs of prehistory.
The house of the Oltretorrente where the conductor was born in 1867, with relics, letters, chopsticks and documents of his career.
The artists' district and the bridge to be photographed.
Remains of the first century amphitheatre in the area of Civitella.

The centre of the Trentino area of the Stelvio National Park, which includes the upper Val di Rabbi and part of the Val di Peio: it illustrates the naturalistic aspects of the protected area with educational panels, photographs and information material.

Walled village of the Cremona plain on the Oglio, with the Fortress of 1473 which houses the Aquaria archaeological museum, the fifteenth-century walls of about two kilometers and the House of Printers, where in 1488 the complete Jewish Bible was printed.

The Park indicates the stone pastures of the Tanarello Valley: Valcona Soprana, Valcona Sottana and Le Salse, linked to the transhumant pastoralism from which the white cuisine is born, of which Mendatica is one of the two Ligurian capitals.

A path of about 4 km from the centre touches the villas of the village, almost all private and visible only from the outside: Villa Diedo (Sixth century) with the chapel of the Annunziata consecrated in 1684, the seventeenth-century complex of Villa Mascarello-Noventa with walls, barchesse and oratory, Villa Arrigoni-Poli, where on June 4, 1916 Cadorna and Vittorio Emanuele III, Villa Scaroni and Villa Chiericati, headquarters of the command of the VI Armata in 1918 and 1917, and the sixteenth-century Villa Monte (Ca' Ostile), prototype of a Venetian villa in barchessa.

Built by the Brotherhood of Mercy (established in 1478) in the hamlet Molinatto and renovated between the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries, it is dedicated to Santa Marta and San Giovanni Decollato. Inside six large eighteenth-century paintings of Grassi, including the Madonna del Carmine and the Baptist's Decollation, golden wooden statues and the urn of San Celestino, martyr of the Tebea Legion. Free entry during functions.

The baroque cathedral and the oldest organ on the island.

In the former bishop's palace, 14 rooms on two floors with sacred art from the palace, the cathedral and the churches damaged by the earthquake of 1980: wooden and paper sculptures, a portrait of Pope Benedict XIII, a pontifical service in golden silver by Luigi Valadier, vestments and processional umbrellas. In the underground under the cathedral the remains of an 11th century church and a sepulchral crypt; visits only by reservation, for groups of at least 6 people.
White dunes and secular junipers.
Founded in 1997 on the initiative of the City after the donation of 190 works of the painter Gianbecchina to his native country; it is also a cultural center for art and promotion of the territory.

The Palazzo dei Conti Marliani, feudal lords of Busto between the Six and the eighteenth century, then of the Cicogna and municipal since 1820, has been a museum since 1990; after the restoration of 2002 the spaces have doubled. Paintings, drawings, documents and sculptures, more temporary exhibitions.

Country at the top of the valley of the same name, between the traditional hemp weaving and the trails of the Mont Avic Regional Park.

On the eastern shore of the lake, about 46 hectares of the villa of the Emperor Domitian (1st century AD): spa area with quadriportico in polychrome marble, gym and latrine with marble seats, the large cisterns (of the Eco and the Navi, with graffiti of boats) and the porticoed fish pond. From here come the Apollo today in Kassel and the Faun of the Vatican Museums. Visit on request on weekdays and in extraordinary openings with booking.
The Castle of Women, from the Arab Qal'at an-Nisa: towers on a cliff overlooking the valley, destroyed by the earthquake of 1567; the ruins dominate the city.

The heart of the village of San Michele is Piazza Oscar Molinari, in front of the hill crowned by the ruins of the medieval castle; from here start via Dante Alighieri, flanked by porticoes that partly preserve the original wooden ceilings. Centre of medieval origins, capital of the Tonda Tonda Gentile delle Langhe, seat of the National Fair of hazelnuts.

Parish with a Renaissance façade, it preserves 17th century furnishings; the patron saint is celebrated at the beginning of August.

Founded in 1984 by a group of citizens, it occupies a building of the twenties of the twentieth century with over 200 m2 of exposure: more than 2000 tools grouped according to use, along a path in monothematic sections that tells the life and work in the Lower Pavese until the decade following the Second World War. The collection of photographic exhibitions, photographic archive, library, historical documents and videos with testimonies of peasants are completed. Open from Tuesday to Sunday in two-hour bands (closed Monday); free entry and guide, welcome an offer; groups and schools by telephone reservation.

City on the Gulf of Asinara founded by the Romans in the first century BC at the mouth of Riu Mannu as Turris Libisonis, then capital of the Judicate of Torres: the archaeological park with the Roman bridge and the Antiquarium, the basilica of San Gavino, the largest Romanesque church of Sardinia, the necropolis of Su Crucifissu Mannu (UNESCO heritage since 2025) and, offshore, the National Park of Asinara, which is part of the municipality.
Frazione di Frabosa Soprana, which houses the ethnographic museum and one of the giant benches of the artist Chris Bangle, a panoramic point.

The parish church was built in late Gothic forms in the middle of the sixteenth century: five spans, a mayor capilla covered with a starry vault and facade with buttresses and stairs, whose portal recalls that of St. Peter extra muros of Bosa. On the historic center overlooking noble residences like Palazzo Parpaglia.

Fort Austro-Hungarian at 1,445 meters near Malga Cherle, built to bar the plateau: block casemates and battery block connected by a corridor, with 4 domes for obici and a garrison of 5 officers and 128 soldiers. Bombarded immediately by the Italian batteries of the Campomolon, in 1936 it was ruined by the recoverers; you visit some internal passages and from the cover you can see up to Lavarone, Luserna and Cima Vezzena. Easy walk 500 meters from the Hotel Cherle.

Loreto de bidda is located in the historic centre, perhaps of medieval origin, rebuilt at the end of the 17th century, with the frescoed dome; outside the village there is the little Loret'Attesu, where the feast of Our Lady of the Snow is celebrated.
Partly uninhabited village: you walk along the public streets, without entering the buildings
The modern counterpoint to Santa Maria Novella.

Built in 1574-1592 on the site of the ancient church of San Quirino, according to the Borromaic dictates, with nineteenth-century façade by Nicolò Bruno; frescoed vaults by Paolo Maggi (1853-56) and works by Aurelio Luini, Vermiglio, Flemish, Moncalvo and Camillo Procaccini. It preserves the urn of San Martiano and the tomb of the composer Lorenzo Perosi.
On the promenade between the Fort Michelangelo and Borgo Odescalchi, the town's marina.

The ancient Calatia, of Etruscan origins and perhaps inhabited by the Bronze Age, lives again in the National Archaeological Museum set up in the Casino of Starza Penta dei duchi Carafa; in the city the National Convitto Giordano Bruno keeps on the ceiling of the salon an eighteenth-century canvas of 700 square meters, and between the churches stand out the Basilica of Corpus Domini and the SS. Heir to the Altomedieval parish church of Macinesso, rises just outside the archaeological enclosure: sixteenth century plant, nineteenth-century decorations and a valuable wooden ciborium carved and gilded from the end of the seventeenth century.

A popular village of the Pesaro Apennines, with hamlets built around medieval castles: in Lamoli the Benedictine abbey of San Michele Arcangelo houses the Museum of Natural Colors.

Latin colony founded by the Romans in 273 BC on the headland of Ansedonia: walls of over a kilometer with nineteen towers and three gates, the forum and, on the acropolis, the Capitolium and the temple of Mater Matuta; the museum, born with the American Academy in Rome, exhibits the finds of the colony, the port and the necropolis.

Monument in reinforced concrete covered with ceramic tiles designed by Ugo Nespolo and made by ceramists with the students of the Institute of Art Felice Fcio; started in 2002 and completed in 2008 thanks to a donation of a local company.

Municipality of the Novara plain overlooking the valley of Ticino, in whose territory there is Villa Picchetta, seat of the Ticino Park and Lake Maggiore, surrounded by historical farms with medieval and eighteenth-century oratories.

Inaugurated in 2001 in the Altomedieval complex of the Grancia di San Pietro and in the adjacent former municipal slaughterhouse, it tells with objects and multimedia materials the story of Latera around the theme of the earth. From the museum starts the Trail of the three churches towards abandoned quarries of industrial archaeology; audioguides available.

The lakefront follows the curved bank at the northern end of Lake Orta, a lake of glacial origin, divided in two by the Nigoglia, which flows northwards bringing the waters of the lake into the Strona, the Toce and finally into Lake Maggiore. Comune dell'alta Valle Camonica which since 1956 bears the name of Camillo Golgi, the first Italian Nobel laureate for medicine (1906), born here in 1843 and remembered by the Golgi Museum; the territory includes the Riserva delle Valli di Sant'Antonio, with the twin valleys Brandet and Campovecchio, and the ski area Aprica-Corteno.

A small town in the middle Tiber Valley, a fief of the Bulgarelli Counts from the 12th century, then of Perugia and from 1540 of the Papal State; it is the largest Umbrian center of the production of bricks, told by the dynamic Museum of the Laterizio, and has in the territory the abbey of San Sigismondo, the castle of Papiano and a San Sebastiano del Perugino in Cerqueto.

Dominated by a tower with four sloping roofs, called in the tradition of the avoucat house; the oven resting on the rock above the fountain has the roof only one sloping and the chapel of the Holy Trinity preserves a fresco dated 1677. A path connects it directly to Vernetti.

Founded in 1337 by an association founded for a vote against an epidemic, on a land donated by Giovanni Trinca, it was renovated in the seventeenth century and has the facade very modified in the early twentieth century. He preserves works by artists from Brescia and Veneto, including a painting by Antonio Paglia with Blessed Fedele da Sigmarringen, a 16th century Nativity and an Annunciation of the 17th century.

Hunting residence of Traiano (98-117 A.D.) on the highlands at 850 meters, spread over about 5 hectares and largely to be dug: plundered from the late antiquity to the seventeenth century, it is systematically investigated by the Sixties and the excavations of 1999. Of the lower terrace, the only excavated, with garden in the center, you can see the south porch with frescoes on dark background and the triclino with niche nymph, mosaic in glass paste and floor in opus sectile. The museum, in a restored farmhouse inside the area, exhibits excavations and a 3D video reconstruction; Tuesday-Sunday 10-16, Monday closed.
Country between the vineyards at the entrance of the Cogne Valley, with the four-tower castle of the Challant and the Roman bridge-aqueduct of Pont d'Aël.

About 200,000 m2 of cork and Mediterranean maquis with the necropolis of Pranu Muteddu and Nuraxeddu, a group of huts, the domus de Janas of Genna Accas with three tombalous circles and the dolmen of Baccoi. The tombs date back to the final Neolithic (culture of Ozieri, 3200-2800 BC) with frequentations up to 2600 BC; there is the highest concentration of menhirs in Sardinia, about sixty, with an alignment of winds perdas fittas oriented according to the course of the sun. The Tomb II has entrance, anticell and cell carved into two blocks of rock. Reception area with multimedia equipment and guided tours; Sardinia Tourism indicates it among the 17 prehistoric Sardinian sites recognized by UNESCO. Recommended the visit in the early morning.

Country of the Middle Campidano at the foot of Mount Linas, the literary home of Giuseppe Dessì, known for the waterfall of Sa Spendula sung by D'Annunzio, the Liberty Washer of 1893, the parish church of Santa Barbara with its museum and the archaeological museum of Villa Leni; behind the forest of Montimannu with the waterfall of Piscina Irgas.

Romanesque church, already parish, that the catalogue of the Ministry dates back to the first half of the 11th century; bound since 1908, is owned by the Municipality and was extensively restored in 1985. The façade in pebbles with fishbone preserves the primitive forms, simple and harmonious, despite repeated interventions; inside a cycle of frescoes of the first fifteenth century attributed to Pseudo Domenico della Marca d'Ancona.

Large building with scenic façade on the valley, next to San Jacopo, built at the end of the nineteenth century on the perimeter of the ancient fortress: the residence of the Polidori from the sixteenth century, then of the Giani and the abbot dantist Gian Battista Giuliani, who made it a villa dedicated to Dante, was renovated by the Sienese architect Giovanni Paciarelli for Count Angelo De Gubernatis. A seaside town on the coast north of Bari, with the fishing port and the old elliptical centre on a peninsula: the old Cathedral of San Corrado with pyramidal domes, the Baroque cathedral with the diocesan museum, the Templar Hall and the Pulo, a large karst dolina inhabited in the Neolithic.

In the fourteenth century, modified at the end of the fifteenth century, with a fourteenth-century bell tower and cloister of 1456-68; it preserves the Complaint on the dead Christ of Agostino de' Fondulis, a wooden choir of 1508 and two windows of 1495. Open every day 9-18.

The noble floor of the palace, born from the tower of the castle of the end of the sixteenth century, houses the archaeological museum of the Park of the Valley of the Temples, with Greek vases and the complement of the CLXX tomb of the middle of the fifth century BC. Next to the parish church of the Assunta, with the ancient courtyard transformed into a botanical garden with marble fragments; it collects works of the diocese from the 16th to the 20th century and has a section in the former Oratory of San Rocco (16th century). Limestone cave that crosses Mount Aqua, crossed by an internal road of about 850-860 meters started in 1866 by Count Pietro Beltrami and completed by Gaetano Semenza to connect Domusnovas to the mining valley of Oridda; open to traffic until 1999, today you visit on foot with artificial lighting. With the secondary branches (reserved for speleologists, including Su Stampu de Pireddu) the development reaches 3920 meters; the two entrances remain traces of prehistoric cyclopic walls, and Neolithic and Byzantine finds attest to its use as a refuge. Visit to the hotel with online booking.

The centre of the Piacenza plain was born at the crossroads between Via Emilia and the Arda valley, with the system aligned to Corso Garibaldi on the path of the Roman consular; the main monument is the Gothic Collegiate Church of San Fiorenzo, next to the Teatro Verdi in an ancient abbey and the former convent of San Giovanni.

Romanesque church attributed to the Comacini Masters (XI-XII century), documented since 1364, transformed into fortification by the Lomeno and returned to worship by order of St. Charles in 1570; national monument since 1864, restored by Gaetano Moretti with decorations by Ernesto Rusca and reconsecrated in 1911. Façade with mosaic bezel of 1920, trussed on sight, a copy of the Virgin of Częstochowa donated by Karol Wojtyła and the Good Shepherd with fake mosaic in the apse.

Remains of the castle overlooking the gorge near San Pantaleo, according to the tradition built in the 10th century at the time of Saracen raids.

It preserves an original "Extractum ab" of the Holy Shroud (1645), a polychrome wooden crucifix of 1440, a wooden altar of the seventeenth century and a altarpiece of 1527 with Madonna and Saints.

In the ancient courthouse of the Serra family, on the main road to Guasila: objects on the cultivation and use of wheat, many donated by the inhabitants, with rooms divided between the male work in the fields and the female work of the bakery and weaving; stands out a rare wooden wheel instead of stone. A room features the film of the early 1960s by Danish scholar Weis Bentzon on sowing, working and collecting, and a section recalls the launeddas player Dionigi Burranca, who died in Ortacesus in 1995. Workshops and the route "The way of bread" with tasting; open all year round, from Tuesday to Sunday 9-13 and 16-19, free for over 65 and under 5.

Massive brick construction with quadrangular plan with four corner towers, begun in 1372 by the will of Galeazzo II Visconti on a project by Ottorello de Meda and Andrea da Mutina. In the present form it dates back to the 11th century and was probably born as a parish church for the pilgrims of the nearby Via Amerina, leaning against a bastion of medieval defenses; the bell tower rises on a watchtower. In the crypt, also with three naves, the relics of the patron Saint Lanno are preserved.

In the porch ancient stone materials and fronts of a chimney of the 14th-XVI century; on the ground floor the section on the excavations of Parabiago; in the study the Sala Collection with Greek, Magno-Greek, Etruscan and Roman objects; in the loggia the local archaeology in chronological order; in the tower the numismatic collection. Closed on Mondays and from 1st to 31st August.

It rises on the classrooms founded in 313 by Bishop Teodoro, whose mosaic floor in four bays, with the Good Shepherd, the winged Victory and the history of Jonah, is the largest of the Christian West; the present building is of the 11th century, restored by Patriarch Poppon in 1031 and renovated in the fourteenth century.
The sea of Cilento in the pool, for families.

Panoramic area of woods, pastures and springs used to water the cattle, with trails towards the Scurosa Valley and Sefro; the Colfiorito Plans, about 800 meters away, color in spring.
Small medieval castle erected to defend the village and the coast.
Walk on an active volcano.
The largest bamboo maze in the world wanted by publisher Franco Maria Ricci, with the art collection and the pyramid in the center.

Valley rich in waterfalls behind Amalfi, where there were paper mills and a ironworks moved by water; there grows the endemic fern Woodwardia rootans and the path descends along the paper mills disused to the center.
The tabernacle in the sandstone.

Closed courtyard farmhouse, with buildings arranged at right angles around the courtyard, today dedicated mainly to the breeding of cattle and pigs. Dai de' Giorgi passed in 1554 to Count Giovanni Battista Busca, in 1642 to Bellisomi (until 1820), then to Marozzi and, by legacy, to the Holy See in 1970; since 1973 it belongs to the Panigati family. Here a workman of the Devecchi brothers isolated from a cultivation of rice \"ranghino" three different ears, from which was born the variety Vialone, spread since 1904.
The most important building in the country.

Rural village of the Primiero at 640 meters, at the foot of the Pale di San Martino and in the Natural Park of Paneveggio Pale di San Martino: alleys in stone and wood, about 400 gardens, the outdoor exhibition Cataste & Canzei, the small museum Tabia del Rico and the church of San Giovanni Battista on the meadows above the village.
The great abbey of Francigena in Lunigiana.
Art and memory inside a bunker in the Alpine Valley.

Rebuilt on a new site after the earthquake of 1693 and protected by UNESCO among the late Baroque towns of Val di Noto: the Cathedral at the top of the stairs, Palazzo Ducezio and, on the coast, the reserve of Vendicari.

Basilica outside the walls, beyond the Tessino stream, of the VII-VIII centuries: rare example of Lombard architecture with Byzantine and classical influences, part of the UNESCO site of the Longobards in Italy.

Built in the 11th century at the behest of Robert Guiscardo and enlarged over the centuries, with two large supporting arches added to the façade in the 17th century. The interior with three naves with chapels preserves the relics of Saint Potito martyr and Bishop Raffaello Delle Nocche; the bell tower preserves a bifora of the thirteenth century.
The mountain cited by Leonardo.
Ancient road lined with rural houses, wooden walkways, stone cellars and votive chapels, which climbs towards the Masegra.

Three waterfalls of the Riva river in the Vedrette di Ries-Aurina Natural Park, fed by the melting of the snows and more spectacular in summer: the first at about 20 minutes (fit for strollers), the second at 40, the third at 55; the highest makes a jump of 42 meters and is admired by a suspended bridge. The San Francesco Trail, with 10 meditation stations and wooden sculptures, rises in about 75 minutes to the chapel of Francesco and Chiara.
A unique tradition of festive shots fired in Lessinia.

Erected since 1658 by the feudal lord Scipione Brancia, prince of Apricena, on the ruins of the castle federiciano, already semi-destroyed also by the earthquake of 1627; Frederick II stayed in Apricena about thirteen times. A bifora on the cylindrical tower is probably the only remainder of the Swabian building; the palace, with a quadrangular plan with a shoe masonry, contains a large courtyard with a central cistern and a garden.

Medieval village enclosed by ancient walls, founded according to the portal of the Municipality around the Mille by the Farfensian monks; in the center are Piazza San Martino with the view towards the coast and the Sibillini, the Civic Tower and the Church of Saints Martin and Marco, while just outside stands the sanctuary of the Madonna of Mercy with the Museum of the wood processions.
The Medici hunting village.
Long beach near the village, with the mouth of the Cedrino and the wreck of the KT.
Matteo da Gualdo in the country churches.
Compose and print with the machines of a real printer.
The Gothic-Renaissance church of Barbagia.
The gallery housed in the church of Sant'Angelo, where you can stop during the visit.

Observatory with planetary, open on the first and third Wednesday evening of the month; organizes courses, workshops and public observation evenings, especially on the occasion of eclipses and comets.

Railway line of the end of the nineteenth century that turns around the Etna from Catania Borgo to Riposto, 110 km in about 3 hours; Randazzo is located halfway through and is the far north of the Catania-Randazzo stretch where you can climb with your bike.

Started in 1812 on a project by Nicola Bettoli on the area of the convent of San Francesco and completed in 1861, with stuccoes and gold by the set designer Girolamo Magnani; the frescoes of the dome were restored in 2004.
The museum of contemporary art in the Palazzo Donnaregina on the "via dei Musei," next to the two churches of Santa Maria Donnaregina: the old, Gothic of the fourteenth century, and the new, Baroque.
The Gothic of Alba.

State park of about one hectare, born in 2006 on the west bank of the Trebbia to protect a village of about 6000 years ago discovered in the eighties and excavated since 1995: exposed houses, wells, walls in pebbles and ovens, with three neolithic huts rebuilt in real scale in 2010. Since 2021, a museum area has rebuilt part of the high medieval necropolis of 117 tombs (V-VIII century). It is a Museum of Quality of the Emilia-Romagna Region and is part of the European EXARC network.

Designed in 1374 by Angeluccio di Ceccolo, called "il Trucascio" and completed in 1389, it was imprisoned there and then lived Armcio Fortebraccio; it was jailed from 1814 to 1923 and houses until 1974, restored by the Municipality between 1984 and 1986. The square mast exceeds 30 metres, with three smaller crenellated towers; the rooms house the Centre for Contemporary Art.
A unique monumental space in Romagna.
A noble residence next to the Cathedral.

Rebuilt after the earthquake of 1693 with a neo-Gothic façade, rare in the area, preceded by a stairway church; of the church of the XIII century there are two waterworks and part of the stone floor behind the altar. The wooden crucifix is attributed to Fra' Umile da Petralia.
The baroque jewel of the village.
The heart of Piazzo, with its restaurants under the arcades, the sixteenth-century façade of the Princes' Palace Dal Pozzo della Cisterna and the terracotta arches of Casa Teccio.
See the luthiers of Bisignano at work.
The hamlet of the glassmakers on the Nestore.
The most famous English garden in Lario.
The public palace of the village, also known as the Parliament.
A medieval village walled in the hills.
A nuraghe overlooking the sea.

Anthropological demoetno museum opened in 2008 in Palazzo Mancini, with interactive and multisensory path and audio guide. Sonnino tells the land of border between the Papal State and the Kingdom of the Two Sicilies: the brigandage, the travellers of the Grand Tour and the artists who portrayed it (Bartolomeo Pinelli, Léopold Robert, Edward Lear), the Procession of the Torches, the decree of Pius VII of 1819 that ordered its destruction, figures such as the brigand Antonio Gasbarrone and Cardinal Giacomo Antonelli. Open Monday-Friday 9-13 and 14-19, Saturday and Sunday by reservation.

The almost 3 km road that connects the island to Sardinia, started by the Carthaginians and completed by the Romans; just before the modern bridge you can see the ruins of the Roman bridge with several arches.
The castle of the legend.

In a large building in the center, it exhibits 260 works donated by Cavallo, artist and local collector, to which is dedicated a monographic section: paintings, sculptures and graphics, from the two small works of Lombard school to a large nucleus of the 1950s and 1960s, with works by Guglielmo Pizzirani, Remo Brindisi, Concept Pozzati, Alberto Sughi, Luigi Filocamo, Salvatore Fiume and Giulio Turcato. A detached seat in the Town Hall hosts the municipal collection in rotation.
Neo-Gothic synagogue, memory of the Jewish ghetto established by the Savoys: on the ground floor the Temple Small, on the upper floor the Temple Great with neo-Gothic decorations and windows.
A unique striped façade in Modenese.

Church built between 1590 and 1595 on top of the hill Crosio, in 1630 quarantine place for soldiers returning from the plague; it is reached on foot with a path from Gusmini Avenue and offers a view of Clusone and the whole plateau. Visitable only from the outside.

At the foot of Mount Ghent, between Appiano and Caldaro, a basin about 200 meters long and 50 meters wide in a cluster of porphyry debris, which remains fresh even in summer. You can walk from San Michele to Pigenò, Castel Gandegg and the hotel Stroblhof.
Opened in 2001 in the Olivetani Monastery, it exhibits the finds of Polesine from the Bronze Age to the Renaissance with reconstructions of daily life and multimedia installations.

Sanctuary of Saints Cosimo and Damiano about 5 km from Oria; next door, the ethnographic museum opened in 2007, with the collection collected in about 40 years by Gerardo Andriulo: over 5000 pieces in three sections, peasant world, social life and missing trades.

Building that exhibits ancient finds of Capri and the Mediterranean; in its walls are walled fragments of marble coming from the villa of Gradola.
Minerals, fossils and shells collected by a passionate naturalist.

A hilly village about 30 km from Turin, known for the Beraudo Castle, still the family residence, and for the nineteenth-century park of Xavier Kurten where every spring, the tulips of "Messer Tulipano" bloom; to see also the sanctuary of the Blessed Virgin of Spina and the parish with the triptych of Jacopino Longo.
One of the best preserved medieval villages around Rome.
15th century frescoes at the door of the village.
