According to tradition, the name comes from the hut of "scarza" built by St. Francis, who suspended there in 1218; in 1282 Nerio di Bulgaruccio dei Conti di Montegiove had it built church and convent, and in the apse of the church of the Santissima Annunziata a fresco depicts the saint in levitation, among his first images. Abandoned by the friars in the eighteenth century, the complex was purchased in 1956 by the Milanese architect Tomaso Buzzi, who built his ideal city between 1958 and 1978 there, a theatre machine of seven theatres culminating in the Acropolis, with the Tower of Babel, the Musical Scala of the seven octaves and the Scala of Jacob; the opera was never finished. Information and reservations on lascarzuola.com.
For a rural village surrounded by water.
The Roman theatre, the thermal baths and the Etruscan-Roman temple of the Etruscan city that controlled the streets of the Apennines, with the museum of artifacts.
The villa on the hill with the Italian garden.
A waterfall in the woods that in winter becomes illuminated ice.
Park and viewpoint on the plain of Coghinas.
The Rock of the Rangons and the Court of Taste.

Medieval castrum plant with concentric circles, steps and views; Piazza Alta, the highest and oldest point of civil and religious life, is closed by the small Palazzo dei Priori and Palazzo del Podestà in bricks.
In Santomato one of the most important outdoor art collections in Italy: about 80 monumental works by artists such as Staccioli, Folon, Sol LeWitt and Nagasawa in the park of a villa.

The walls were commissioned by Ludovico il Moro in 1487 after a first raid of the Grisons; of the three gates (Bormina, Milanese and Poschiavina) the best preserved is the Poschiavina Gate, with frescoes of the sixteenth century, which is unique body with the Palazzo Pretorio, ancient seat of the Grigion Podestà with a large portal and coats of arms frescoed in the hallway.
16th century church in the alleys of the historic center of Piano delle Fosse.
private property visible only from outside according to the Foundation; the MiC card (agg. 2021) indicates closed every day

Along the promenade of Viale Fonte Nuova, with a perennial source, you arrive at the springs of Rinaggiu under the Limbara, known since the Roman era for its therapeutic, panoramic and surrounded by a centenary park.

He keeps manuscripts and papers of the writer, all his works in Italian and foreign editions, the private library of about 9,000 volumes, about 600 records and CDs, 350 videotapes recorded by the same Bufalino, cinephile, and the photographic archive.

Built around the year 1000 with defensive structure then adapted to residence; its remains, symbol of the noble past of the village, still seem to control the whole territory. A restoration project is planned for the building.
A thirteenth-century church in the village of Ioannella.
A church on the square.

An ancient town of commercial tradition on the two banks of the Adda, where the Poschiavo Valley meets the Valtellina; to see the Renaissance shrine of the Madonna di Tirano, the walled village with its narrow doors, noble palaces such as Palazzo Salis and the station from which starts the Red Bernina Train, UNESCO World Heritage line since 2008.

Labyrinth of alleys built between the IX and X century, which is accessed by the gates Amato, Maggiore and Gate; the Palazzo di Corte of the fourteenth century was the seat of the court and the town hall, and in the square in front were held the poles "a candle"; in the village also the Fontana di Ciocio, Roman fountain of the second century.
Tuff valleys and woods in the Etruscan Park.

Stage 18 of the Liguria Path (10,3 km, 3 hours and 15, 413 m difference in altitude): behind the Cruise terminal of Savona-Go with the red triangle marker, climb to the Fort San Giacomo, then for a steep staircase between the brooms to the ruins of the fort of Santo Stefano and along the walls of the battery of San Sebastiano, continue on the botanical path and in the cork grove towards Mount Sant'Elena.
Tropical greenhouse with hundreds of free butterflies and an insectario, in the pinewood of Milano Marittima.

He collects paintings and sculptures by the Salentine artist Ezekiel Leandro (1905-1981), set up by himself in the garden of his home: in addition to the paintings, the Sanctuary of Patience, inspired by the sacred iconography, with statuary groups in stone, concrete and recovery materials.

It connects the Mamuthones and Issohadores with the carnivals of other Mediterranean lands: at the entrance images, texts and sounds on the origins of the Mamuthones and the oldest Mamuthone mask, perhaps early nineteenth century; then the hall of the barbaric carnival, with Boes, Merdules and Filonzana of Ottana and Thurpos of Orotelli, and the Mediterranean hall, with the carnivals of the Alpine arch and the Iberian and Balkan peninsulas. The Mamuthones carry the black face of wood, sheepskins and about 30 kilos of bells. A cumulative ticket with the Museum of Culture and Work €6, reduced €4.

Rare example in central Italy of hydraulic factory to crowd and dye with natural colors cloths of wool and hemp, at the foot of the castle of Pievebovigliana: the plant dates back to the seventeenth century, was managed by Stefano Cianni in the nineteenth century and in 1822 worked about 10,000 arms of fabric a year. There are still foundations, walls and a stretch of the canal fed by the river Capodacqua; the municipality provides for its recovery as a museum of industrial archaeology.
On one of the highest heights of the Monferrato, the Sacred Marian Mount of Crea, a UNESCO World Heritage Site, with the spectacular Paradise Chapel.
The sea with the mountains behind it.

The seventeenth-century mill of the historic centre, with a restored arched porch, still active and crossed by the Montecuccoli channel that unites Marano to Vignola; then became the central ENEL of the village, houses the Museum of Energies, with ancient machinery of the first electric production and materials on canals, mills and opifici of Panaro and Samoggia, and the Documentation Center .
The remains of the monastery founded in 754 by the Longobard Walfredo, reachable by a nice walk.

The village of the chestnuts is located on the Tyrrhenian side of Aspromonte, between 500 and 700 meters, surrounded by chestnut trees, holm oaks and abetinas up to the Piani di Carmelia; in the village the churches of San Nicola and dell'Assunta and the Garibaldi Virtual Museum on the Aspromonte countryside of 1862.

A small town at the ford of Enza, built around the castle of the Matilda period renovated by the Estensi; in the center porticos, tower houses and the parish church of San Donnino, just outside the Sanctuary of the Olmo and Villa Aiola the museum of Parmigiano Reggiano.
The villa frequented by Giosuè Carducci, with the Carduccian Museum and Musicalia, the museum of mechanical musical instruments.
The Matterhorn valley, with Breuil-Cervinia at 2000 meters, the glaciers of the Plateau Rosa for skiing all year round and the Gouffre des Busserailles gorge.

Ruins in the center of the village on a spur of limestone, where Paolo Orsi recognized the acropolis of the Hellenized indigenous center. The Byzantines built a fortress there in the 8th century; the castle is mentioned in 1272 in the Angevin list of the Sicilian fortresses, in 1393 it passed to Ughetto Santapau and was destroyed by the earthquake of 11 January 1693. From the Arabic name of the hill, to the Kudyah, would be the name Licodia.

The heart of the Riviera delle Palme: a 5 km promenade with thousands of palm trees, one of the largest fishing ports in Italy with the Museum of the Sea Pole, the High Country with the Tower of Gualtieri and the Sentina Reserve at the mouth of the Tronto.
The peasant life of Langa in two rebuilt rooms.
The works saved from the earthquake of Belice.

Erected by the Friars Minor in the 14th century at the western end of the village: on the high altar the polyptych of Lorenzo d'Alessandro, long attributed to Niccolò Alunno and returned to his author thanks to the balance document of the contract, dated 1496.
Listing in extension: the guide covers 4 of the 6 places of culture recorded by the Ministry of Culture in this municipality, as well as churches, squares and nature.

In 1623 the archpriest De Santis brought to Roseto the cult of Saint Philip Neri: his house became an oratory that still holds a silver bust of the saint. In the center there is also the church of SS. Body of Christ, an important place of worship between the Seven and the Nineteenth Century, then restored and named after Christ the King, today desecrated; in the village the churches of St. Nicholas and St. Mary Lauretana.

The only authentic remains of the ancient Benedictine abbey of San Silvano, in the center of the village near the parish church; cited as "Cantina dei Santi" in a document of 1777, has older origins and an eighteenth-century portico. One of the two rooms decorated contains frescoes from the second half of the fifteenth century: originally 28 squares, almost all still legible, with biblical stories, especially of the life of King David, attributed with uncertainty to Bartulonus da Novara.
A flat cycle path along the canal, from the Plan de la Tour (Palaplan) pavilion to the Black Earth Mill, a graphite mill near Bec Dauphin, for which there is a redevelopment project.

Inaugurated in June 2007, it presents archaeological research on the territory: at the center is the necropolis of Piano (Campo dei) Cerasuoli, with tombs of the 8th-VII century BC of the culture of Oliveto Citra-Cairano. Female sets of rank with fibula and bronze bracelets, male accessories with weapons, a ritual axe and vases with wolf protomes, totemic animal of the Irpini, a Sannitic belt, attic ceramics and materials of the inhabitants of Piano dei Tivoli, excavated between 1979 and 1985. Irpinia system indicates opening Monday-Friday 9-12 (Tuesday and Thursday 16-18 also), Saturday and Sunday 9-13.
The sculptures of the Gagini.

Villa of delights built between the sixteenth and eighteenth centuries, designed around 1585 by Count Pirro I Visconti Borromeo, which transformed an agricultural estate inspired by the Medici villas and made it one of the most renowned country houses in Milan; the project is by Martino Bassi, the decorations of Camillo Procaccini, Morazzone, Volpino and others. In the eighteenth century, Giulio Visconti Borromeo Arese added the "Fourth new" with the ballroom; the City bought the villa in 1971. Season 2026 from May to October; on Sunday the Palaces can be visited also on a free visit. Free up to 5 years and with Musei Lombardia subscription.
Letters and relics of the Alps.
The rocks to Bari.

The wooded area of more than 20 hectares is equipped in the Selva di Meana, state property, with tall trees, maples, roses and wild orchids, and fauna such as wild boars, deer and roe deer.

Acqualagna is the capital of the truffle: the national fair, held every year from 1965 between late October and early November and now international, offers exhibition-market, cooking shows with starred chefs, tastings and workshops. The Tuber magnatum Pico grows in the woods of Furlo; the harvest runs from 1 October to 31 December and the area holds the national record of sales.
A miniature crochet that reproduces the territory between Vinci and Cerreto Guidi, signalled by Feel Florence as a stop not to be missed.
Designed in the late 1930s by Adalberto Libera, between neoclassical and functionalism.
12th century church with cross plan covered by a pyramidal dome.

Phoenician-punic centre then Roman, whose remains were brought to light by a tide: a tophet, the ancient road to Nora and a necropolis with the temple of the god Bes, whose statue is at the National Archaeological Museum of Cagliari.

Small castle village of the Bass Monferrato astigiano, near the forests of Muscandia, dominated by the Castle Gavotti; in the former Municipal Forn the Ecomuseo of the Bass Monferrato Astigiano exhibits a collection of carpenter and cabinetmaker objects.

Site of 670-695,000 years ago with nine levels of excavation: the skull with tusks of an ancient elephant, a fragment of femur of Homo heidelbergensis, the oldest human presence in Italy, and the most ancient Acheulean bifacials of Western Europe.
Puppets and scenery of the Emilian tradition.

Ancient entrance to the Etruscan acropolis, imposing symbol of the city overlooking Piazza Fortebraccio.

The historic centre is located on the terraces of the ancient Praeneste, with alleys and stairways that go up to the highest point; the city has dominated the countryside south of Rome for almost three thousand years. On 18 August the Palio of Sant'Agapito with the Scifa Giostra.

Monastery complex founded in 1126 by St. William of Vercelli, one of the most visited Marian shrines in the South: in the ancient basilica the Gothic portal of the end of the thirteenth century, the cosmatescan canopy and the wooden choir of 1573; in the new church (1952-61) the table of the "Mamma Schiavona" of Montano d'Arezzo, of the end of the thirteenth century; in the crypt the tomb of the founder.
The largest artificial lake of the Marche, an oasis of wildlife protection on the routes of water birds, with hiking trails and mountain bikes between maquis and holm oaks.
Laboratory-museum of hand-woven art.

A small village with a short detour with a view of the plain, known for the Ecomuseum of Castagna, with the ancient water mill still working, and for the Fontana 'l Burnel, a prehistoric coppellate mass.
The return of the gipeto.

A small town on the Tyrrhenian coast of Cosenza, whose name evokes the ancient cultivation of cedar: the fortified old town revolves around Piazza del Popolo with the Fontana del Nettuno and Palazzo del Trono, seat of the Museo dei Brettii e del Mare; on the coast the Torre di Rienzo, the Scogliera dei Rizzi and a large marina.
Rebuilt in 1233 on the site of the church of St. Thomas of Canterbury.
An itinerary among medieval walled villages in the hills of Marche.
The Giugiaro funicular.
Romanesque bichrome in open country.
Villages scattered in the sun in high Valpelline under the Dent d'Hérens, with about twenty glaciers and the large dam of Place Moulin.

In the family house left as a legacy by art historian Luigi Mallé, who died in 1979, with his collections ordered by historical period: Flemish paintings, eighteenth century pastels, ceramics, vases and vintage photographs; on the ground floor the Civic Library. guided tours only and limited number, recommended booking
Fortification of Norman-Sveva origin between the XI and XII century, with four towers, in a dominant position on top of a rocky spur above the village.

Founded in 1004 by St. Nile of Rossano among the ruins of a Roman villa, where a republican sepulchre closed by iron grates gave the name of "Crypta ferrata" , the basilica was consecrated on 17 December 1024 and Leo XIII gave it the title of basilica. Inside the mosaics with the Pentecost on the triumphal arch, thirteenth-century frescoes attributed to the school of Pietro Cavallini, the Byzantine icon of the Theotokos of the XII-XIII century, the bell tower of the XII-th century with five orders of triphores and the chapel of the Holy Founders, rebuilt in 1608 for Odoardo Farnese and frescoed by the Domenichino; the complex is closed by a belt of the fifteenth century.

Franciscan monastery of the fourteenth century, today of the Dominican nuns; according to tradition here Saint Francis found a source considered miraculous. There was the altarpiece with San Francesco di Margarito d'Arezzo, from the second half of the thirteenth century, today at the Museum of Medieval and Modern Art in Arezzo.
The oldest medieval quarter in the village.
A Romanesque church with frescoes from the 12th to the 15th century.

Recently restored, it preserves elements of the seventeenth century: baptistery, holy water and altar of St. Joseph with the altarpiece of the Death of St. Joseph. A plaque recalls the donation of the body of Valentine by Cardinal Orsini to the Castelli family.

Also called the Convent Museum, it is inside the sanctuary, in front of the cell of St. Humble; in the windows objects and sacred books, paintings and reliquaries. It was founded by the impulse of Father Modesto Calabretta and pilgrims who arrived at the birthplace of the saint.

Well temple of the final Bronze (XII century B.C.) in basalt cones, with fence to ... serratura..., staircase of 25 steps and chamber to tholos; around the hut of the meetings and, at 200 meters, the nuraghe Santa Cristina of the XV century B.C.

In the Palazzo dei Musei the archaeological, ethnological, art and musical collections of the city, from prehistory to twentieth century.

Small medieval village, first settlement from which the current Pineto was born, developed along a ridge around a main street with side alleys; on some facades of the streets and main squares murals with scenes of daily life.
Former road dug into the rock, with tunnels and parapets, today reserved for pedestrians and cyclists: connects the valley of Ledro with Pregasina and Riva del Garda.

The garden of the convent of San Francesco sul Colle, between the Calle Madonna della Snow and a stretch of the fourteenth-century walls: for over four centuries vineyard and vegetable garden of the friars, donated to the Municipality in 1986 and re-arranged by Italia Nostra since 1994 with vines, olive trees and fruit trees; from the vines you get a strawberry wine.

Dedicated to the patroness of the mule tracks, it rises on a hill at the south-eastern edge of the village; it could go back to the high Middle Ages, with modifications of the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries.

Outside the village, it was part of the convent built in 1583 by the Friars Minor of St. Francis: church with, on the long side, the friars' building and an internal cloister.

It rises in the open countryside about 9 km from Cerignola, on a spur overlooking the river Ofanto from which it derives its name (the high ripa) . The church of the patron saint holds for six months a year the Greek-Byzantine icon of Our Lady, probably of Basilian origin, found in 1172; in the area was found a stone with inscription to the goddess Bona. Diocesan shrine since 1992, has been several times among the Places of the FAI Heart.

About 60 hectares of forest between the village and the river Degano, with narrow streets, streams, horse riding for hippotherapy, pond for sport fishing and refreshment; from here start the paths towards Invillino and Enemonzo (Clap Foràt).

In the former convent of Minor Conventuals next to St. Francis (XIV century, rebuilt between 1683 and 1727 after the earthquake of 1654), built on the foundations of a Roman villa; established in 1979, opened in 2005 and completed in 2010, it develops on three floors from prehistory to the twentieth century. The materials of the sacred area underneath the Cathedral (the bronze thesaurus, headphone dedicated to Minerva, altar of Mars, architectural terracotta), statues of military tribes, medieval capitals, the copy of the diploma of 1292 of Charles II of Anjou and a section on the Duchy Boncompagni and the first paper mills. Open Monday and Wednesday-Friday 9-13, Saturday 9-13 and 16-20, Sunday 15-19; closed on Tuesday.
The peasant life of the Apennines in a farmhouse in the park.
The Romanesque cathedral of Bishop Vicinio, a pilgrim's destination, overlooking the square dedicated to the playwright.
Scarlino's treasure.
The only Roman bridge in Verona.
Consecrated in 1291 and rebuilt in the nave between 1707 and 1727; the Cappella Vitelli of the middle sixteenth century is by Giorgio Vasari and there is a copy of the Bride of the Virgin of Raphael.

The church is located on the site of a more ancient, of which remains a walled inscription at the entrance of the convent; the current building bears witness to the passage from the Byzantine to the Norman dominion. Inside stand out the apse, very well preserved, and the work of local chisels, with columns, pilasters and blind arches made from unique blocks.
The Bramantesque palace at the top of the village.
Museum circuit in the historic centre: works by local, national and international artists decorate doors, windows and walls of the village, with braille signs for blind visitors.

An interesting urban centre formed by the villages of San Bernardino and San Giovanni, on the two banks of the Nure, joined by a picturesque bridge; a lively village especially in summer, where you can taste the Bettolese village De.Co., a water pancake and flour served with cold cuts and cheeses.

Church mentioned already in 1070 among the possessions of Bonifacio di Canossa; it preserves late-Doroma traces along the sides, eighteenth-century furnishings in local tarsia and the canvas of the Madonna della Pace, of the school of Rodolfo del Ghirlandaio. Since 1446 the Six had the right to appoint their archpriests.
The place where the Biga was found.
Before the Greeks, in the center of Locri.
The view from the loggia.
The nineteenth-century clothes of ordinary people, reappeared from a crypt.

Designed by the Turin architect Vandone for the industrial Luigi Moretti (project 1897-1900) and built in 1904 as a neo-Gothic castle with towers and battlements, half-cost on the Coja hill, dominates the town. Magazine in 1919-1922 by the Trieste Ruggero and Arduino Berlam in a liberty key and modernized in 1952, was severely damaged by the earthquake of 1976 and then restored and returned to public use. The large park, born from an Italian garden, is today a public park.
Walk through alleys to the castle.
Parish church that preserves valuable reliquaries with a small cross and a Sacred Spina.

The southernmost Etruscans in Italy.

Founded in 1398 for the legacy of Sveva Orsini, widow of Francesco Del Balzo: sixteenth-century portal with the Madonna and Child in a shell, unique nave with four altars in polychrome marble of Neapolitan taste; in sacristy the mummified body of Duke Francesco II Del Balzo.
A sheltered and comfortable beach.
A small Colosseum in the Volturno valley.

130-metre cave in three rooms, shelter of the bandit Giovanni Corbeddu Salis and described by Grazia Deledda in "L'Edera" . In the second room were found among the oldest human remains of Sardinia, with a phalanx dated about 20,000 years ago, and fossils of the Prolagus sardus.

Romanesque building of the 12th century on the walls at the top of the old town, completely renovated in 1448; in the sacristy a majolica floor, in a seventeenth-century chapel by Julius Caesar Angels. Until 1986 it was a cathedral of the diocese of Nocera and Gualdo; according to the Commune it would rise on a temple dedicated to the goddess Favonia.
From the sea to the Sibillini in one glance.
Get off at 20 meters below the industrial city of war.
Promontory north of Portopaglietto, reachable by the road that runs along the pine forest, with abandoned military fortifications and excellent panoramic points for the sunset.

The remains of the 12th century castle stand on a rocky spur overlooking the road and the ford on the Magra; it was the seat of the Malaspina of Spino Secco, which in the division of assets of 1221 held Villafranca for its commercial and financial advantages. Next are the remains of the church of San Nicolò and the square dedicated to Dante, guest of the Malaspina; from the area of the castle the medieval road leads to the parish church of San Giovanni.
The square with the Governor's Palace and the statue of the painter, between the long Padan arcades and the Borgatti Theatre of the nineteenth century.

The square is dominated by the Gothic town hall in bricks crowned with Ghibelline blackbirds, whose central body dates back to 1265 and its wings probably to 1512; in front, the cockpit of the Pilacorte (1494), symbol of the city, with the two cranes faced sculpted by the Turchetto.

Opened from 2005 near Santa Maria Assunta, it is an antenna of the Ecomuseo della Dorsale Apenninea Umbra dedicated to the oral tradition of Valnerina: myths, legends, fairy tales and satires like the stories          .Vallinates, books, audio and video, the wardrobe of memory in wood and a copper sculpture-light by Franco Pappalardo, and the photographic exhibition ...Vallo dei Racconti. Contact: tel. 0743 616143.
The sulphur lake that the Romans believed was a gateway to the underworld.

Romanesque-Gothic facade in local red stone; inside a Renaissance crib in polychrome terracotta, a wooden Crucifix, paintings of the fourteenth and fifteenth centuries and in the crypt frescoes with Hell, Paradise, Madonna dell'Ulivo and biblical scenes. Church and cloister house the demo-anthropological museum.
The rural castle.

In the former cheese factory of the village, it tells about the production of cheese with the Friulian system through the original machinery, with a photographic exhibition on dairy farms and pastures, a section "In mont" on the alpine pastures and the nature of the Park, a space on the Colvera Valley and a multimedia post on the farmhouses of the Park.
A walk along the medieval defenses.
The Sicilian Gothic and the sculptures of Mazzullo.
On the trail of the father of Italian literary critics.

Monte San Michele (342 m), on the southern slopes of Monte Moscal, is the highest point of the municipality; with Monte Ceriel it offers some of the best views of Lake Garda.

Network of tunnels dug into the tuff, with tanks and cellars intact, which corresponds to the medieval walls and connects different parts of the country; it probably served military purposes, as a passage for defenders during the sieges, but another hypothesis is the water reserve.

On the plateau of Macereto, about 1000 meters below Mount Bove, it was built from 1528-29 by Giovan Battista from Lugano in Bramante's forms around a fourteenth-century chapel: octagonal plan covered with travertine, inside with Greek cross and works by Simone De Magistris (1580-82) in the apse. Next to the Palazzo delle Guaite (1571-83), which with the sanctuary is closed by a wall with a porch for pilgrims and animals.
A deep throat in Cellina's Forra.
The bronze doors of the matrix.
18th century plasters and ancient crucifix.
The white seatimes.
Rural villages on the hills of the Park.

At the foot of Mount Fenera, the main economic centre of Valsesia: the parish church of Saints Peter and Paul with works by Bernardino Lanino and Tanzio da Varallo, the Sacred Mount of Sant'Anna di Montrigone and the Carlo Conti Museum with prehistoric finds of the caves of Fenera; famous Carnival with the Mercu Scurot, born in 1854.
Hot bath in the sea in front of the Castle.
The apses on the harbor.

The parish church of the village took the place of the church of San Pietro, demolished in 1770; its bell tower, with that of the deconsecrated church of the Confraternity of San Michele, stands out on the roofs of the center.

Italian theatre built between 1862 and 1868 on a project by Antonio Tegani, modelled on the theatres of Reggio and Carpi; it replaced the court theatre decorated by Lelio Orsi. Room and reduced are decorated by Cesare Cervi; you enter from the inner courtyard of the Fortress. It is named after the tenor Franco Tagliavini from Novella.
Ancient frescoes in a small country church.
Built in 1532 as a residence of the governors and pontifical legates.
Romanesque Church on the Montorfano, in the early Christian and early medieval baptismal complex.

Municipality of the reclamation plain of the eastern Veneto; in the hamlet of Sant'Anna di Boccafossa two museums tell the territory: the Museum of peasant civilization, born from the community of reclamation, and the Museum of the landscape with Venetian painters of the twentieth century.
A free visit inside the castle walls.

Caneva is linked to ancient wines, in particular Marzemino, and to its numerous fig trees, with which is prepared the "Figo Moro" , suitable for sweet and savoury dishes; recommended tastings of wine and local products.
Along the route "Wine," Oil and Flavours Trail you can visit the wineries Marco Carpineti, Cincinnato and Pietrapinta; among the local specialties the pizzerias and Cori DOC wines.

On the hills between Lentini and Carlentini, inhabited by the Neolithic at the Iron Age, the Calcidesi founded in 729 BC. Leontinoi, one of the oldest Greek colonies in Sicily: allied with Athens in 433 BC, fortified by Dionysius in 405 BC, occupied by the Romans from 214 BC and then in decline. In the territory of Carlentini remains the monumental remains of the South Gate with the adjacent fortifications; the North Gate is being excavated with the University of Catania. Open Monday, Tuesday, Thursday and Friday 9-14, Wednesday 9-17.30, Saturday and first Sunday of the month 9-13.
A circular church erected on the nymph of the villa of Domitian, consecrated in 1060 and restored in 1938; it has a Byzantine icon and a 13th century fresco attributed to Cavallini.
The tower that dominates the village.
The Greek cross sanctuary with the marble crypt.

Calabrian art in a small town museum.

Romanesque Pisa church with Byzantine influences, built around 1100; inside a major altar in marble of the eighteenth century and three wooden altars of the seventeenth century. Patron Festival at the end of August.
A granite giant left by the glaciers.

Former convent with a museum in the press and a large collection of ancient books, considered one of the most important archives in Italy; the church, known for its paintings, has wooden ceilings painted by hand with Baroque religious images.

The sandy coast of Ascea, which from the Path of the Lovers can be seen to Capo Palinuro, has three rewarded stretches with the Blue Flag 2026: Torre del Telegrafo, Piana di Velia and Marina di Ascea. As part of the redevelopment of the Park Authority with the Municipality, 12 walkways have been built to access the beaches, which protect the dunal flora, along with a bike path and wooden platforms.
Trails and granite tanks above the city.
The fishing village and the Strada Regina.
The door of the Roman walls of the first century A.D., originally Porta Iovia, so called by the "bursarii" who collected duties; a plaque recalls the clash between Tebaldo and Romeo.

The most beautiful of the 38 Nuragic settlements in the territory, on a promontory on the Gulf of Cagliari above the beach of Capitana and Is Mortorius, guarding the Nuragic Harbour: central tower with false tholos dome, two minor towers connected and courtyard closed by a wall, with entrance to the Dolmenic system; dated to the middle of the II millennium BC, dug from the fifties, in the second world war the tower was reinforced as a viewing post.
Two thousand years of quarry.

Born as a kind chapel around 1500 on the remains of a church of the thirteenth century, a single nave with baroque stuccoes and oil paintings; in 1890 Giuseppe Barone designed its extension and the bell tower.

The coins and medals of Mantova and Gonzaga of the BAM Foundation; in the Palace of the Chamber of Commerce, made by the Andreani in 1914, the Art and Art Gallery.

Restored in the fifteenth century by the Dominicans, who officiated it from 1428 to 1920: fifteenth-century fresco of the Madonna enthroned with the Saints Domenico and Pietro martyr and the Madonna of the Rosary painted by Guercino in 1642, with the fifteen Mysteries in the ovals of the frame.

Built between the fifteenth and seventeenth centuries on the remains of the Norman castle: it includes the Tower of Charles V, the walls of the castle, a large panoramic square and an exhibition area on two floors; since 2017 the ancient secrets of the castle are open.

Museum of railway modeling on over 1,000 m2 and three floors, presented as the largest digital installation of miniature railways in Italy: over 20,000 pieces in scale 1:87, 40 trains in motion, 7,000 figurines and 400 m of tracks; on the top floor a plastic of 130 m2 reproduces South Tyrol in miniature and children can drive a train.
From the tower you can see the whole valley to the sea.

Small lake of glacial origin in the hamlet of Capo di Lago, between the hills of the Sorline and Rodino at the foot of Monte Pora; the steep walls of Lombardy reddish-brown wart darken the waters, surrounded by chestnut woods, swamp straw and florid fern. Since 2000 it has been protected as a Local Park of Sovercomunal Interest established with Angolo Terme; in summer it is frequented for bathing and boat trips, and is surrounded by hiking trails.
You walk under the chimney of the window.

In the former House of the Colletta, once the Cavalleggeri barracks: the archaeological section was born from excavations and researches since 1994 and documents the territory from the recent Neolithic to the Middle Ages, with the findings of the nuraghe Santa Itroxia, Bruncu Mogumu and Papalinu. The most important piece is a punic terracotta statue of the god Bes; a fragment of the early medieval epigraphic mentions Saint Saturnino. The art gallery exhibits paintings by artists from the south-eastern Campidano from the 16th century to the present day.

Church of the historic center consecrated in 1746, with classical facade and interior with three naves on pillars, without dome, a portal for nave. It preserves two great nineteenth-century paintings by the Neapolitan painter Alfonso Simonetti with the history of the saint. Without fixed hours: easier to find it open on Sunday morning.

Borgo Bandiera Arancione in the heart of the Madonie Park, with a 17th-century old town centre of alleys, stairs and fountains: the Mother Church with the Gothic-Catalan portal, the Gagini ancona alla SS. Trinità, the Civic Museum Collisani, the first Geological Route Urban of Europe, the hydroelectric power plant of 1908 and, at altitude, Piano Battaglia.

Established by the Municipality in 2014, the first literary park of the Ciociaria, winds through the alleys of the historic center with twelve panels in wood and aluminum on the places of the stories of Landolfi (the lunar stone and others); a second path, the "Paese del P." follow the mountain paths of the territory.

In the enclosure of the cemetery, at the east exit of the village: seat of the small medieval diocese (transferred to Nuoro in 1496), includes the Romanesque cathedral started around 1090 and remained unfinished, the sixteenth-century bell tower and the church of San Pietro with frescoes from the first thirteenth century of Umbrian-Latial painters on stories of the Old and New Testaments.

Medieval village of the Peligna Valley, \"inter aquasÂ" between the Contra and Sant'Antonio valleys, gathered around the 12th-XIII century dongion, with the 15th century Mother Church, the Trasmondi Palace and, at altitude, Mount Genzana.

The tower was born near a tunnel at the foot of the Dolomite rock above Musi (620 m), a village referred to as the Italian pole of rainfall.It takes off from Plan di Tapou in paragliding.

About fifteen old stables that housed herds during transhumance, under the Forata Crete and Mount Pleros; you can reach them with a short walk from Truia.

On the hill of the plateau of the Melle, between the rivers Tricuccio and Cumi, remain parts of the walls and doors, the castle called Aragonese, the cathedral, the cloister of the Minimi and some houses of the medieval city destroyed by the earthquake of 1783. Nearby, in Mella district, the excavations of a Hellenistic-Roman settlement with masonry, a cobbled road and houses with hardwood floors; the finds are in Reggio Calabria.

Ethnographic museum with over 700 objects and tools of the life of a mountain community, set up as thematic workshops: haymaking, milk processing, crafts of the blacksmith, carpenter and mason, and the rooms of the peasant house. A collection of 50 photographs documents the rural life of Andrate; in the park equipped with vintage agricultural means, a lever press and parts of the old forge of the country. Open on Sundays in summer-autumn, 10-12 and 15-18 (calendar 2025: from 6 July to 19 October).

Command building of the fortress built in 1854; on November 11, 1917, after Caporetto, King Vittorio Emanuele III brought together the Allied commanders asking not to withdraw. Today it houses the museum that recalls the encounter with documents, photographs and testimonies, and every year exhibitions of classical and contemporary art.

The hilly village of the Val di Magra, Orange Flag, with the towers of the Bishops-Conti Palace of Luni, the parish church with a canvas by Brueghel the Younger and the Regional Winery.
The ancient nucleus of the village: in the Lower Borgo there was a small square with the oratory of the Holy Family; in Piazza Mercato stood the Mint, when Masserano was a pontifical fief.

Municipality of the morainic hills to the north of Udine dominated by the castle of Colloredo Mels Waldsee, started in 1302, where Ippolito Nievo wrote the "Confessions of an Italian"; in September 2026 the Region returned the castle to the community with the reopening of the Ala Nievo. In the territory there are also the tower of the ancient castle of Mels and, in Entesano, the church of San Zenone with a cycle of seventeenth-century frescoes in the presbytery.
The semi-Otagonal palace with its shops and tourist office and the former Cistercian monastery.

At the base of the 17th-century civic tower, the former Museum of Embroidery is today a workshop-association that exhibits ancient and recent embroideries of the women of the country, a tradition documented since the fifteenth century.
